Definition: Possessive particle that shows ownership or describes a relationship between nouns, similar to 's or 'of' in English. Also used to mark adjectives modifying nouns.
Usage: Used in phrases like 我的书 (my book), 红的花 (red flowers), 中国的首都 (China's capital)

Definition: The number one; also used as an indefinite article similar to 'a/an' in English.
Usage: Common in counting and quantifying expressions like 一个人 (one person) or 一本书 (a book)

Definition: Aspect particle that indicates completion of an action or a change of state. Also used at the end of sentences to show that a new situation has occurred.
Usage: Placed after verbs (我吃了饭 - I ate) or at sentence end (下雨了 - It's raining now)

Definition: Third-person singular pronoun meaning 'he' or 'him', used to refer to a male person or sometimes gender-neutral.
Usage: Used in sentences like 他是老师 (he is a teacher)

Definition: Earth, ground, or land; refers to the surface we stand on or a piece of territory.
Usage: Common in words like 土地 (land), 地方 (place), 地球 (Earth)

Definition: Negative adverb meaning 'not' or 'no', used to negate verbs, adjectives, and certain other words.
Usage: Used in phrases like 不是 (is not), 不好 (not good), 不去 (not go). Note: changes to 'bú' (2nd tone) before 4th tone syllables.

Definition: Indicates location or ongoing action; means 'at', 'in', or 'on' when showing where something is, and forms the progressive tense (similar to '-ing') when placed before verbs.
Usage: Used in phrases like 我在家 (I'm at home) or 我在看书 (I am reading)

Definition: Aspect particle that indicates an ongoing state or continuous action, similar to '-ing' in English. Also shows that an action is in progress or a state is being maintained.
Usage: Attached directly after verbs, as in 坐着 (sitting), 穿着 (wearing), 开着 (open/turned on)

Definition: The verb 'to be' used to link a subject with a noun or noun phrase, indicating identity or classification.
Usage: Used in sentences like 我是学生 (I am a student) or 这是书 (This is a book)

Definition: The most common measure word (classifier) in Mandarin, used for counting general objects and people when no specific classifier applies.
Usage: Used in phrases like 一个人 (one person), 三个苹果 (three apples)

Definition: Benefit, profit, or advantage; also means sharp or favorable. Commonly used in business and economic contexts to refer to gains or interests.
Usage: Found in words like 利益 (benefit/interest), 胜利 (victory), and 利用 (to utilize)

Definition: The first-person singular pronoun meaning 'I' or 'me'. One of the most fundamental and frequently used words in Mandarin Chinese.
Usage: Used as the subject (我是学生 - I am a student) or object (他看见我 - He sees me) in sentences

Definition: An onomatopoeia representing laughter or a sound of exhaling; also used as a phonetic component in transliterations of foreign words
Usage: Common in expressions like 哈哈 (haha, laughter) and names like 哈尔滨 (Harbin)

Definition: To say, speak, or talk; to explain or tell something to someone.
Usage: Common in everyday conversation, as in 说话 (to speak) or 他说 (he says)

Definition: Plural suffix added to pronouns and nouns referring to people to indicate more than one person.
Usage: Used in words like 我们 (we/us), 你们 (you all), 孩子们 (children)

Definition: To have, to possess, or to exist. This is one of the most fundamental verbs in Mandarin, used to indicate possession or the existence of something.
Usage: Common in phrases like 我有书 (I have a book) or 有问题 (there is a problem)

Definition: Indicates upward direction, position above, or going onto/up something; also means 'previous' or 'last' when referring to time, and 'to go to' or 'to attend' as a verb.
Usage: Common in phrases like 上面 (above/on top), 上车 (get on a vehicle), 上课 (attend class), 上个月 (last month)

Definition: The second-person singular pronoun meaning 'you', used when addressing one person directly.
Usage: Used in greetings like 你好 (hello) and questions like 你叫什么名字? (What's your name?)

Definition: Inside, within, or in; indicates location or position inside something. Also used as a unit of distance (Chinese mile, approximately 0.5 km).
Usage: Common in phrases like 家里 (at home), 心里 (in one's heart), 这里 (here)

Definition: Demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this' or 'these', used to indicate something close to the speaker in space, time, or context.
Usage: Used in phrases like 这个 (this one), 这里 (here), 这是 (this is)

Definition: To come or arrive; to move toward the speaker or a reference point. Also used as a verb complement indicating direction toward the speaker.
Usage: Common in phrases like 来中国 (come to China), 过来 (come over), 起来 (get up/rise up)

Definition: Demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' or 'those', used to refer to something distant from the speaker. Can also function as 'in that case' or 'then' when used as a conjunction.
Usage: Common in phrases like 那个 (that one), 那里 (there), 那么 (then/in that case)

Definition: Person or people; human being. One of the most fundamental Chinese characters referring to individuals or humanity in general.
Usage: Used in countless compounds like 中国人 (Chinese person), 人们 (people), 好人 (good person)

Definition: To arrive at or reach a destination; also used as a resultative complement meaning 'successfully completed' or 'up until (a time)'.
Usage: Common in phrases like 到了 (arrived), 看到 (saw/catch sight of), 从...到... (from...to...)

Definition: A suffix particle used at the end of questions and certain words to soften tone or indicate uncertainty. Most commonly seen in question words like 什么 (shénme, what) and 怎么 (zěnme, how).
Usage: Rarely used alone; typically appears as part of compound question words

Definition: A grammatical particle used to move the object before the verb, emphasizing that an action is done to something specific. Also used as a measure word for objects with handles or things that can be grasped.
Usage: Common in sentences like 把门关上 (close the door) or 一把椅子 (a chair)

Definition: To look at, to see, or to watch; also means to read or to visit someone.
Usage: Common in phrases like 看书 (read a book), 看电视 (watch TV), 看医生 (see a doctor)

Definition: To get, obtain, or acquire something; to gain or receive.
Usage: Common in phrases like 得到 (to obtain) and 获得 (to gain). Also means 'must' when followed by a verb.

Definition: Negation word meaning 'not have' or 'did not'; used to negate past actions or indicate absence/lack of something.
Usage: Common in phrases like 没有 (don't have/didn't), 没关系 (it doesn't matter), and 我没去 (I didn't go)

Definition: A conjunction meaning 'and' that connects nouns, pronouns, or noun phrases together.
Usage: Used in phrases like 你和我 (you and me), 苹果和橙子 (apples and oranges)

Definition: Big, large, or great in size, scale, or importance. One of the most fundamental adjectives in Mandarin for describing physical size or significance.
Usage: Used in common words like 大学 (university), 大家 (everyone), and 大小 (size)

Definition: An adverb expressing 'then', 'right away', 'just', or 'only' to emphasize immediacy, limitation, or consequence. Also used to indicate something happening earlier than expected or as soon as a condition is met.
Usage: Common in patterns like 就是 (exactly/precisely), 我就来 (I'm coming right away), or 一...就... (as soon as...then...)

Definition: Sound, voice, or noise. Also used as a measure word for sounds or utterances.
Usage: Common in words like 声音 (sound), 大声 (loud voice), and phrases like 一声 (one sound/utterance)

Definition: Way, path, or road; also means to say or speak. In philosophy, refers to 'the Way' or fundamental principle (as in Daoism).
Usage: Common as a measure word for questions, orders, or dishes (一道菜 - one dish), and in words like 知道 (to know) and 道路 (road)

Definition: Adverb meaning 'all' or 'both' that indicates inclusiveness of everything or everyone mentioned. Also used to mean 'already' or 'even' in certain contexts.
Usage: Placed before verbs, as in 我们都是学生 (we are all students) or 都十点了 (it's already 10 o'clock)

Definition: Particle indicating past experience or completed action, meaning 'have ever done' or 'have been to'. Also used as a verb meaning 'to pass' or 'to cross'.
Usage: As particle: 我去过中国 (I have been to China). As verb: 过马路 (cross the street)

Definition: Auxiliary verb meaning 'can' or 'to know how to' (indicating learned ability); also means 'will' (indicating future possibility) or 'meeting/gathering' as a noun.
Usage: Used before verbs like 我会说中文 (I can speak Chinese) or 明天会下雨 (It will rain tomorrow)

Definition: Head (the body part); also used as a suffix for nouns and as a measure word for certain animals
Usage: Common in words like 石头 (stone), 木头 (wood), and counting livestock like 一头牛 (one cow)

Definition: To go out, exit, or come out from inside to outside; also means to produce or appear.
Usage: Common in words like 出去 (go out), 出来 (come out), 出门 (leave home/go out)

Definition: Many, much, or a lot; indicates a large quantity or number of something. Also used in questions to ask 'how much/many' or 'how' (as in 'how old').
Usage: Common in phrases like 很多 (very many), 多少 (how much/many), 多大 (how old)

Definition: Demon, devil, or magic; refers to supernatural evil forces or magical powers. Often used in compound words related to fantasy, supernatural beings, or obsessive behavior.
Usage: Common in words like 魔鬼 (devil), 魔法 (magic), 恶魔 (demon), and 着魔 (bewitched/obsessed)

Definition: To want or to need; also used as an auxiliary verb to express future intention or necessity (will/going to/must).
Usage: Common in expressions like 我要水 (I want water) or 我要去 (I'm going to go)

Definition: To go; to leave for a place or move away from the current location.
Usage: Common in phrases like 去学校 (go to school) or 我去 (I'm going). Often paired with destination words.

Definition: A noun suffix that forms nouns from other words, often indicating small objects or familiar things; also means 'child' or 'son' in classical Chinese.
Usage: Commonly attached to words like 桌子 (table), 椅子 (chair), 孩子 (child), 儿子 (son)

Definition: A question word meaning 'what' that appears in the common compound 什么 (shénme). Rarely used alone in modern Mandarin.
Usage: Almost always appears in the word 什么 (what), as in 你要什么? (What do you want?)

Definition: To think, to want, or to miss someone/something. This versatile verb expresses thoughts, desires, and feelings of longing.
Usage: Common in phrases like 我想你 (I miss you), 想吃 (want to eat), 我想... (I think...)

Definition: Adverb meaning 'also', 'too', or 'as well', used to indicate that something applies in addition to what was previously mentioned.
Usage: Typically placed before the verb or adjective, as in 我也是 (I am too) or 他也去 (he's also going)

Definition: Means 'down', 'below', or 'under' as a position word; also used as a verb meaning 'to go down', 'to get off', or 'next' (as in next time).
Usage: Common in directional phrases like 下去 (go down), 下车 (get off a vehicle), 下面 (below/underneath), and time expressions like 下次 (next time)

Definition: To see, to meet, or to perceive. Also used to indicate passive voice or the result of an action being experienced.
Usage: Common in words like 看见 (to see), 见面 (to meet), and 再见 (goodbye, literally 'see you again')

Definition: Can, able to, or be capable of doing something. Expresses ability or possibility.
Usage: Used before verbs like 我能说中文 (I can speak Chinese)

Definition: A measure word (classifier) used for counting animals, birds, and certain objects like boats or hands. Also means 'only' or 'just' (though that usage has a different pronunciation: zhi3).
Usage: Common in phrases like 一只猫 (one cat), 两只鸟 (two birds), or 只有 (only have)

Definition: Small, little, or young; describes size, age, or importance that is less than average or expected.
Usage: Common in words like 小孩 (child), 小狗 (puppy), and as a prefix for names to show affection

Definition: A preposition meaning 'from' that indicates a starting point in time, place, or direction. Also means 'to follow' or 'since' depending on context.
Usage: Common in phrases like 从...到... (from...to...), 从今天开始 (starting from today), 从中国来 (come from China)

Definition: To rise, get up, or start; indicates the beginning of an action or upward movement.
Usage: Common in phrases like 起来 (qǐlái - to get up/rise) and 起床 (qǐchuáng - to get out of bed)

Definition: To give birth, to be born, or to grow; also means raw or uncooked, and living or alive.
Usage: Common in words like 学生 (student, literally 'studying person'), 生日 (birthday), and 生病 (to get sick)

Definition: Can, may, or able to; expresses permission or possibility. Also used to mean 'but' or as an intensifier in certain contexts.
Usage: Common in phrases like 可以 (kěyǐ - can/may), 可是 (kěshì - but), and 可爱 (kě'ài - cute)

Definition: Good, well, or fine; expresses positive quality or approval. Also used to indicate completion or readiness.
Usage: Common in greetings like 你好 (hello), responses like 好的 (okay), and descriptions like 很好 (very good)

Definition: Pattern, standard, or style; also means grid or frame. Commonly used as a suffix in compound words to indicate format, character, or qualification.
Usage: Found in words like 性格 (personality), 风格 (style), 格子 (grid/checkered pattern), and 合格 (qualified)

Definition: An adverb meaning 'very' or 'quite' that intensifies adjectives and some verbs. In simple statements with adjectives, it's often used even when no strong emphasis is intended.
Usage: Essential in basic sentences like 我很好 (I'm fine/well) and 很大 (very big)

Definition: Correct, right; also means 'to' or 'toward' when indicating direction or target of an action or attitude
Usage: Used as an adjective (对/不对 right/wrong), preposition (对我说 say to me), or to express agreement

Definition: To walk or to go; to leave or depart from a place.
Usage: Common in everyday expressions like 走路 (to walk), 我走了 (I'm leaving)

Definition: To do, to act, or to be; commonly used to mean 'for' or 'for the sake of' when indicating purpose or beneficiary.
Usage: Often seen in phrases like 为了 (wei4le, in order to) and 因为 (yin1wei4, because)

Definition: The third-person singular feminine pronoun meaning 'she' or 'her' in English.
Usage: Used to refer to female people, as in 她是老师 (she is a teacher)

Definition: To know, to be aware of, or to understand something. This is one of the most common verbs for expressing knowledge or awareness.
Usage: Found in common words like 知道 (zhīdào - to know), 通知 (tōngzhī - to notify), and 知识 (zhīshi - knowledge)

Definition: A common Chinese surname (romanized as Luo or Law); also means to spread out, arrange in order, or catch with a net.
Usage: Most frequently encountered as a family name, as in 罗马 (Luómǎ, Rome) or in compound words

Definition: Eye; the organ of sight. Also used as a measure word for wells, springs, or glances.
Usage: Common in words like 眼睛 (yǎnjing - eyes), 眼光 (yǎnguāng - vision/perspective)

Definition: Grace, favor, or kindness received from someone; benevolence or a good deed done for another person.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 恩人 (benefactor) and 感恩 (to be grateful)

Definition: Time or a specific point in time; also used as a measure word for hours.
Usage: Common in expressions like 小时 (hour), 时间 (time), and 当时 (at that time)

Definition: Means 'again' or 'also/both' to indicate repetition or addition. Often used to express that something happens once more or to connect two qualities or actions.
Usage: Common in patterns like 又...又... (both...and...) as in 又高又帅 (both tall and handsome), or to mean 'again' as in 他又来了 (he came again)

Definition: Adverb meaning 'still' or 'yet' to indicate a continuing state or action. Also means 'in addition' or 'also' when expressing something additional.
Usage: Common in phrases like 还有 (also have/there's more), 还是 (still/or), and 还在 (still at/doing)

Definition: To open, turn on, or start something. Also means to drive (a vehicle) or to hold (a meeting).
Usage: Common in phrases like 开门 (open the door), 开车 (drive a car), 开会 (hold a meeting), 开灯 (turn on the light)

Definition: Sky or heaven; also means 'day' as a unit of time.
Usage: Common in words like 今天 (today), 明天 (tomorrow), and 天气 (weather)

Definition: To study or learn; to imitate or follow. Also refers to a field of study or school (as in 学校).
Usage: Common in words like 学习 (to study), 学生 (student), 大学 (university)

Definition: Self or oneself; also means 'from' when indicating a starting point in time or place.
Usage: Common in words like 自己 (oneself), 自然 (nature/natural), and 来自 (to come from)

Definition: Law, method, or way of doing something. Also commonly used as an abbreviation for France (法国) or Buddhism (佛法).
Usage: Found in words like 方法 (method), 法律 (law), 办法 (solution/way), and 语法 (grammar)

Definition: Air, gas, or breath; also refers to anger or vital energy. Can mean weather or smell depending on context.
Usage: Common in words like 天气 (weather), 生气 (to be angry), 空气 (air)

Definition: A suffix or particle meaning 'so' or 'like that', often used to form adverbs or indicate a state of being. Commonly appears in compound words to express manner or condition.
Usage: Found in words like 当然 (of course), 自然 (natural), 突然 (suddenly), and 虽然 (although)

Definition: To use or to employ something; can also mean 'with' when indicating the instrument or means of doing something.
Usage: Common in phrases like 用筷子 (use chopsticks) or 不用 (no need to)

Definition: After, behind, or later in time or position; also means back or rear.
Usage: Common in words like 后面 (behind), 以后 (after/later), 然后 (then/afterwards)

Definition: A preposition meaning 'with', 'by means of', or 'in order to', used to indicate method, purpose, or reason. Also functions as a verb meaning 'to use' or 'to take' in classical Chinese.
Usage: Common in phrases like 可以 (can/may), 所以 (therefore), and 以后 (after/later)

Definition: Body or physical form; also refers to oneself or one's life/status.
Usage: Common in words like 身体 (body/health), 自身 (oneself), and 身份 (identity/status)

Definition: Means 'illustrious', 'grand', or 'impressive'; describes something or someone famous, prominent, or awe-inspiring.
Usage: Commonly seen in names and formal expressions like 赫赫有名 (hèhè yǒumíng, very famous) or 显赫 (xiǎnhè, illustrious)

Definition: To look into the distance, to gaze at, or to hope for something. Also means to expect or wish for a future outcome.
Usage: Common in words like 希望 (hope), 愿望 (wish), and 看望 (to visit someone)

Definition: To send, emit, or issue; to develop or happen. Also means hair when pronounced fà (4th tone).
Usage: Common in words like 发现 (discover), 发生 (happen), 发送 (send)

Definition: Face or surface; also commonly means noodles in everyday usage. Can refer to the front side of something or an aspect/dimension of a situation.
Usage: Used in words like 面条 (noodles), 表面 (surface), 见面 (meet face-to-face), and 方面 (aspect)

Definition: Hand; the body part at the end of the arm used for grasping and holding things.
Usage: Common in everyday expressions like 洗手 (wash hands), 右手 (right hand), and 手机 (mobile phone, literally 'hand machine')

Definition: Means 'kind', 'type', 'manner', or 'appearance'; used to describe how something looks or what kind of thing it is.
Usage: Common in phrases like 这样 (this way/like this), 那样 (that way/like that), 怎么样 (how is it?), and 一样 (the same)

Definition: A literary particle meaning 'this' or 'thus'; primarily used in formal or classical Chinese contexts and as a phonetic component in transliterating foreign names and words.
Usage: Commonly seen in transliterations like 斯坦福 (Stanford), 莫斯科 (Moscow), and formal expressions

Definition: Oneself; self. A pronoun referring to one's own person, often used in formal or literary contexts.
Usage: Common in words like 自己 (zìjǐ - oneself) and 知己 (zhījǐ - close friend, literally 'one who knows oneself')

Definition: Quick, agile, or sensitive in response or perception. Describes someone who is sharp, alert, or fast in thinking and reacting.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 敏感 (sensitive), 敏捷 (agile), and 灵敏 (keen/sharp)

Definition: To resemble or be like; to look like or seem. Also used as a noun meaning 'image' or 'portrait'.
Usage: Common in comparisons like 他像他爸爸 (he looks like his father) or 看起来像 (it seems like)

Definition: Third-person pronoun meaning 'it', used to refer to animals, objects, and abstract concepts (not people).
Usage: Used for non-human subjects, like 它是一只猫 (it is a cat) or 它很重要 (it is important)

Definition: Superlative marker meaning 'most' or '-est', used before adjectives or verbs to indicate the highest degree
Usage: Used in phrases like 最好 (best), 最大 (biggest), 最喜欢 (like the most)

Definition: Matter, affair, thing, or event; refers to situations, activities, or tasks that need attention or have occurred.
Usage: Common in phrases like 没事 (it's nothing/no problem), 有事 (have something to do), and 事情 (matter/affair)

Definition: Meaning, idea, thought, or intention; refers to what someone thinks or intends to express or do.
Usage: Commonly appears in words like 意思 (meaning), 注意 (pay attention), 同意 (agree), and 意见 (opinion)

Definition: To teach or instruct someone; to show or tell someone how to do something.
Usage: Common in words like 教师 (teacher), 教室 (classroom), and phrases like 教我中文 (teach me Chinese)

Definition: Strange, unusual, or odd; also means wonderful or surprising in a positive sense.
Usage: Common in words like 奇怪 (strange), 好奇 (curious), and 神奇 (magical/miraculous)

Definition: Face; the front part of the head from forehead to chin. Also used figuratively to refer to dignity, reputation, or self-respect.
Usage: Common in expressions like 洗脸 (wash face), 脸红 (blush/face turns red), and 丢脸 (lose face)

Definition: Child or son; also used as a diminutive suffix (儿化音) added to the end of words in northern Chinese dialects, especially in Beijing Mandarin.
Usage: As a standalone word means 'child/son' (儿子); as a suffix it softens words and is common in everyday speech (e.g., 玩儿 wánr 'to play', 花儿 huār 'flower')

Definition: A unit of weight measurement equal to one gram; also means to overcome or conquer.
Usage: Common in measurements like 公克 (gram) and compound words like 克服 (to overcome)

Definition: To listen or to hear; the primary verb for perceiving sound with your ears.
Usage: Common in phrases like 听音乐 (listen to music) and 听说 (hear that/it is said)

Definition: Cloth or fabric; can also mean to announce, spread, or arrange something.
Usage: Common in words like 布料 (fabric), 发布 (to release/announce), and 分布 (to distribute)

Definition: Front, forward, or before in space or time; the opposite of 后 (back/after).
Usage: Used in words like 前面 (in front), 以前 (before/previously), 前天 (day before yesterday)

Definition: Passive voice marker that indicates the subject receives an action, similar to 'by' in English passive constructions. Often implies an undesirable or negative outcome.
Usage: Used in patterns like 被...了 (was/were...), as in 我被骗了 (I was cheated)

Definition: Words, speech, or something that is said; can also mean language or dialect. Often used to refer to spoken statements, conversations, or what someone says.
Usage: Common in phrases like 说话 (to speak), 电话 (telephone), 中国话 (Chinese language)

Definition: Means 'present', 'current', or 'now'; also means 'to appear' or 'to show'. Most commonly used to indicate the present time or current state of something.
Usage: Frequently seen in words like 现在 (xiànzài - now), 现代 (xiàndài - modern), and 出现 (chūxiàn - to appear)

Definition: A measure word for rooms or small buildings; also means 'between' or 'among' (when pronounced jiàn).
Usage: Used in phrases like 房间 (room), 卫生间 (bathroom), or 时间 (time)

Definition: Sound, tone, or voice. Refers to any audible noise or musical note.
Usage: Common in words like 声音 (sound/voice), 音乐 (music), and 发音 (pronunciation)

Definition: Home, house, or family. Also used as a suffix to indicate a specialist or expert in a field.
Usage: Common in words like 家人 (family members), 回家 (go home), 作家 (writer), 科学家 (scientist)

Definition: The number two, specifically used when counting with measure words (classifiers). It means 'two of something' or 'both' when referring to a pair.
Usage: Used in phrases like 两个人 (two people), 两天 (two days). Note: 二 (èr) is used for counting or in numbers, while 两 is used before measure words.

Definition: Question word meaning 'how many' or 'how much', used to ask about quantity (typically for numbers under 10). Also means 'several' or 'a few' in statements.
Usage: Common in questions like 几个 (how many) or 几点 (what time)

Definition: Question word meaning 'how' or 'why', used to ask about the manner, method, or reason for something.
Usage: Most commonly appears in 怎么 (zěnme, how/why) and 怎样 (zěnyàng, how/in what way)

Definition: Side, edge, or border of something; also used to mean 'while' when repeated (边...边...) to indicate doing two actions simultaneously.
Usage: Common in words like 旁边 (beside), 这边 (this side), and patterns like 边吃边看 (eating while watching)

Definition: To give; also used as a preposition meaning 'to' or 'for' to indicate the recipient of an action.
Usage: Common in phrases like 给你 (give you) or 我给他打电话 (I call him/make a call to him)

Definition: To laugh or smile; to express amusement, happiness, or joy through facial expressions or sounds.
Usage: Common in everyday expressions like 笑一笑 (smile a bit) or 大笑 (laugh loudly)

Definition: To do or to make; a general action verb used for performing activities, creating things, or working as something.
Usage: Common in phrases like 做饭 (to cook), 做作业 (to do homework), 做医生 (to work as a doctor)

Definition: A preposition meaning 'with' or 'and', used to indicate accompaniment or connection between people or things. Also means 'to follow' when used as a verb.
Usage: Common in phrases like 我跟你 (I and you / with you) or 跟着 (to follow along)

Definition: Mouth; also used as a measure word for people in a family or things with openings.
Usage: Common in words like 人口 (population), 门口 (doorway), and counting family members like 三口人 (family of three)

Definition: A preposition used to make comparisons between two things, meaning 'compared to' or 'than'. It introduces the standard of comparison in comparative sentences.
Usage: Used in the pattern A + 比 + B + adjective, like 我比他高 (I am taller than him)

Definition: A measure word used for flat objects like paper, tables, beds, and faces; also a common Chinese surname.
Usage: Used in phrases like 一张纸 (a sheet of paper), 一张桌子 (a table), 张先生 (Mr. Zhang)

Definition: To grow or to increase in size, age, or development; can also mean an elder or leader.
Usage: Common in words like 长大 (to grow up), 成长 (to mature), 校长 (school principal)

Definition: To live or reside in a place; also used as a verb complement meaning 'firmly' or 'to a halt' to indicate stopping or holding steady.
Usage: Common in 住在 (to live in), 站住 (stop/halt), 记住 (to remember firmly)

Definition: To return or go back to a place; to reply or answer. Also used as a measure word for counting occurrences or times of actions.
Usage: Common in phrases like 回家 (go home), 回答 (answer), and 一回 (one time)

Definition: Fast or quick; also means 'soon' or 'almost' when referring to time.
Usage: Used as an adjective (快车 fast train) or adverb (快来 come quickly, 快要下雨了 it's about to rain)

Definition: Eyeball or pupil of the eye. This character is rarely used alone and almost always appears in the compound word 眼睛 (yǎnjing), meaning 'eye'.
Usage: Most commonly seen in 眼睛 (eye), as in 她的眼睛很大 (her eyes are big)

Definition: Door or gate; an entrance or opening that can be opened and closed. Also used to refer to a field of study or category (like 'department').
Usage: Common in words like 开门 (open the door), 大门 (main gate), 专门 (specialized)

Definition: To move or to act; indicates physical movement or taking action.
Usage: Common in words like 运动 (yùndòng - sports/exercise), 动作 (dòngzuò - movement/action), and 感动 (gǎndòng - to move emotionally)

Definition: A point, dot, or spot; also used as a measure word for time (o'clock) and to mean 'a little bit'
Usage: Common in expressions like 三点 (3 o'clock), 一点 (a little), and 点菜 (order food)

Definition: To tell, inform, or notify someone about something; also means to accuse or report (to authorities).
Usage: Common in words like 告诉 (gàosu - to tell), 报告 (bàogào - report), and 广告 (guǎnggào - advertisement)

Definition: The number three. It is one of the most basic and frequently used numbers in Mandarin Chinese.
Usage: Used in counting, dates, times, and quantities like 三个人 (three people) or 星期三 (Wednesday)

Definition: Virtue, morality, or moral character; also refers to kindness and good conduct. Commonly used in formal contexts and appears in many compound words related to ethics and behavior.
Usage: Found in words like 道德 (morality), 品德 (moral character), and country names like 德国 (Germany)

Definition: Room or chamber; a formal term for an enclosed space within a building.
Usage: Commonly used in compound words like 教室 (classroom), 办公室 (office), 卧室 (bedroom)

Definition: A type of wild vegetable or herb; commonly used as a phonetic component in transliterations of foreign names and places.
Usage: Most frequently seen in words like 莱茵河 (Rhine River) and 蓬莱 (Penglai, a mythical place)

Definition: West; the direction where the sun sets. Also used to refer to Western countries or things from the West.
Usage: Common in directional words like 西边 (west side), 东西 (east-west/things), and 西方 (the West/Western countries)

Definition: To stand (in an upright position); a station or stop (for buses, trains, etc.)
Usage: As a verb: 站起来 (stand up). As a noun: 车站 (bus/train station), 地铁站 (subway station)

Definition: Letter (mail); to trust or believe. As a noun, it refers to written correspondence, and as a verb, it means to have faith or confidence in something or someone.
Usage: Common in words like 信件 (letter/mail), 相信 (to believe), and 自信 (confidence)

Definition: Prefix used before numbers to form ordinal numbers, similar to '-th' in English (first, second, third, etc.)
Usage: Used in phrases like 第一 (first), 第二 (second), 第三 (third)

Definition: To tell, inform, or complain about something; to accuse or bring a lawsuit against someone.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 告诉 (gàosu - to tell), 诉说 (sùshuō - to recount), and 起诉 (qǐsù - to sue)

Definition: Middle or center; also means 'in' or 'among' when indicating location or state. One of the most fundamental characters in Chinese, appearing in words like China (中国, literally 'Middle Kingdom').
Usage: Used in 中国 (China), 中间 (middle), 中文 (Chinese language), 其中 (among them)

Definition: A measure word meaning 'some' or 'a few', used to indicate an indefinite small quantity of something.
Usage: Commonly appears after 这 (zhè) or 那 (nà) as in 这些 (these) and 那些 (those), or after verbs to mean 'a little bit'

Definition: Too, excessively, or overly; used to indicate that something exceeds a normal or acceptable degree.
Usage: Commonly placed before adjectives or verbs, as in 太好了 (too good/great!) or 太贵 (too expensive)

Definition: Year; a period of 12 months or 365 days. Also refers to age or a specific year in time.
Usage: Common in expressions like 今年 (this year), 去年 (last year), 明年 (next year), and 三年 (three years)

Definition: Special, particular, or exceptional; indicates something that stands out from the ordinary or has distinctive characteristics.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 特别 (especially/special) and 特点 (characteristic/feature)

Definition: The color black; dark or without light.
Usage: Used to describe colors (黑色 - black color), darkness (天黑了 - it's getting dark), or as part of compound words

Definition: Real, true, or genuine; also used as an adverb meaning 'really' or 'truly' to emphasize a statement.
Usage: Common in expressions like 真好 (really good) or 真的 (really/truly)

Definition: A common Chinese surname, most famously associated with Deng Xiaoping, the former leader of China.
Usage: Primarily used as a family name in names like 邓小平 (Deng Xiaoping)

Definition: A class, lesson, or course of study. Also used as a measure word for counting lessons or class periods.
Usage: Common in school contexts like 上课 (attend class), 汉语课 (Chinese class), or 第一课 (Lesson 1)

Definition: To hit, strike, or beat; also a versatile verb used in many common expressions meaning 'to do' or 'to make' (like打电话 make a phone call, 打球 play ball).
Usage: Extremely common in daily expressions and verb-object compounds

Definition: To give, grant, or confer something (such as knowledge, authority, or a title) to someone; to teach or instruct.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 教授 (professor), 授课 (to teach a class), and 授权 (to authorize)

Definition: To ask or inquire; to pose a question to someone.
Usage: Common in phrases like 问题 (question/problem) and 请问 (excuse me, may I ask)

Definition: Means 'correct', 'straight', or 'exactly/just' (in the process of doing something). Also indicates something is upright, proper, or precisely at a certain time or state.
Usage: Common in phrases like 正在 (zhengzai, in the process of), 正好 (zhenghao, just right), and 正确 (zhengque, correct)

Definition: To let, allow, or permit someone to do something; also means to yield or give way to someone.
Usage: Commonly used in causative constructions like 让我看看 (let me see) or to express yielding as in 让座 (give up one's seat)

Definition: Sea or ocean; a large body of salt water. Can also refer to something vast or numerous, like a sea of people.
Usage: Common in words like 上海 (Shanghai), 海洋 (ocean), 大海 (the sea)

Definition: To eat or consume food. Can also mean to have a meal or to live off something.
Usage: Used in everyday contexts like 吃饭 (eat rice/have a meal), 吃早饭 (eat breakfast)

Definition: Heart, both as the physical organ and as the center of emotions, thoughts, and intentions. Also means mind, feeling, or core/center of something.
Usage: Common in words like 小心 (be careful), 心情 (mood), 关心 (care about), and 中心 (center)

Definition: A walking stick, cane, or staff used for support while walking or as a symbol of authority.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 拐杖 (crutch/walking stick) and 手杖 (cane)

Definition: A measure word for types, kinds, or varieties of things; also means 'kind' or 'type' as a noun.
Usage: Used in phrases like 这种 (this kind), 各种 (various kinds), 一种方法 (one type of method)

Definition: To pass through, to experience, or to undergo something. Also used as a component in words related to classics, scriptures, or regular/constant things.
Usage: Common in words like 经过 (to pass through), 经验 (experience), 已经 (already), and 经常 (often)

Definition: Color or hue; can also refer to appearance, look, or expression on someone's face.
Usage: Common in words like 颜色 (color), 红色 (red), 脸色 (facial expression/complexion)

Definition: Star, referring to celestial bodies in the sky or used in compound words related to stars and planets.
Usage: Common in words like 星期 (week), 明星 (celebrity/star), 火星 (Mars), and 星星 (stars)

Definition: Horse; a common domesticated animal used for riding and transportation.
Usage: Used in compound words like 马上 (immediately, literally 'on horseback') and as a surname

Definition: Adverb indicating that something happened later than expected or only just now; also means 'only' to emphasize a small amount or degree.
Usage: Common in phrases like 我才到 (I just arrived) or 才三岁 (only three years old)

Definition: To feel or sense something; to become aware of a sensation or perception. Also means sleep when pronounced 'jiao4'.
Usage: Common in words like 感觉 (gǎnjué - feeling), 觉得 (juéde - to think/feel), and 睡觉 (shuìjiào - to sleep)

Definition: First, before, or earlier in time or sequence; indicates doing something ahead of other actions or people.
Usage: Commonly used in phrases like 先生 (Mr./teacher) and 先...再... (first...then...)

Definition: Light or brightness; can also mean smooth, bare, or used up/empty when describing surfaces or quantities.
Usage: Common in words like 阳光 (sunlight), 光滑 (smooth), and 光盘 (empty plate/CD)

Definition: Even more; still more. Used to indicate a higher degree or level when comparing things.
Usage: Commonly used in comparisons like 更好 (even better), 更快 (even faster)

Definition: To enter, go into, or move forward into a space or location. Also means to advance or make progress.
Usage: Common in words like 进来 (come in), 进去 (go in), and 进步 (progress)

Definition: Again, once more; indicates repetition of an action or additional occurrence. Also means 'then' or 'only then' when referring to future actions in sequence.
Usage: Used before verbs like 再见 (goodbye, literally 'see again') or 再说 (talk about it later)

Definition: School; an educational institution where students learn. Also used as a short form for various types of schools and military ranks.
Usage: Most commonly seen in words like 学校 (xuéxiào - school), 校长 (xiàozhǎng - principal), and 校园 (xiàoyuán - campus)

Definition: Teacher, master, or expert in a particular field; also refers to a skilled professional or mentor.
Usage: Common in words like 老师 (teacher), 师傅 (master/skilled worker), and 医师 (doctor)

Definition: Tall or high; describes physical height of objects, people, or elevation. Can also mean advanced level or superior quality.
Usage: Common in phrases like 很高 (very tall), 高兴 (happy), 高中 (high school)

Definition: Often, frequently, or regularly; also means ordinary or normal. Used to describe actions that happen repeatedly or states that are usual.
Usage: Common in words like 经常 (jīngcháng - often), 常常 (chángcháng - frequently), and 正常 (zhèngcháng - normal)

Definition: Strange, odd, or weird; can also mean to blame someone or a monster/supernatural creature when used as a noun.
Usage: Common in expressions like 奇怪 (strange), 怪不得 (no wonder), or 怪物 (monster)

Definition: A measure word for counting the number of times an action occurs or events happen.
Usage: Used in phrases like 一次 (one time), 两次 (twice), 下次 (next time)

Definition: Indicates completion or that something has already happened or been done, meaning 'already' or 'to have finished'.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 已经 (already) and at the end of sentences to mark completion

Definition: A measure word (classifier) used for long, narrow, flexible objects like rivers, roads, fish, pants, or items that can be listed (like rules or messages). Also means 'strip' or 'item' as a noun.
Usage: Common in phrases like 一条河 (a river), 一条鱼 (a fish), 一条裤子 (a pair of pants), 三条规则 (three rules)

Definition: Tight, tense, or close-fitting; also means urgent or pressing when describing situations or time.
Usage: Common in phrases like 紧张 (nervous/tense), 要紧 (important/urgent), and 时间很紧 (time is tight)

Definition: Classical Chinese particle used to indicate a question, exclamation, or to mark the end of a statement. In modern Chinese, it appears mainly in literary expressions and set phrases.
Usage: Common in phrases like 似乎 (it seems), 几乎 (almost), and classical-style questions

Definition: Emotion, feeling, or sentiment; also refers to affection, love, or human relationships. Commonly appears in compound words related to emotional states and interpersonal connections.
Usage: Found in words like 感情 (feelings), 爱情 (romantic love), 心情 (mood), 友情 (friendship)

Definition: To fly or move through the air; describes the action of birds, planes, or objects moving swiftly through space.
Usage: Common in words like 飞机 (airplane), 飞鸟 (flying bird), and 飞快 (extremely fast)

Definition: To feel or sense; a feeling or sensation. Often used in compound words related to emotions and perceptions.
Usage: Common in words like 感觉 (gǎnjué - to feel), 感谢 (gǎnxiè - to thank), 感动 (gǎndòng - to be moved/touched)

Definition: Straight, direct, or upright; describes something without curves or bends, or behavior that is honest and straightforward.
Usage: Common in words like 一直 (always, continuously), 直接 (direct), and 笔直 (perfectly straight)

Definition: To turn, rotate, or change direction; also means to transfer or pass something to another person or place.
Usage: Common in words like 转身 (turn around), 转弯 (turn a corner), 转账 (transfer money)

Definition: East; the cardinal direction where the sun rises. Also used as a component in many compound words related to direction and geography.
Usage: Common in words like 东方 (the East), 东西 (thing/stuff, literally 'east-west'), and 东边 (east side)

Definition: A written character or word; can also refer to a person's formal name or style name in classical contexts.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 汉字 (Chinese characters), 名字 (name), and 文字 (written language)

Definition: To hope for or cling to something; also used as a suffix in place names and certain nouns
Usage: Common in words like 尾巴 (tail), 嘴巴 (mouth), and place names like 成都巴 or 巴黎 (Paris)

Definition: Don't; used to tell someone not to do something, forming a negative imperative command.
Usage: Common in phrases like 别走 (don't go), 别说话 (don't talk)

Definition: To fix, set, or decide; to make definite or certain. Also means stable, calm, or settled.
Usage: Common in words like 决定 (to decide), 一定 (certainly), 定时 (to set a time), and 安定 (stable)

Definition: To be called/named; to call or shout. Most commonly used to introduce names or to call out to someone.
Usage: Used in phrases like 我叫... (I am called/My name is...) or 叫他 (call him)

Definition: To grab, grasp, or catch something with your hand or claws. Also means to arrest or seize someone.
Usage: Common in phrases like 抓住 (to grab hold of), 抓紧 (to grasp tightly/hurry up), and 抓人 (to arrest someone)

Definition: Every, each; used to indicate that something applies to all members of a group individually without exception.
Usage: Commonly appears before time words (每天 every day, 每年 every year) or measure words (每个人 every person)

Definition: Eye; also means item, section, or category in formal contexts. This character is commonly seen in compound words related to vision or classification.
Usage: Found in words like 目标 (goal/target), 项目 (project/item), and 目的 (purpose)

Definition: Means 'sudden' or '突然' (suddenly), or to突出 (突 out/protrude). Most commonly used to describe unexpected or abrupt actions and changes.
Usage: Frequently appears in compounds like 突然 (suddenly), 突出 (outstanding/prominent), 突破 (breakthrough)

Definition: Same, identical, or together with; indicates similarity or doing something jointly with another person.
Usage: Common in words like 同学 (classmate), 同意 (agree), 不同 (different), and with 和/跟 to mean 'with'

Definition: Means 'towards' or 'facing' a direction; also means 'dynasty' or 'imperial court' as a noun.
Usage: Common in phrases like 朝着 (facing towards) and dynasty names like 唐朝 (Tang Dynasty)

Definition: Father or male parent. This character is primarily used in formal contexts or compound words rather than as a standalone term for 'dad'.
Usage: Common in words like 父亲 (fùqīn, father), 父母 (fùmǔ, parents), 祖父 (zǔfù, grandfather)

Definition: To divide, separate, or distinguish; also means a minute (unit of time) or a cent/point (unit of measurement)
Usage: Common in expressions like 分开 (to separate), 十分 (very/extremely), and telling time

Definition: Brain; the organ inside the head responsible for thinking and controlling the body. Also used in compounds related to the mind or head.
Usage: Common in words like 脑子 (brain/mind), 电脑 (computer, literally 'electric brain'), and 头脑 (mind/brains)

Definition: To recognize or identify someone or something; to acknowledge or admit something as true.
Usage: Common in words like 认识 (to know/recognize a person), 认为 (to think/believe), and 认真 (serious/earnest)

Definition: Bright, clear, or light; also means to understand or be obvious. Can refer to something being well-lit or a situation being clear and transparent.
Usage: Common in words like 明天 (tomorrow, literally 'bright day'), 明白 (to understand), and 光明 (bright/light)

Definition: A measure word (classifier) used for counting items, matters, or pieces of clothing. Also means 'item' or 'piece' as a noun.
Usage: Common in phrases like 一件衣服 (one piece of clothing) or 这件事 (this matter)

Definition: Name; also used as a measure word for people (counting individuals) and to mean 'famous' or 'reputation'.
Usage: Common in words like 名字 (name), 姓名 (full name), 有名 (famous), and counting people like 三名学生 (three students)

Definition: Classical/literary word meaning 'you' or 'your'; also used as a suffix in transliterations of foreign names and places.
Usage: Mainly found in formal writing, classical texts (如此而已 'that's all'), and names like 巴黎 (Paris) or 贝尔 (Bell)

Definition: A conjunction meaning 'but' or 'however' used to introduce a contrast or exception to what was previously stated.
Usage: Often appears as 但是 (danshi) in spoken and written Chinese, though 但 alone is common in formal writing

Definition: A building with multiple floors or stories; a floor/story of a building. Can also refer to a storied structure or tower.
Usage: Common in words like 大楼 (building), 二楼 (second floor), 楼上 (upstairs)

Definition: Public, common, or official; also means male (for animals) or duke. Often used in compound words related to public matters or formal contexts.
Usage: Common in words like 公司 (company), 公园 (public park), 公共 (public), and 老公 (husband)

Definition: Orchid, a type of elegant flower highly valued in Chinese culture. Also used as a component in names and place names.
Usage: Common in compounds like 兰花 (orchid flower) and names like 荷兰 (Holland/Netherlands)

Definition: Woman, female, or daughter. This character represents the female gender and is one of the most fundamental Chinese characters.
Usage: Used in compounds like 女人 (woman), 女孩 (girl), 女儿 (daughter), and as a radical in many characters related to females

Definition: A structural particle used to form noun phrases from verbs, meaning 'that which' or 'what is'. Also serves as a measure word for buildings like houses and schools.
Usage: Common in patterns like 所 + verb (e.g., 所说 'what is said') and as MW for institutions (e.g., 一所学校 'a school')

Definition: To die or death; can also mean extremely or to the extreme when used as an intensifier.
Usage: Used literally for death (死了 - died) or as an intensifier in colloquial speech (累死了 - extremely tired)

Definition: Soft leather or tanned hide; also commonly used as a Chinese surname (Wei)
Usage: Rarely used alone in modern Chinese; primarily appears in names and classical texts

Definition: To look for, search for, or seek something or someone. Also means to give change (money) in transactions.
Usage: Common in phrases like 找人 (look for someone), 找东西 (look for things), or 找钱 (give change)

Definition: A step or pace; can refer to a physical step when walking or a stage/phase in a process.
Usage: Common in words like 散步 (take a walk), 进步 (progress), and 步骤 (steps/procedure)

Definition: Fire; flame or heat produced by burning. Also means anger or temper in colloquial usage.
Usage: Common in words like 火车 (train, literally 'fire vehicle') and 发火 (to get angry)

Definition: Gold or metal; also means money or something precious and valuable.
Usage: Common in words like 金钱 (money), 黄金 (gold), and as a surname

Definition: Low in height, position, or level; the opposite of high (高). Can describe physical height, volume, temperature, price, or status.
Usage: Common in words like 低头 (lower one's head), 低价 (low price), 声音很低 (voice is low)

Definition: To use, to make, or to cause someone/something to do something. Also means 'to send' or 'envoy' in certain contexts.
Usage: Common in causative constructions like 使我高兴 (make me happy) and in the word 使用 (to use)

Definition: To add, increase, or put in more of something. Also means 'plus' in mathematical operations.
Usage: Common in phrases like 加油 (add fuel/cheer on), 加水 (add water), and math expressions like 一加一 (one plus one)

Definition: To sit or to sit down; to take a seat in a chair or other seating position.
Usage: Common in everyday phrases like 请坐 (please sit) and 坐下 (sit down). Also used for traveling by vehicle, as in 坐车 (take a car/bus)

Definition: Shape, form, or appearance of something; the physical outline or structure that something has.
Usage: Common in words like 形状 (shape), 形式 (form/format), and 情形 (situation/condition)

Definition: To become, to turn into, or to succeed in doing something. Also means to complete or accomplish something.
Usage: Common in words like 成功 (succeed), 成为 (become), and 完成 (complete)

Definition: To take, hold, or grasp something with your hand(s); to carry or bring something.
Usage: Common in everyday expressions like 拿书 (take a book) or 拿来 (bring it here)

Definition: A measure word used for counting books, magazines, and other bound printed materials; also means 'root' or 'origin' as a noun.
Usage: Most commonly used as a classifier, as in 一本书 (one book) or 三本杂志 (three magazines)

Definition: A modal particle used at the end of sentences to make suggestions, soften commands, or indicate uncertainty or supposition.
Usage: Common in phrases like 走吧 (let's go), 好吧 (okay then), or 是吧 (right?/isn't it?)

Definition: Aunt, specifically referring to mother's sister or mother's female friends; also used for wife's sister.
Usage: Common in family terms like 阿姨 (auntie, also used politely for any middle-aged woman)

Definition: A shaman, witch, or wizard; a person who practices spiritual rituals and communicates with spirits or deities in traditional Chinese culture.
Usage: Often appears in compound words like 巫师 (wūshī - wizard/sorcerer) or 巫婆 (wūpó - witch)

Definition: To think, to consider, or to miss someone. This character represents mental activity related to thinking, pondering, or longing.
Usage: Common in words like 思考 (to think/ponder), 思念 (to miss someone), and 意思 (meaning)

Definition: Square or direction; also means method or way of doing something. As a measure word, it refers to square units of area.
Usage: Common in words like 方法 (method), 地方 (place), 东方 (east/eastern direction), and 平方米 (square meter)

Definition: The color white; also means clear, plain, or blank. Can describe something pure, innocent, or done in vain.
Usage: Common in words like 白色 (white color), 明白 (to understand), 白天 (daytime), and 白费 (wasted effort)

Definition: Gift, present; also refers to ceremony, ritual, or etiquette/manners in social contexts.
Usage: Common in words like 礼物 (gift), 礼貌 (polite/politeness), and 婚礼 (wedding ceremony)

Definition: To do, to make, or to act as. Often used in compound words related to work, creation, or functioning.
Usage: Common in words like 工作 (work), 作业 (homework), 作用 (function/effect)

Definition: The number ten; a fundamental number in Chinese counting and the base of the decimal system.
Usage: Used in counting, telling time (十点 - 10 o'clock), and forming larger numbers like 十一 (eleven) or 二十 (twenty)

Definition: Table or desk; a piece of furniture with a flat surface supported by legs used for eating, working, or placing objects.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 桌子 (zhuōzi - table), 书桌 (shūzhuō - desk), 饭桌 (fànzhuō - dining table)

Definition: Mutually, each other, or one another; indicates reciprocal action or relationship between people or things.
Usage: Common in words like 相信 (believe), 相同 (same), 互相 (mutually)

Definition: A bag, sack, or pouch used for carrying or storing things. Can also be used as a measure word for things that come in bags.
Usage: Common in words like 口袋 (pocket), 袋子 (bag), 塑料袋 (plastic bag), or 一袋米 (a bag of rice)

Definition: A preposition meaning 'toward' or 'to' that indicates direction or the target of an action. Also used as a verb meaning 'to face' or 'to turn toward.'
Usage: Common in phrases like 向前 (forward), 向左 (to the left), or 向他学习 (learn from him)

Definition: To make a sound or noise; loud. Can also mean to respond or have an effect.
Usage: Common in words like 响亮 (loud and clear), 影响 (influence), and 声响 (sound/noise)

Definition: Thing, object, or matter; refers to physical items, creatures, or abstract entities.
Usage: Common in compounds like 动物 (animal), 食物 (food), 物品 (goods/items), and 人物 (person/character)

Definition: Flat, level, or even; also means peaceful or calm. Describes surfaces without bumps or slopes, and situations without conflict or disturbance.
Usage: Common in words like 平安 (safe/peaceful), 水平 (level/standard), and 公平 (fair)

Definition: A literary/classical Chinese particle meaning 'not' or 'no', equivalent to 不 in modern Chinese. Also used as a phonetic component in transliterations of foreign names and words.
Usage: Commonly seen in names like 弗吉尼亚 (Virginia) and classical texts; rarely used in everyday modern Chinese

Definition: To be startled, alarmed, or surprised; to shock or frighten someone or something.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 吃惊 (be surprised), 惊讶 (amazed), and 惊喜 (pleasant surprise)

Definition: A room or house; a general term for living spaces and buildings used for residence.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 房间 (room), 房子 (house), and 厨房 (kitchen)

Definition: To dare or have the courage to do something. Often used to express boldness or willingness to take risks.
Usage: Common in phrases like 我不敢 (I don't dare) or 你敢吗? (Do you dare?)

Definition: A question particle used to soften questions or indicate an ongoing situation. Also used to ask 'what about' or 'where is' something/someone.
Usage: Common in questions like 你呢? (What about you?) or 他在哪儿呢? (Where is he?)

Definition: To do or to work; also means dry (as an adjective). As a verb, it's commonly used in colloquial speech to mean 'do' or 'engage in an activity.'
Usage: Used in phrases like 干什么 (do what), 干活 (do work), or 干杯 (cheers/bottoms up)

Definition: Should or ought to, indicating obligation or necessity; also used to mean 'that particular' or 'the said' when referring to something previously mentioned.
Usage: Common in phrases like 该做 (should do) or 该学生 (that student)

Definition: To flash, shine, or flicker with sudden light; also means to dodge or move quickly to the side.
Usage: Common in words like 闪电 (lightning), 闪光 (flash), and when describing quick movements to avoid something

Definition: A surname (one of the common Chinese family names); also means 'suddenly' or 'quickly' in classical Chinese.
Usage: Most commonly encountered as a surname, as in 霍元甲 (Huo Yuanjia, a famous martial artist)

Definition: To resemble, to be similar to, or to seem like something. Often used to make comparisons between things or describe appearances.
Usage: Commonly appears in compounds like 似乎 (sìhū - seemingly) and 相似 (xiāngsì - similar), or in the pattern A似B (A resembles B)

Definition: To change, transform, or become different. This verb describes the process of something becoming altered or modified from its original state.
Usage: Common in words like 变化 (change), 改变 (to change), and 变成 (to become)

Definition: Empty or vacant; having nothing inside or unoccupied. Can also mean sky or air.
Usage: Common in words like 空间 (space), 天空 (sky), and 空的 (empty)

Definition: Means 'whole', 'entire', 'complete', or 'all'. Used to indicate completeness or totality of something.
Usage: Common in phrases like 全部 (all/entire), 全国 (whole country), 安全 (safety/safe)

Definition: Physical strength, power, or force; also refers to ability or capability to do something.
Usage: Common in words like 力量 (strength), 努力 (effort), 能力 (ability), and 力气 (physical strength)

Definition: To handle, manage, or take care of something; to do or conduct business or affairs.
Usage: Common in words like 办公 (work in an office), 办法 (method/way), and 办事 (handle affairs)

Definition: Mouth; the body part used for eating, drinking, and speaking.
Usage: Common in everyday expressions like 张嘴 (open one's mouth) or 嘴巴 (mouth)

Definition: Husband or man (formal/literary); also used as a classical Chinese particle at the beginning of sentences for emphasis.
Usage: Common in words like 丈夫 (zhàngfu, husband) and 夫妻 (fūqī, married couple)

Definition: Question word meaning 'who' or 'whom', used to ask about a person's identity.
Usage: Used in questions like 你是谁? (Who are you?) or 谁来了? (Who came?)

Definition: Indicates that something has just happened or occurred a very short time ago, equivalent to 'just' or 'just now' in English.
Usage: Commonly used before verbs, as in 我刚到 (I just arrived) or 他刚走 (He just left)

Definition: Root (of a plant or tree); also used as a measure word for long, thin objects like sticks, strings, or hair strands.
Usage: Common in phrases like 树根 (tree root) or as a counter: 一根头发 (one strand of hair), 三根香蕉 (three bananas)

Definition: A measure word for events, performances, games, or occurrences; also means an open space, field, or venue.
Usage: Used to count events like 一场电影 (one movie showing), 一场比赛 (one game/match), or refers to places like 广场 (plaza), 球场 (sports field)

Definition: Pointed, sharp, or having a tip; describes objects that taper to a point or end in a sharp edge.
Usage: Common in words like 尖叫 (to scream), 笔尖 (pen tip), 尖锐 (sharp/acute)

Definition: To sweep or clean with a broom; also means to scan (as in scanning a QR code with your phone).
Usage: Common in 扫地 (sweep the floor) and 扫码 (scan a code)

Definition: To wear or put on (clothing, shoes, or accessories that go through or onto the body); to pierce through or penetrate.
Usage: Most commonly used for clothing items like 穿衣服 (wear clothes), 穿鞋 (wear shoes). Also means to pass through, as in 穿过 (pass through).

Definition: Fragrance or pleasant aroma. This character is often used in literary contexts or as part of compound words related to pleasant smells.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 芬芳 (fēnfāng - fragrant) and in transliterations of foreign names like 芬兰 (Fēnlán - Finland)

Definition: Competition, match, or contest; can also be used as a verb meaning 'to compete' or 'to race'
Usage: Common in words like 比赛 (competition), 赛跑 (race), 足球赛 (football match)

Definition: Question word meaning 'which' or 'where', used to ask about choices or locations.
Usage: Common in questions like 哪个 (which one), 哪里 (where), 哪天 (which day)

Definition: Outside, outer, or external; refers to anything beyond a boundary or different from oneself. Also means foreign or unrelated.
Usage: Common in words like 外面 (outside), 外国 (foreign country), 外婆 (maternal grandmother)

Definition: Foot; the lower part of the leg below the ankle used for standing and walking. Can also refer to the base or bottom part of objects.
Usage: Common in everyday expressions like 脚下 (under one's feet) and 山脚 (foot of a mountain)

Definition: A flat, thin piece or slice of something; also used as a measure word for flat, thin objects like slices, tablets, or expanses of land.
Usage: Common in phrases like 一片面包 (a slice of bread), 照片 (photograph), or 片刻 (a brief moment)

Definition: To stare at or gaze fixedly at something or someone; to keep a close watch on.
Usage: Often used in contexts like 盯着看 (stare at) or 盯住 (keep eyes fixed on)

Definition: Thatched roof or thatch; also refers to thorny plants or brambles.
Usage: Mainly appears in compound words like 茅茨 (thatched cottage) or in place names like 茨城

Definition: To close, shut, or turn off; also means a barrier, pass, or checkpoint. As a verb, it's the opposite of 开 (kāi, to open).
Usage: Common in phrases like 关门 (close the door), 关灯 (turn off the light), 关系 (relationship/connection)

Definition: Hope or wish; also means rare or scarce. Most commonly seen in compound words rather than used alone.
Usage: Found in words like 希望 (xīwàng - hope), 希奇 (xīqí - rare), and 希腊 (xīlà - Greece)

Definition: Clear, clean, or pure; describes something that is transparent, uncontaminated, or easy to understand.
Usage: Common in words like 清楚 (clear/obvious), 清水 (clear water), and 清洁 (clean)

Definition: Wolf; a wild carnivorous animal known for hunting in packs.
Usage: Common in idioms and expressions like 狼狈 (in a difficult position) and 狼来了 (the boy who cried wolf)

Definition: To rise, prosper, or flourish; to start or establish something. Also means interest or enthusiasm (when pronounced xìng in the fourth tone).
Usage: Common in words like 兴奋 (excited), 高兴 (happy), and 兴起 (to rise up)

Definition: To receive, catch, or pick up something; to connect or join things together.
Usage: Common in phrases like 接电话 (answer the phone), 接人 (pick someone up), 接着 (continue/next)

Definition: Fertile or rich (describing soil or land); to irrigate or water land.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 肥沃 (fertile) and in brand names like 沃尔玛 (Walmart)

Definition: To leave, depart from, or be away from a place or person; also means distance or separation from something.
Usage: Common in expressions like 离开 (to leave), 距离 (distance), and 离...远/近 (far from/close to)

Definition: A prefix or adverb meaning 'not' or 'non-', used to negate or indicate the opposite of something. More formal than 不 (bù).
Usage: Common in words like 非常 (fēicháng - very/extremely) and 非法 (fēifǎ - illegal)

Definition: Inside, interior, or within; refers to the inner part or internal area of something, as opposed to outside (外).
Usage: Common in words like 国内 (domestic/within the country), 室内 (indoor), and 内容 (content/contents)

Definition: Mother or mom; an informal, affectionate term for one's female parent.
Usage: Commonly used in 妈妈 (māma, mom) and appears in family-related expressions

Definition: To bring, carry, or take something/someone along with you; can also mean to wear or have something on you.
Usage: Common in phrases like 带钱 (bring money), 带孩子 (take care of children), 带路 (lead the way)

Definition: Universal, general, or common; means widespread or applicable to all.
Usage: Most commonly seen in words like 普通 (pǔtōng - ordinary/common) and 普遍 (pǔbiàn - universal/widespread)

Definition: Question particle placed at the end of a statement to turn it into a yes/no question.
Usage: Used in phrases like 你好吗? (How are you?) and 这是书吗? (Is this a book?)

Definition: To breathe in, inhale, or suck in; to absorb or draw in something (air, liquid, smoke, etc.)
Usage: Common in words like 呼吸 (breathe), 吸烟 (smoke/smoking), 吸收 (absorb)

Definition: To point at or indicate something; also means finger. As a verb, it refers to pointing out, directing attention to, or referring to something specific.
Usage: Common in words like 手指 (finger), 指出 (to point out), and 指导 (to guide/instruct)

Definition: Essence, spirit, or energy; also means refined, skilled, or精通 (proficient). Can refer to精神 (spirit/vitality) or精彩 (brilliant/wonderful).
Usage: Common in words like 精神 (spirit), 精彩 (wonderful), 酒精 (alcohol), and 精通 (proficient in)

Definition: Old or aged; also used as a prefix to show respect or familiarity with people's surnames or to indicate long-standing status.
Usage: Common in words like 老师 (teacher), 老人 (elderly person), or 老王 (Old Wang - familiar address)

Definition: To allow, permit, or promise; also means 'many' or 'much' when used in certain compounds.
Usage: Common in words like 也许 (perhaps), 许多 (many), and 允许 (to permit)

Definition: Eagle or hawk; a large bird of prey known for its sharp vision and powerful hunting abilities.
Usage: Often used in metaphors for keen observation (鹰眼 eagle eye) or in names and symbolic contexts

Definition: Book or written work. One of the most fundamental nouns for reading materials and literature.
Usage: Used in common words like 看书 (read a book), 书店 (bookstore), 图书馆 (library)

Definition: To serve as, to act as, or to work as something; also means 'when' or 'at the time of' in certain contexts.
Usage: Common in phrases like 当老师 (to work as a teacher) or 当时 (at that time)

Definition: To put, place, or set down something; also means to release, let go, or let out.
Usage: Common in everyday expressions like 放下 (put down), 放学 (school lets out), 放心 (feel relieved)

Definition: A board, plank, or flat piece of wood or other material; can also mean stiff or rigid.
Usage: Common in words like 黑板 (blackboard), 木板 (wooden plank), and 老板 (boss)

Definition: To be happy, joyful, or merry; to like or enjoy something. This character is rarely used alone in modern Chinese.
Usage: Most commonly seen in compounds like 欢迎 (huānyíng - welcome), 喜欢 (xǐhuan - to like), and 欢乐 (huānlè - joyful)

Definition: Reason, logic, or principle; also means to manage, pay attention to, or tidy up. As a noun, it refers to rational thinking or natural laws.
Usage: Common in words like 道理 (reason/truth), 理解 (understand), 管理 (manage), and 不理 (ignore)

Definition: To blink or wink; the rapid closing and opening of one or both eyelids.
Usage: Most commonly used in 眨眼 (zhǎyǎn - to blink) and 眨眼睛 (zhǎ yǎnjing - to blink one's eyes)

Definition: To be willing to or to agree to do something; to consent or affirm.
Usage: Commonly used in phrases like 肯定 (certainly/affirmative) and 我肯 (I'm willing)

Definition: Light in weight or gentle in manner; not heavy or not serious. Can describe physical lightness, soft actions, or minor degree.
Usage: Common in words like 轻松 (relaxed), 年轻 (young), 轻声 (soft voice), and 轻重 (weight/importance)

Definition: To wait or await; refers to a period of time or season. Most commonly seen in compound words related to waiting or time periods.
Usage: Found in common words like 时候 (shíhou - time/moment), 等候 (děnghòu - to wait), and 气候 (qìhòu - climate)

Definition: A possessive pronoun meaning 'his', 'her', 'its', or 'their'; also used as a demonstrative meaning 'that' or 'such' in formal or written Chinese.
Usage: Common in formal expressions like 其他 (qítā - other), 其中 (qízhōng - among which), and 尤其 (yóuqí - especially)

Definition: A scholar, soldier, or person with specialized skills; historically referred to educated gentlemen or warriors in ancient China.
Usage: Commonly appears in compound words like 战士 (warrior), 护士 (nurse), 博士 (doctor/PhD), and 律师 (lawyer)

Definition: A bed, the piece of furniture used for sleeping or resting.
Usage: Common in phrases like 上床 (go to bed), 床上 (on the bed), 一张床 (a bed)

Definition: To sink or submerge in water; also means heavy or deep in a figurative sense.
Usage: Common in words like 沉默 (silent), 沉重 (heavy/serious), and 下沉 (to sink down)

Definition: To stare or glare at someone with wide-open eyes, often expressing anger, surprise, or disapproval.
Usage: Common in phrases like 瞪眼 (stare with wide eyes) or 瞪着他 (glare at him)

Definition: To remember, to record, or to write down. Also means to take notes or keep a record of something.
Usage: Common in words like 记得 (to remember), 日记 (diary), 记录 (to record)

Definition: Heavy or weighty; also means important or serious. Describes physical weight or the significance/gravity of something.
Usage: Common in words like 重要 (important), 体重 (body weight), and 严重 (serious)

Definition: To show, display, or reveal; to be obvious or apparent. Often used to describe something becoming visible or evident.
Usage: Common in words like 显示 (to display), 明显 (obvious), and 显得 (to appear/seem)

Definition: Good fortune, happiness, or blessing. This character represents luck and prosperity in Chinese culture.
Usage: Commonly seen during Chinese New Year on red decorations, and in phrases like 幸福 (happiness) and 祝福 (blessing/wish)

Definition: To wait or await; also used to mean 'rank/class' or as a suffix meaning 'and so on/etc.'
Usage: Common in phrases like 等一下 (wait a moment) and 我等 (I and others/we)

Definition: A character primarily used in transliterating foreign names and places, meaning 'to enlighten' or 'to guide' in classical Chinese.
Usage: Commonly seen in names like 迪士尼 (Dísīní, Disney) and 迪拜 (Dìbài, Dubai)

Definition: To cut, slice, or chop something with a knife or sharp tool. Also means 'all' or 'everything' in certain contexts.
Usage: Common in cooking contexts like 切菜 (cut vegetables) and in phrases like 一切 (everything)

Definition: Severe, strict, or harsh; also means fierce or intense. Most commonly seen in compound words describing strictness or intensity.
Usage: Common in words like 厉害 (lìhai - powerful/awesome), 严厉 (yánlì - stern/strict)

Definition: Means 'pair' or 'double'; used as a measure word for things that come in pairs like shoes, chopsticks, or hands.
Usage: Common in phrases like 一双鞋 (a pair of shoes) or 双手 (both hands)

Definition: Means 'other' or 'another', indicating something different or separate from what has been mentioned.
Usage: Commonly used in phrases like 另外 (in addition), 另一个 (another one), or 另一方面 (on the other hand)

Definition: Means 'like', 'as', or 'according to', used to make comparisons or indicate similarity between things.
Usage: Common in phrases like 如果 (if), 例如 (for example), and 如此 (like this/such)

Definition: Fruit; also means result or outcome. As a suffix, it appears in words for specific fruits like 苹果 (apple) and 水果 (fruit).
Usage: Commonly used in compound words related to fruits and results

Definition: Grade, level, or rank in a hierarchical system. Used to indicate classification, stages, or degrees of something.
Usage: Common in contexts like school grades (年级), difficulty levels (初级, 中级, 高级), and rankings (一级, 二级)

Definition: To injure or hurt (physically or emotionally); an injury or wound.
Usage: Common in words like 受伤 (to be injured), 伤心 (sad/heartbroken), 伤口 (wound)

Definition: To toil or work hard; labor or effort. Also used as a polite expression meaning 'to trouble' or 'to bother' someone.
Usage: Common in phrases like 劳驾 (excuse me, may I trouble you) and 辛劳 (hard work/toil)

Definition: An adverb meaning 'actually (not)' or 'in fact (not)', used to emphasize negation or contrast with expectations. Also means 'and' or 'together' when used as a conjunction.
Usage: Most commonly seen in negative sentences like 并不 (actually not) or 并没有 (in fact did not)

Definition: Indicates direction or movement toward a place or direction, meaning 'to' or 'toward'.
Usage: Commonly used before verbs of motion like 往前走 (go forward) or 往北 (toward the north)

Definition: To pour or concentrate; to focus attention on something or to make a note/annotation.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 注意 (zhùyì - to pay attention) and 注册 (zhùcè - to register)

Definition: Ball or sphere; any round object used in sports or games
Usage: Common in sports terms like 足球 (soccer), 篮球 (basketball), 网球 (tennis)

Definition: Ear; the organ used for hearing. Also appears as a radical in characters related to hearing or the ear.
Usage: Common in words like 耳朵 (ear), 耳机 (earphones/headphones)

Definition: Means 'because' or 'cause/reason'. Most commonly used in the compound word 因为 (yīnwèi) meaning 'because'.
Usage: Often appears in cause-and-effect sentences like 因为...所以... (because...therefore...)

Definition: A cup or glass used for drinking; also serves as a measure word for beverages.
Usage: Used in phrases like 一杯水 (a cup of water) or 茶杯 (teacup)

Definition: God, deity, or spirit; can also mean magical, mystical, or supernatural. Additionally used to describe someone's mental state or expression.
Usage: Common in words like 神话 (mythology), 精神 (spirit/mind), and 神奇 (magical)

Definition: A courtyard or enclosed area; also refers to institutions like hospitals, colleges, or government departments.
Usage: Common in words like 医院 (hospital), 学院 (college), 法院 (court)

Definition: To lift, raise, or hold up; also means to cite or give an example.
Usage: Common in words like 举手 (raise one's hand), 举行 (hold/conduct an event), and 举例 (give an example)

Definition: Close, intimate, or related by blood; can also mean to kiss or to do something personally.
Usage: Common in words like 父亲 (father), 母亲 (mother), 亲人 (relatives), and 亲自 (personally)

Definition: To like, to be fond of, or to be happy/delighted about something. Also means joy, happiness, or good news (especially relating to weddings and celebrations).
Usage: Common in words like 喜欢 (to like), 喜事 (happy occasion), and 欢喜 (happy)

Definition: A broom or brush used for sweeping. This character is often seen in compound words related to cleaning.
Usage: Commonly appears in words like 扫帚 (sǎozhou, broom)

Definition: Means 'without', 'not have', or 'lacking'. It is the opposite of 有 (yǒu, to have) and is used to indicate absence or negation.
Usage: Common in phrases like 无聊 (bored, literally 'without interest') and 无法 (unable to, cannot)

Definition: Full or filled to capacity; can also mean satisfied or to reach a certain amount or time period.
Usage: Common in expressions like 满了 (it's full), 不满 (dissatisfied), or 满18岁 (to reach 18 years old)

Definition: Chapter or section of a book or document; also means seal, stamp, or badge.
Usage: Common in 第一章 (chapter one), 文章 (article/essay), 印章 (seal/stamp)

Definition: Vehicle or car; any wheeled mode of transportation including bicycles, cars, trains, and carts.
Usage: Common in words like 汽车 (car), 火车 (train), 自行车 (bicycle)

Definition: The number four. It is one of the basic counting numbers in Mandarin Chinese.
Usage: Used in counting, dates, addresses, and mathematical expressions like 四个人 (four people)

Definition: Should, ought to; to respond or answer to something. Also means to agree to or comply with a request.
Usage: Common in words like 应该 (yīnggāi - should) and 反应 (fǎnyìng - reaction/response)

Definition: Side, beside, or next to something; indicates a position adjacent to or near a reference point.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 旁边 (beside/next to) and 路旁 (roadside)

Definition: Forest or grove; a dense collection of trees. Also commonly used as a surname (Lin).
Usage: Found in words like 森林 (forest) and 树林 (woods); very common as a family name

Definition: Hemp or flax (the plant/fiber); also means numb or tingly (as a physical sensation).
Usage: Common in words like 麻烦 (trouble/bothersome), 芝麻 (sesame), and 麻木 (numb)

Definition: A polite measure word (classifier) used for counting people, especially in formal contexts; also means 'position' or 'place' as a noun.
Usage: Used in phrases like 这位老师 (this teacher) or 三位客人 (three guests)

Definition: A measure word for machines, equipment, and performances; also means platform, stage, or table. Commonly used as a short form for Taiwan (台湾).
Usage: Used in phrases like 一台电脑 (one computer), 舞台 (stage), or 台北 (Taipei)

Definition: To fall, drop, or descend; can refer to physical falling (like leaves or rain) or abstract decline (like falling behind).
Usage: Common in words like 落下 (to fall down), 降落 (to land), 落后 (to lag behind)

Definition: To need or require something; to be necessary or essential.
Usage: Most commonly seen in compounds like 需要 (xūyào, to need) and 必需 (bìxū, essential/necessary)

Definition: Chief, leader, or first place; describes something big, tall, or outstanding in size or importance.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 魁梧 (tall and sturdy), 夺魁 (win first place), or 罪魁祸首 (chief culprit)

Definition: Breath or rest; also refers to interest (on money) or news/information. Most commonly seen in compound words related to breathing, resting, or息 息相关 (closely related).
Usage: Common in words like 休息 (to rest), 利息 (interest), 消息 (news), and 气息 (breath)

Definition: To lift or raise something, typically with effort or by multiple people working together. Can also mean to raise one's head or eyes to look up.
Usage: Common in phrases like 抬头 (raise one's head), 抬起 (lift up), or 抬桌子 (carry a table)

Definition: To pull, drag, or draw something toward oneself or in a particular direction. Can also mean to play (a stringed instrument) or to transport.
Usage: Common in phrases like 拉手 (hold hands), 拉小提琴 (play violin), 拉车 (pull a cart)

Definition: To lift, raise, or carry something (usually with a handle); to mention or bring up a topic in conversation.
Usage: Common in words like 提高 (to improve/raise), 提问 (to ask a question), 提供 (to provide)

Definition: A clock or bell; also used as a measure word for time duration in hours.
Usage: Common in expressions like 闹钟 (alarm clock), 钟头 (hour), and 一点钟 (one o'clock)

Definition: Cold or cool in temperature; can also describe a person or atmosphere as unfriendly or indifferent.
Usage: Used to describe weather (天气很冷 - the weather is cold), food/drinks (冷水 - cold water), or emotions (冷淡 - indifferent)

Definition: To pant, gasp, or breathe heavily, especially when out of breath from exertion or illness.
Usage: Common in expressions like 喘气 (to catch one's breath) and 气喘 (asthma)

Definition: A measure word for pieces, chunks, or blocks of something; also the informal word for the Chinese currency yuan (dollar)
Usage: Used with objects like 一块钱 (one yuan), 一块蛋糕 (a piece of cake), or 一块石头 (a block of stone)

Definition: To harm, injure, or cause damage to someone or something; can also mean to kill or murder in certain contexts.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 害怕 (to be afraid), 伤害 (to hurt/harm), and 害虫 (pest/harmful insect)

Definition: Spirit, soul, or supernatural being; also means quick, nimble, or effective when describing responsiveness.
Usage: Common in words like 灵魂 (soul), 精灵 (spirit/elf), 灵活 (flexible/agile), and 灵验 (effective/efficacious)

Definition: Melon or gourd; refers to various types of melons and gourd-like fruits and vegetables.
Usage: Common in words like 西瓜 (watermelon), 黄瓜 (cucumber), 南瓜 (pumpkin)

Definition: Flower or blossom; can also mean to spend (money or time) when used as a verb.
Usage: As a noun in 鲜花 (fresh flowers); as a verb in 花钱 (spend money)

Definition: To look at, to view, or to regard/consider something in a certain way. Often used in formal or written contexts.
Usage: Common in compounds like 电视 (television), 视为 (regard as), and 重视 (attach importance to)

Definition: To lie down flat or prostrate oneself; to hide or ambush. Also means to submit or yield to someone or something.
Usage: Common in words like 伏击 (ambush), 起伏 (rise and fall), and 伏天 (dog days of summer)

Definition: To stop, halt, or cease movement or activity; to park (a vehicle).
Usage: Common in phrases like 停车 (to park a car) and 停止 (to stop/cease)

Definition: A hall or large room, especially for formal gatherings or ceremonies; also used as a measure word for classes or lessons.
Usage: Common in words like 课堂 (classroom), 食堂 (dining hall), and 一堂课 (one class session)

Definition: To lose or to miss; to fail to keep, maintain, or achieve something.
Usage: Common in words like 失败 (to fail), 失去 (to lose), 失望 (disappointed)

Definition: Late or evening; refers to the latter part of the day or something happening after the expected time.
Usage: Common in words like 晚上 (evening), 晚饭 (dinner), and 晚了 (it's late)

Definition: A period of time or scheduled date; commonly used to indicate stages, terms, or expected times.
Usage: Found in words like 星期 (week), 学期 (semester), 日期 (date), and 期待 (to expect)

Definition: A conjunction meaning 'and', 'but', or 'yet' that connects clauses or phrases, often showing contrast or sequence. More formal and literary than 和 (hé).
Usage: Common in written Chinese and formal speech, as in 美而便宜 (beautiful and cheap) or 简单而有效 (simple yet effective)

Definition: Clothing, garments, or clothes in general. This character refers to items worn on the body.
Usage: Often appears in compound words like 衣服 (yīfu, clothes) and 毛衣 (máoyī, sweater)

Definition: Quiet, calm, or still; describes an absence of noise or movement.
Usage: Common in words like 安静 (quiet/peaceful) and 冷静 (calm/composed)

Definition: Bright or light; describes something that emits or reflects light well, or is clear and shining.
Usage: Common in phrases like 明亮 (bright), 灯亮了 (the light is on), or 月亮 (moon)
