Definition: To pass, transmit, or spread something from one person or place to another; to convey information, objects, or traditions.
Usage: Common in words like 传统 (tradition), 传播 (to spread/disseminate), and 传递 (to pass on)

Definition: To protect, keep, or maintain something in its current state; to guarantee or ensure safety.
Usage: Common in words like 保护 (protect), 保持 (maintain), 保证 (guarantee), and 环保 (environmental protection)

Definition: To finish, complete, or run out of something. Often used as a complement after verbs to indicate completion of an action.
Usage: Common in phrases like 做完 (finish doing), 吃完 (finish eating), or 完了 (it's over/finished)

Definition: To treat or deal with someone in a certain way; to wait or stay. Also means treatment or hospitality shown to someone.
Usage: Common in words like 对待 (to treat), 待遇 (treatment/benefits), and 等待 (to wait)

Definition: To be afraid of or to fear something; to worry that something bad might happen.
Usage: Common in expressions like 我怕狗 (I'm afraid of dogs) or 别怕 (don't be afraid)

Definition: To be willing, to wish, or to hope for something; expresses desire or willingness to do something.
Usage: Common in phrases like 我愿意 (I'm willing) and 祝愿 (to wish someone well)

Definition: Cat; a common domestic animal kept as a pet or for catching mice.
Usage: Used in words like 猫咪 (kitty) and 熊猫 (panda, literally 'bear cat')

Definition: Classical Chinese possessive or attributive particle, equivalent to 的 in modern Chinese. Also used to mean 'to go to' in literary contexts.
Usage: Mainly found in formal writing, idioms, and classical expressions like 总之 (in summary) or place names

Definition: A measure word for sentences or lines of text; also means 'sentence' as a noun.
Usage: Used in phrases like 一句话 (one sentence) or 两句诗 (two lines of poetry)

Definition: To pull out, draw out, or extract something from a larger group or container; also means to smoke (a cigarette) or to take time from a busy schedule.
Usage: Common in phrases like 抽烟 (to smoke), 抽签 (to draw lots), 抽时间 (to find/make time)

Definition: A tree; a woody plant with a trunk and branches.
Usage: Common in words like 树木 (trees), 果树 (fruit tree), 大树 (big tree)

Definition: Deep or profound, describing physical depth (like water or holes) or abstract depth (like knowledge, feelings, or colors).
Usage: Common in words like 深夜 (late night), 深色 (dark color), 深刻 (profound)

Definition: Simple, brief, or uncomplicated. Often used to describe things that are easy to understand or not complex.
Usage: Common in words like 简单 (simple), 简历 (resume/CV), and 简体字 (simplified characters)

Definition: Near or close in distance or time; can also mean recent or intimate.
Usage: Used in words like 最近 (recently), 附近 (nearby), 接近 (to approach)

Definition: Far or distant in space or time; the opposite of near (近).
Usage: Used to describe physical distance (很远 - very far) or relationships (远亲 - distant relative)

Definition: Top, peak, or summit of something; also used as a measure word for things with tops like hats or sedan chairs
Usage: Common in words like 山顶 (mountain top) and as a measure word in 一顶帽子 (one hat)

Definition: To cause, to make, or to order/command someone to do something. Also used as a formal word for 'order' or 'decree'.
Usage: Commonly seen in compounds like 命令 (command), 令人 (to make people feel), and 口令 (password/command)

Definition: Half or semi-; indicates one of two equal parts or an incomplete amount of something.
Usage: Common in time expressions like 半天 (half a day), 一半 (one half), and 半夜 (midnight)

Definition: Bottom, base, or foundation of something; the lowest part or end of an object or place.
Usage: Common in words like 底下 (below/underneath), 海底 (seabed), 到底 (after all/in the end)

Definition: To resist, defend against, or ward off; also means imperial or related to the emperor in classical contexts.
Usage: Common in words like 防御 (defense), 抵御 (to resist), and historical terms like 御用 (for imperial use)

Definition: Early or morning; describes something happening in the early part of the day or before the expected time.
Usage: Commonly used in greetings like 早上好 (good morning) or to describe arriving early

Definition: Method, technique, or skill; often refers to a specialized art, craft, or systematic approach to doing something.
Usage: Commonly used in compound words like 技术 (technology), 美术 (fine arts), 手术 (surgery), and 武术 (martial arts)

Definition: The color red; also means popular, successful, or revolutionary in certain contexts.
Usage: Used to describe red objects like 红色 (red color), 红花 (red flower), or popularity as in 走红 (become popular/famous)

Definition: A table, form, or chart used to display information; also means a watch or meter for measuring time or quantities.
Usage: Common in words like 手表 (wristwatch), 表格 (form/table), and 时间表 (timetable)

Definition: To go through, connect, or lead to; to be open or unobstructed. Also means to communicate or understand thoroughly.
Usage: Common in words like 交通 (traffic), 通过 (to pass through), and 普通 (ordinary/common)

Definition: To defend, guard against, or prevent something from happening. Commonly used to describe protective measures or prevention of unwanted situations.
Usage: Found in words like 预防 (prevent), 防止 (prevent/guard against), 国防 (national defense)

Definition: Ghost, spirit, or demon; a supernatural being in Chinese folklore and culture. Also used informally to describe someone who is sneaky or crafty.
Usage: Common in expressions like 小鬼 (little devil/kid) or 鬼故事 (ghost story)

Definition: The number two; the second in a sequence or order.
Usage: Used in counting, dates, and ordinal expressions like 第二 (the second)

Definition: To fall down, collapse, or topple over; also means to pour (liquid) or to move backwards.
Usage: Common in phrases like 倒水 (pour water), 摔倒 (fall down), 倒车 (reverse a car)

Definition: Together, in total, or altogether; indicates a sum or collective amount.
Usage: Commonly used in phrases like 一共 (yígòng - altogether) to express totals, as in 一共十块钱 (altogether 10 yuan)

Definition: A quarter of an hour (15 minutes); also means to carve, engrave, or cut into a surface.
Usage: Most commonly used in telling time, like 三点一刻 (3:15) or 差一刻四点 (3:45). As a verb, used for carving or engraving.

Definition: Friend or friendship. This character represents a companion or someone you have a friendly relationship with.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 朋友 (péngyou - friend), 友好 (yǒuhǎo - friendly), and 友谊 (yǒuyì - friendship)

Definition: To exhale, breathe out, or call out loudly; also means to shout or yell someone's name.
Usage: Common in words like 呼吸 (to breathe), 呼叫 (to call out), and 欢呼 (to cheer)

Definition: To shake, tremble, or shiver; to vibrate or quiver suddenly or repeatedly.
Usage: Commonly used to describe physical shaking from cold (发抖), trembling from fear, or shaking something to remove dust

Definition: New, fresh, or recent; the opposite of old (旧). Used to describe things that have just been made, acquired, or are modern.
Usage: Common in words like 新年 (New Year), 新闻 (news), 新鲜 (fresh)

Definition: Ladder or stairs; a structure with steps used for climbing up or down.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 楼梯 (staircase), 电梯 (elevator), and 梯子 (ladder)

Definition: To play, have fun, or enjoy oneself; can also mean to play with something or visit a place for leisure.
Usage: Common in phrases like 玩游戏 (play games), 玩具 (toy), or 去北京玩 (go to Beijing for fun)

Definition: To manage, control, or be in charge of something; also means a tube or pipe as a noun.
Usage: Common in phrases like 管理 (to manage), 不管 (no matter/regardless), and 管子 (pipe/tube)

Definition: A measure word for short bursts or spells of something, like wind, rain, or sound. Also means battle formation or position in military contexts.
Usage: Common in phrases like 一阵风 (a gust of wind) or 一阵雨 (a spell of rain)

Definition: Difficult or hard; not easy to do or understand. Can also mean unpleasant or bad when describing situations.
Usage: Common in phrases like 很难 (very difficult), 难过 (sad/upset), 困难 (difficulty)

Definition: World, generation, or era. Refers to the human world, society, or a period of time spanning approximately 30 years.
Usage: Common in words like 世界 (world), 世纪 (century), and 一生一世 (one's whole life)

Definition: Agriculture or farming; also refers to a farmer or peasant.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 农民 (farmer), 农业 (agriculture), and 农村 (rural area/countryside)

Definition: To shout, yell, or call out loudly. Used when someone raises their voice to get attention or express strong emotion.
Usage: Common in phrases like 大声喊 (shout loudly) or 喊名字 (call someone's name)

Definition: To stuff, fill, or block something; to squeeze or cram into a space
Usage: Common in expressions like 塞车 (traffic jam) or 塞满 (to stuff full)

Definition: A wall, typically referring to the vertical structure that forms the side of a building or encloses an area.
Usage: Common in phrases like 墙壁 (wall), 长城 (Great Wall), and 撞墙 (hit a wall)

Definition: A character primarily used in transliterations of foreign words and names, most commonly seen in 姆妈 (māma, nanny/nursemaid) or foreign place names.
Usage: Frequently appears in words like 保姆 (bǎomǔ, nanny/housekeeper) and transliterations such as 斯德哥尔姆 (Stockholm)

Definition: To begin or start; the beginning or origin of something.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 开始 (kāishǐ - to start) and 始终 (shǐzhōng - from beginning to end)

Definition: A character primarily used in transliterations of foreign words and names, most commonly seen in Buddhist terms. Also means 'nun' in Buddhist context.
Usage: Common in words like 尼姑 (Buddhist nun), 尼泊尔 (Nepal), and 肯尼亚 (Kenya)

Definition: Work, labor, or worker; also refers to engineering or industry. One of the most fundamental characters related to employment and construction.
Usage: Common in words like 工作 (work/job), 工人 (worker), and 工程 (engineering/project)

Definition: Strong, powerful, or better than others. Can describe physical strength, ability, or intensity.
Usage: Common in words like 强大 (powerful), 坚强 (strong-willed), and comparisons like 比...强 (better than...)

Definition: Always, invariably; also means 'total' or 'overall'. Used as an adverb to indicate something happens consistently or as an adjective for totals and general situations.
Usage: Common in phrases like 总是 (always), 总共 (altogether), 总统 (president)

Definition: Moon; also means month in the calendar sense.
Usage: Used in time expressions like 一月 (January), 三个月 (three months), and phrases like 月亮 (moon)

Definition: To be annoyed, irritated, or troubled; to feel vexed or bothered by something or someone.
Usage: Commonly used in expressions like 烦人 (annoying), 烦恼 (worried/troubled), or 别烦我 (don't bother me)

Definition: Skin, leather, or outer covering/peel of something. Also means naughty or mischievous when describing behavior.
Usage: Common in words like 皮肤 (skin), 皮鞋 (leather shoes), 果皮 (fruit peel), and 顽皮 (naughty)

Definition: A measure word for books, films, machines, and vehicles; also means 'part', 'section', or 'department'
Usage: Used in phrases like 一部电影 (one film), 部分 (part/portion), or 外交部 (Ministry of Foreign Affairs)

Definition: To hide, conceal, or keep something secret; to be hidden or invisible from view.
Usage: Common in words like 隐藏 (to hide), 隐私 (privacy), and 隐瞒 (to conceal information)

Definition: The number five. One of the most basic and frequently used numbers in Chinese.
Usage: Used in counting, dates, times, and quantities like 五个人 (five people) or 星期五 (Friday)

Definition: To appoint or assign someone to a position; to take on or assume a responsibility or duty. Also means 'any' or 'no matter' when used in certain compound words.
Usage: Common in words like 任务 (task/mission), 责任 (responsibility), 任何 (any), and 担任 (to hold a post)

Definition: A place or location; also means to get along with someone or to handle/deal with a situation.
Usage: Common in words like 到处 (everywhere), 相处 (get along with), and 处理 (handle/deal with)

Definition: A character meaning 'girl' or 'young woman', primarily used as a suffix in names or informal terms for girls.
Usage: Commonly seen in names like 妮妮 (Nini) or in the word 小妮子 (little girl)

Definition: Real, true, or solid; refers to something actual or concrete as opposed to empty or false.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 现实 (reality), 实际 (actual), 老实 (honest), and 事实 (fact)

Definition: Huge, enormous, or gigantic in size or scale. Used to describe something exceptionally large or significant.
Usage: Commonly appears in words like 巨大 (jùdà - huge), 巨人 (jùrén - giant), and 巨额 (jù'é - enormous sum)

Definition: Means 'tiny', 'minute', or 'slight'; describes something extremely small or minimal in size, degree, or amount.
Usage: Common in words like 微笑 (smile), 微信 (WeChat), and 微小 (tiny)

Definition: Friend or companion. This character is most commonly seen in the word 朋友 (péngyou), meaning 'friend'.
Usage: Rarely used alone in modern Chinese; almost always appears in compound words like 朋友 (friend)

Definition: Chair or seat. Most commonly used in the compound word 椅子 (yǐzi) meaning chair.
Usage: Almost always appears as 椅子 rather than alone

Definition: To disappear, vanish, or eliminate; to reduce or dispel something.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 消息 (news), 取消 (cancel), 消费 (consume), and 消失 (disappear)

Definition: Male or man; refers to the masculine gender or a male person.
Usage: Common in words like 男人 (man), 男孩 (boy), and 男女 (male and female)

Definition: To sleep or go to bed. This is the primary verb used to express sleeping in Mandarin Chinese.
Usage: Commonly used in phrases like 睡觉 (shuì jiào - to sleep) and 睡着 (shuì zháo - to fall asleep)

Definition: Window; an opening in a wall or vehicle that lets in light and air, typically fitted with glass.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 窗户 (chuānghu - window) and 窗口 (chuāngkǒu - window/counter)

Definition: Cooked rice; a meal or food in general. This is one of the most essential food-related words in Chinese.
Usage: Used in common phrases like 吃饭 (eat a meal), 早饭 (breakfast), 午饭 (lunch), 晚饭 (dinner)

Definition: A preposition meaning 'in', 'at', 'to', or 'from' that indicates location, time, or direction. It is commonly used in formal or written Chinese to show relationships between actions and places/times.
Usage: Often appears in phrases like 位于 (to be located at), 关于 (about/regarding), 由于 (due to)

Definition: Still, yet; indicates that a situation or action continues unchanged from before
Usage: Commonly used in phrases like 仍然 (still, yet) and 仍旧 (still, as before)

Definition: To rest, take a break, or have time off from work or activities. Also means to stop or cease doing something.
Usage: Common in words like 休息 (rest), 休假 (take a vacation), and 退休 (retire)

Definition: Question word meaning 'what', 'why', or 'how'; used in formal or literary contexts to ask questions.
Usage: Common in phrases like 为何 (why), 如何 (how), and 何时 (when). More formal than 什么.

Definition: Means 'and', 'as well as', or 'to reach/attain'. Used to connect nouns or phrases in formal or written Chinese, similar to 'and' but more literary than 和.
Usage: Common in formal contexts like 老师及学生 (teachers and students) or in the word 以及 (as well as)

Definition: Week; also means 'around' or 'circumference'. Most commonly used in time expressions to refer to a week or days of the week.
Usage: Found in words like 星期/周末 (weekend), 周一 (Monday), 周围 (surroundings)

Definition: Dense, thick, or close together; secret or confidential. Describes things that are tightly packed or information that should be kept private.
Usage: Common in words like 秘密 (secret), 密码 (password), 紧密 (tight/close), and 茂密 (dense/thick)

Definition: A formal or literary word meaning 'will' or 'shall' to indicate future action; also used as a preposition meaning 'to take' or 'to use' to introduce an object that undergoes an action.
Usage: Common in written Chinese and the 将 (bǎ) construction, as in 将来 (future) or 将书放在桌子上 (place the book on the table)

Definition: Shadow or reflection; also commonly used to mean image, picture, or film/movie.
Usage: Found in words like 电影 (diànyǐng - movie), 影子 (yǐngzi - shadow), and 摄影 (shèyǐng - photography)

Definition: To stop, halt, or cease; to prevent or prohibit something from continuing.
Usage: Common in words like 停止 (to stop), 禁止 (to forbid), and 阻止 (to prevent)

Definition: Solemn, respectful, or reverent; describes a dignified and serious atmosphere or manner.
Usage: Commonly used in formal contexts and frequently appears in Chinese surnames (穆先生)

Definition: Wing, as in the wing of a bird or airplane; can also mean flank or side in formal contexts.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 机翼 (airplane wing), 左翼 (left wing), and 羽翼 (wings/feathers)

Definition: Leg; the limb used for standing and walking in humans and animals.
Usage: Used for both human legs (人的腿) and animal legs (动物的腿), as well as the legs of furniture like tables and chairs

Definition: Means 'hero' or 'outstanding/brilliant'; most commonly used as a short form for England/English (英国, 英语).
Usage: Frequently seen in 英国 (England/UK), 英语 (English language), and 英雄 (hero)

Definition: Blood; the red liquid that flows through the body. Can also refer to bloodline, descent, or family relations.
Usage: Common in medical contexts (献血 donate blood) and expressions about family ties (血缘 blood relation)

Definition: A corner or angle; also a unit of Chinese currency equal to one-tenth of a yuan (similar to a dime).
Usage: Used in geometry (角度 'angle'), locations (角落 'corner'), and money (一角 'one jiao')

Definition: To rush, hurry, or catch up with something or someone; also means to drive (animals) or to be in time for something.
Usage: Common in phrases like 赶时间 (rush for time), 赶车 (catch a bus/train), 赶快 (hurry up)

Definition: A team, group, or organized unit of people working together. Also used as a measure word for groups or lines of people.
Usage: Common in words like 球队 (sports team), 队伍 (队wǔ, team/troops), and 排队 (páiduì, to line up)

Definition: Main, primary, or principal; also means host, owner, or master. Used to indicate the primary or most important element of something.
Usage: Common in words like 主人 (host/owner), 主要 (main/primary), and 主席 (chairman)

Definition: A common Chinese surname (Lu). In classical Chinese, it also referred to a type of black color or a vessel.
Usage: Primarily used as a family name in modern Chinese, as in 卢浮宫 (Louvre Museum)

Definition: To receive, accept, or endure something; often used to indicate experiencing or suffering something (positive or negative).
Usage: Common in words like 接受 (to accept), 受伤 (to be injured), 感受 (to feel/experience)

Definition: A pile, heap, or stack of things; can also be used as a verb meaning to pile up or heap together.
Usage: Common as a measure word for piles of objects, like 一堆书 (a pile of books) or 堆雪人 (to build a snowman)

Definition: Child or young person. This character is rarely used alone and typically appears in compound words.
Usage: Most commonly seen in 孩子 (háizi, child) and 小孩 (xiǎohái, small child/kid)

Definition: Peaceful, calm, or safe; also means to install or settle. As an adjective, it describes a state of tranquility or security.
Usage: Common in words like 安全 (safety), 安静 (quiet), and 平安 (peace)

Definition: To help or assist someone with something. Can also mean a group or gang of people.
Usage: Very common in everyday speech, as in 帮我 (help me) or 帮忙 (to help/lend a hand)

Definition: To shake, sway, or rock back and forth. Can refer to physical movement of objects or body parts.
Usage: Common in words like 摇头 (shake one's head), 摇晃 (sway/rock), and 摇篮 (cradle)

Definition: To live, to be alive; living or alive (as an adjective). Also means lively, flexible, or movable.
Usage: Common in words like 生活 (life/to live), 活动 (activity), and 活着 (to be alive)

Definition: A class, team, or group of people organized together; also refers to a scheduled shift or regular transport service.
Usage: Common in contexts like 上班 (go to work), 班级 (class at school), 飞机班次 (flight schedule)

Definition: Okay, alright, or acceptable; indicates that something will work or is permissible. Also means a row, line, or profession/trade.
Usage: Commonly used in spoken Chinese to express agreement (行！= OK!) or to ask if something is acceptable (行吗？= Is that okay?)

Definition: Mirror or lens; a reflective surface used to see one's reflection or an optical device that focuses light.
Usage: Common in words like 镜子 (mirror), 眼镜 (eyeglasses), and 照镜子 (to look in a mirror)

Definition: To raise, keep, or support (animals, children, or plants); to nourish or cultivate.
Usage: Common in words like 养狗 (raise a dog), 养孩子 (raise children), 营养 (nutrition)

Definition: A hall or large room in a building; also used to refer to certain government departments or offices.
Usage: Common in words like 餐厅 (restaurant/dining hall), 客厅 (living room), and 办公厅 (general office)

Definition: Life, fate, or destiny; also means to command or order. Most commonly refers to one's life span or predetermined fate in Chinese culture.
Usage: Found in words like 生命 (life), 命运 (fate/destiny), and 命令 (command/order)

Definition: A curse or spell; to curse or put a hex on someone. Can also refer to incantations or magic formulas used in religious or mystical contexts.
Usage: Common in words like 诅咒 (curse), 咒语 (incantation/spell), 念咒 (chant a spell)

Definition: To surround, encircle, or enclose something; to gather around.
Usage: Common in words like 周围 (zhōuwéi - surroundings), 围巾 (wéijīn - scarf, literally 'surround cloth'), and 包围 (bāowéi - to surround)

Definition: Poor, inferior, or not good enough; also means to lack or fall short of a certain amount or standard.
Usage: Common in expressions like 差不多 (almost, about the same) or 很差 (very poor/bad)

Definition: To do, make, or handle something; to play with or fiddle with something. Often used colloquially to mean 'to get/obtain' or 'to cause/make happen'.
Usage: Common in everyday speech like 弄坏了 (broke it), 弄错了 (got it wrong), 你在弄什么? (What are you doing?)

Definition: Must, have to, or certainly; expresses necessity, obligation, or inevitability.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 必须 (must), 必要 (necessary), and 必然 (inevitable)

Definition: Evil, bad, or wicked; refers to something morally wrong or harmful. Can also mean fierce or ferocious.
Usage: Common in words like 恶人 (evil person), 罪恶 (sin/crime), 凶恶 (fierce)

Definition: Hair or fur on the body of humans or animals; also refers to feathers on birds. Additionally used as a unit of currency meaning one-tenth of a yuan (10 cents).
Usage: Common in words like 毛衣 (sweater, literally 'wool clothing') and 羽毛 (feather)

Definition: Boundary, border, or realm; commonly used to refer to different fields, circles, or worlds of activity.
Usage: Frequently appears in compounds like 世界 (world), 界限 (boundary), 科学界 (scientific community), 各界 (all walks of life)

Definition: A box, case, chest, or trunk used for storing or transporting items. Commonly refers to containers like suitcases, crates, or compartments.
Usage: Found in words like 箱子 (xiāngzi - box), 冰箱 (bīngxiāng - refrigerator), 邮箱 (yóuxiāng - mailbox)

Definition: Thunder or thunderstorm; the loud sound produced during a storm when lightning occurs.
Usage: Common in weather-related expressions like 打雷 (thunder strikes) and compound words like 雷雨 (thunderstorm)

Definition: To tremble, shake, or shiver, typically due to cold, fear, or emotion.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 颤抖 (chàndǒu - to shiver/tremble) and 发颤 (fāchàn - to shake)

Definition: Wheat or general grain crops; refers to cereal plants, especially wheat and barley.
Usage: Common in words like 小麦 (wheat), 麦片 (oatmeal), and 麦当劳 (McDonald's)

Definition: Tall or lofty; also means to disguise or pretend. Most commonly encountered as a surname (Qiao) or in compound words.
Usage: Frequently used in names like 乔木 (tall tree) or the surname 乔

Definition: To write or compose text, characters, or other written content. Can refer to writing by hand, typing, or creating written works like letters, essays, or books.
Usage: Common in phrases like 写字 (write characters), 写信 (write a letter), 写作业 (do homework/write assignments)

Definition: To wrap or包age something; also means a bag, bundle, or包aged item. As a verb, it can mean to包ver, surround, or include everything.
Usage: Common in words like 书包 (schoolbag), 包子 (steamed bun), and 包括 (to include)

Definition: To get stuck or wedged in something; also means 'card' (like credit card, ID card). As a verb, it describes something being jammed or blocked in a tight space.
Usage: Common in 卡住 (stuck), 信用卡 (credit card), 卡片 (card)

Definition: To participate in or take part in an activity or event; to join or attend.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 参加 (cānjiā - to participate) and 参观 (cānguān - to visit/tour)

Definition: Picture, diagram, map, or chart; any visual representation or illustration. Also means to plan or seek something.
Usage: Common in words like 地图 (map), 图书馆 (library), 图片 (picture/image)

Definition: Urgent, anxious, or in a hurry; describes situations requiring immediate attention or a state of worry and impatience.
Usage: Common in phrases like 着急 (worried/anxious), 急事 (urgent matter), 紧急 (emergency)

Definition: Wave or ripple, referring to the undulating movement of water or similar motion. Also used metaphorically for waves of events, trends, or influences.
Usage: Common in words like 波浪 (waves), 风波 (disturbance), and 波动 (fluctuation)

Definition: A character primarily used in place names and proper nouns, most commonly seen in 洛阳 (Luòyáng), an ancient Chinese city.
Usage: Rarely used alone; appears in geographical names like 洛杉矶 (Luòshānjī, Los Angeles) and historical references

Definition: To stay, remain, or keep; also means to leave behind or retain something for later use.
Usage: Common in phrases like 留学 (study abroad), 保留 (preserve/keep), and 留下 (leave behind/stay)

Definition: To know, to recognize, or to be acquainted with someone or something. Also means knowledge or awareness.
Usage: Common in words like 认识 (to know/recognize), 知识 (knowledge), and 常识 (common sense)

Definition: Soul or spirit; the spiritual or immaterial part of a person, often contrasted with the physical body.
Usage: Common in expressions like 灵魂 (línghún - soul), 魂魄 (húnpò - soul and spirit), and idioms about being scared or losing one's composure

Definition: Chaotic, messy, or in disorder; can also mean to confuse or mix up things randomly.
Usage: Common in phrases like 乱七八糟 (very messy) or 别乱说 (don't talk nonsense)

Definition: Means 'now' or 'the present'; refers to the current time period including today, this year, or modern times.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 今天 (today), 今年 (this year), and 古今 (ancient and modern)

Definition: To scare, frighten, or startle someone. Often used to describe causing fear or alarm in others.
Usage: Common in phrases like 吓人 (scary), 吓一跳 (to give someone a fright)

Definition: A tower or pagoda, typically referring to tall structures used for religious, commemorative, or architectural purposes.
Usage: Common in words like 宝塔 (pagoda), 铁塔 (iron tower), 灯塔 (lighthouse), and 埃菲尔铁塔 (Eiffel Tower)

Definition: To seal, close, or block something; also used as a measure word for letters and sealed items
Usage: Common in words like 封信 (a letter) and 封闭 (to seal/close)

Definition: To hold in one's arms or embrace; to cherish or keep in one's heart/mind (feelings, thoughts, or memories)
Usage: Common in words like 怀念 (to miss/cherish memories), 怀孕 (to be pregnant), and 胸怀 (mind/heart)

Definition: Writing, text, or language; also refers to culture, literature, or civilian matters (as opposed to military). A fundamental character often used in compound words related to written communication and cultural concepts.
Usage: Common in words like 中文 (Chinese language), 文化 (culture), 文章 (article/essay)

Definition: Sun or day; refers to the celestial body or a 24-hour period of time
Usage: Common in words like 今日 (today), 明日 (tomorrow), 生日 (birthday), and 日本 (Japan, literally 'sun origin')

Definition: To govern, rule, or manage; also means to treat or cure (an illness).
Usage: Common in words like 政治 (politics), 治疗 (to treat/cure), and 治理 (to govern/manage)

Definition: Thick, coarse, or rough in texture or quality; the opposite of fine or thin. Can describe physical objects, materials, or behavior that is crude or unrefined.
Usage: Common in phrases like 粗心 (careless), 粗糙 (rough/coarse), 粗线 (thick line)

Definition: Fine, thin, or slender in physical size; also means detailed, careful, or meticulous when describing actions or observations.
Usage: Common in words like 细心 (careful), 仔细 (attentive), and 细节 (details)

Definition: Language or speech; refers to a system of communication or words spoken.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 汉语 (Chinese language), 英语 (English language), and 语言 (language)

Definition: Used to indicate 'the more...the more...' in comparative constructions, or to mean 'to exceed/surpass' or 'to cross over'
Usage: Most commonly seen in the pattern 越...越... (the more...the more...), as in 越来越好 (getting better and better)

Definition: To run or to move quickly on foot. Also used to mean 'to escape' or 'to run away' in certain contexts.
Usage: Common in everyday expressions like 跑步 (to jog/run) and 快跑 (run quickly)

Definition: Must or have to; indicates necessity or obligation. Also means beard or whiskers as a noun.
Usage: Commonly seen in formal written Chinese like 必须 (must) and 须知 (things one should know)

Definition: Question, problem, or topic. Commonly refers to test questions, homework problems, or subjects for discussion.
Usage: Found in words like 问题 (question/problem), 题目 (question/title), and 考题 (exam question)

Definition: To stretch out, extend, or straighten (a body part or object). Commonly used for physical actions like reaching out one's hand or stretching one's body.
Usage: Found in words like 伸手 (stretch out one's hand), 伸腰 (stretch one's back), and 伸展 (stretch/extend)

Definition: Body or physical form; also refers to a style, system, or form of something (like a writing style or political system).
Usage: Common in words like 身体 (shēntǐ - body/health), 具体 (jùtǐ - concrete/specific), 体育 (tǐyù - physical education/sports)

Definition: Beast or wild animal; refers to four-legged mammals, especially those that are wild or untamed.
Usage: Common in words like 野兽 (wild beast), 猛兽 (fierce animal), and 禽兽 (birds and beasts)

Definition: Accurate, precise, or standard; also means to allow or permit. As an adjective, it describes something that is exact or on target.
Usage: Common in words like 准备 (to prepare), 准时 (on time), 标准 (standard), and 批准 (to approve)

Definition: To combine, join together, or fit; also means suitable or in accordance with something.
Usage: Common in words like 合作 (cooperate), 结合 (combine), 合适 (suitable)

Definition: Night or nighttime, referring to the period of darkness between sunset and sunrise.
Usage: Common in words like 夜晚 (night), 今夜 (tonight), and 半夜 (midnight)

Definition: A corridor, hallway, or covered walkway, typically found in traditional Chinese architecture connecting different parts of a building or garden.
Usage: Common in words like 走廊 (hallway) and 画廊 (art gallery)

Definition: To kill or slaughter; to put to death. Can also mean to reduce or weaken in certain contexts.
Usage: Common in words like 杀人 (to kill someone), 杀价 (to bargain down prices), and 自杀 (suicide)

Definition: General, approximate, or rough; often used to indicate a summary or overview of something.
Usage: Most commonly seen in compounds like 大概 (probably/approximately) and 概念 (concept)

Definition: Mother or female parent; also used as a prefix to indicate 'female' or 'maternal' in compound words.
Usage: Common in words like 母亲 (mother), 父母 (parents), 字母 (letter of alphabet)

Definition: Water; the clear liquid essential for life that falls as rain and fills rivers, lakes, and oceans.
Usage: Used in common words like 喝水 (drink water), 水果 (fruit, literally 'water fruit'), and 开水 (boiled water)

Definition: Paper, the material used for writing, printing, or wrapping things.
Usage: Common in words like 纸张 (paper sheets), 报纸 (newspaper), 卫生纸 (toilet paper)

Definition: To jump, leap, or bounce; to skip over something. Also used for actions involving jumping movements like dancing.
Usage: Common in words like 跳舞 (tiàowǔ - to dance), 跳高 (tiàogāo - high jump), 心跳 (xīntiào - heartbeat)

Definition: A measure word used to count the number of times an action is completed from beginning to end.
Usage: Common in phrases like 看一遍 (read once through), 再说一遍 (say it again)

Definition: A formal word meaning 'and' or 'with', used to connect nouns or indicate association between things or people.
Usage: More common in written or formal Chinese; in spoken language, 和 (hé) is preferred

Definition: To buy or purchase something in exchange for money.
Usage: Common in everyday transactions like 买东西 (buy things) or 买票 (buy tickets)

Definition: To fight for, compete for, or strive for something; to argue or dispute over something.
Usage: Common in words like 竞争 (compete), 争论 (argue), 争取 (strive for)

Definition: A suffix meaning 'small thing' or 'young one', commonly used in compound words to indicate something small, young, or a person associated with a particular role or place.
Usage: Found in words like 靓仔 (handsome guy), 仔细 (careful/detailed), and 牛仔 (cowboy)

Definition: False, fake, or artificial; also means vacation or holiday (as a noun)
Usage: Used in words like 假的 (fake), 放假 (have a holiday), 暑假 (summer vacation)

Definition: To rush, charge forward, or dash toward something with force and speed; also means to rinse or flush with water.
Usage: Common in words like 冲进 (rush into), 冲水 (flush water), and 冲茶 (make tea by pouring hot water)

Definition: A suffix meaning 'member', 'personnel', or 'staff member' that is attached to words to indicate a person who performs a specific role or belongs to a group.
Usage: Common in compound words like 服务员 (waiter/waitress), 演员 (actor), 职员 (office worker), 会员 (member)

Definition: City or town; can also refer to city walls or fortifications in classical contexts.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 城市 (city), 长城 (Great Wall), and 进城 (to go into town)

Definition: A fortress, castle, or fortified structure; also commonly used in the word 汉堡 (hànbǎo) meaning hamburger.
Usage: Found in place names and compound words like 城堡 (chéngbǎo - castle) and 汉堡包 (hànbǎobāo - hamburger)

Definition: Few, little, or less in quantity; not enough or lacking. Used to describe a small amount or insufficient number of something.
Usage: Common in phrases like 少一点 (a little less) or 人很少 (very few people). Note: pronounced 'shào' when meaning 'young'

Definition: Tail or end of something; the rear or final part of an object, animal, or sequence.
Usage: Common in words like 尾巴 (tail), 结尾 (ending), and as a measure word for fish

Definition: To wave, swing, or wield something with a sweeping motion; to scatter or disperse.
Usage: Common in words like 挥手 (wave hand), 指挥 (command/direct), and 发挥 (bring into play)

Definition: To take (a photograph or video); to absorb or take in. Also means to act on behalf of or to regulate.
Usage: Most commonly seen in 摄影 (photography) and 拍摄 (to film/shoot)

Definition: Means 'whole', 'entire', or 'complete'; also used as a verb meaning 'to put in order' or 'to fix/arrange'.
Usage: Common in phrases like 整天 (whole day), 整个 (entire/whole), or 整理 (to organize)

Definition: To doubt or suspect; to have uncertainty or questions about something.
Usage: Common in words like 怀疑 (to suspect), 疑问 (question/doubt), and 可疑 (suspicious)

Definition: A component character used in words related to the arm or limbs, rarely used alone.
Usage: Most commonly seen in 胳膊 (gēbo, arm) and 胳肢窝 (gāzhiwō, armpit)

Definition: Arm, specifically the upper arm or shoulder area of the body.
Usage: Most commonly used in the compound word 胳膊 (gēbo) meaning 'arm'

Definition: Road, path, or route; a way to get from one place to another.
Usage: Common in words like 马路 (street), 路上 (on the road), and when giving directions

Definition: To lie down or recline in a horizontal position, typically to rest or sleep.
Usage: Common in phrases like 躺在床上 (lie on the bed) or 躺下 (lie down)

Definition: Quantity, amount, or volume of something; can also mean to measure or estimate.
Usage: Common in words like 数量 (quantity), 质量 (quality), and 重量 (weight)

Definition: Dangerous, risky, or perilous; describes situations or places that pose potential harm or difficulty.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 危险 (wēixiǎn - danger) and 保险 (bǎoxiǎn - insurance)

Definition: Strict, stern, or severe; describes rules, discipline, or attitudes that are rigorous and demanding.
Usage: Common in words like 严格 (strict), 严重 (serious/severe), and 严厉 (stern)

Definition: Measure word for pairs or sets of items (like glasses, gloves, or playing cards); also means 'deputy' or 'vice-' when used as a prefix.
Usage: Used in phrases like 一副眼镜 (a pair of glasses) or 副总统 (vice president)

Definition: Danger or peril; describes something that is dangerous, risky, or in a precarious state.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 危险 (wēixiǎn - dangerous) and 危机 (wēijī - crisis)

Definition: To press down, push down, or apply pressure on something; can also mean to suppress or control.
Usage: Common in words like 压力 (pressure/stress) and 血压 (blood pressure)

Definition: Enough or sufficient; to reach a certain standard or quantity. Can also mean 'quite' or 'rather' when used as an adverb.
Usage: Common in phrases like 够了 (that's enough), 不够 (not enough), or 够好 (good enough)

Definition: A house, room, or building structure with a roof. Refers to an enclosed space where people live or work.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 房屋 (house), 屋子 (room), and 屋顶 (roof)

Definition: Slow; not fast in speed or pace. Can describe movement, actions, or the passage of time.
Usage: Common in phrases like 慢慢走 (walk slowly) and 请说慢一点 (please speak more slowly)

Definition: A fan (the handheld object used for cooling); also used as a measure word for doors and windows.
Usage: Common in words like 扇子 (fan), 电扇 (electric fan), or 一扇门 (a door)

Definition: To protect, guard, or defend someone or something from harm or danger.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 保护 (bǎohù - to protect), 护士 (hùshi - nurse), and 护照 (hùzhào - passport)

Definition: Dog; a common domestic animal kept as a pet or for work purposes.
Usage: Used in everyday conversation and compounds like 小狗 (puppy) or 狗肉 (dog meat)

Definition: A scar or mark left on the skin after a wound or injury has healed.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 疤痕 (bāhén, scar) and 伤疤 (shāngbā, scar from a wound)

Definition: Short or low in height, used to describe people, objects, or buildings that are not tall.
Usage: Commonly used in comparisons like 矮个子 (short person) or to describe furniture and structures

Definition: A covering or canopy made of cloth or other material, such as an awning, tent cover, or boat sail.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 帐篷 (zhàngpeng, tent) and 篷布 (péngbù, tarpaulin)

Definition: Means 'even' when used as an adverb to emphasize something unexpected or extreme; also means 'to link' or 'to connect' as a verb.
Usage: Common in phrases like 连...都/也 (even...also), as in 连我都知道 (even I know)

Definition: Two (people or things); a colloquial way to say 'two' that combines 两 (two) and 个 (measure word).
Usage: Used informally as in 我们俩 (the two of us) or 他俩 (those two). Already includes the measure word, so don't add 个 after it.

Definition: To decide or determine; to make a final judgment or resolution about something.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 决定 (decide), 决心 (determination), and 解决 (solve/resolve)

Definition: A sharp pointed object like a thorn or splinter; as a verb, it means to pierce, stab, or prick something.
Usage: Common in words like 刺痛 (stinging pain), 鱼刺 (fish bone), and 刺绣 (embroidery)

Definition: Single, alone, or odd (as opposed to even or paired). Also means simple or only.
Usage: Common in words like 单人 (single person), 单数 (odd number), 简单 (simple)

Definition: Power, might, or authority that commands respect or fear; prestige or imposing force.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 威力 (power/force), 权威 (authority), and 威胁 (threat/threaten)

Definition: Mother or a young woman; also used as a suffix meaning 'lady' or 'woman'
Usage: Common in words like 姑娘 (gūniang, young lady/girl) and 新娘 (xīnniáng, bride)

Definition: To hold, contain, or allow; also means appearance or facial expression. Commonly used to indicate capacity or tolerance.
Usage: Found in words like 容易 (easy), 内容 (content), 笑容 (smile), and 容纳 (to accommodate)

Definition: A piece of cloth used for wiping or cleaning, such as a handkerchief or towel. Also used as a transliteration component in foreign names and place names.
Usage: Common in compounds like 手帕 (handkerchief), 围巾帕 (scarf), and foreign names like 帕斯卡 (Pascal)

Definition: To wear or put on (accessories, hats, glasses, jewelry, etc. on the head or upper body)
Usage: Used for items worn above the shoulders, like 戴眼镜 (wear glasses), 戴帽子 (wear a hat), 戴手表 (wear a watch)

Definition: Clear, distinct, or neat; also refers to the ancient state of Chu in Chinese history
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 清楚 (qīngchu - clear/understood) and 楚国 (Chǔguó - State of Chu)

Definition: To open (one's eyes). This verb specifically refers to the action of opening the eyes, either from a closed state or opening them wide.
Usage: Most commonly used in phrases like 睁眼 (open eyes) and 睁开眼睛 (open one's eyes)

Definition: Secret or confidential; something that is hidden or not publicly known.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 秘密 (secret), 秘书 (secretary), and 神秘 (mysterious)

Definition: Means 'to cut off' or 'to break'; commonly used to express 'extremely' or 'absolutely' in modern Chinese.
Usage: Often appears in compounds like 绝对 (absolutely), 拒绝 (to refuse), or 绝望 (despair)

Definition: A group or crowd of people, animals, or things gathered together; also used as a measure word for groups.
Usage: Common in words like 群众 (the masses), 人群 (crowd), or 一群人 (a group of people)

Definition: Snake; a long, legless reptile that slithers on the ground.
Usage: Also refers to the Snake in the Chinese zodiac (生肖)

Definition: To reach, arrive at, or attain a goal or destination; to achieve or accomplish something.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 到达 (arrive), 达到 (reach/achieve), and 表达 (express)

Definition: To give (as a gift), to deliver, or to see someone off/escort. This verb is commonly used when giving presents, delivering items, or accompanying someone to a departure point.
Usage: Used in phrases like 送礼物 (give a gift), 送货 (deliver goods), 送朋友 (see a friend off)

Definition: A measure word for items, clauses, or categories in a list or set; also means 'item' or 'term' as a noun.
Usage: Commonly used in formal contexts like 三项任务 (three tasks) or 项目 (project)

Definition: To wear or carry (accessories, ornaments, or items) on one's body; to admire or respect someone deeply
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 佩戴 (to wear accessories), 钦佩 (to admire), and 佩服 (to respect/admire)

Definition: Original, former, or primary; refers to the initial or unchanged state of something. Also means source or origin.
Usage: Common in words like 原来 (originally), 原因 (reason/cause), 原本 (originally), and 草原 (grassland/prairie)

Definition: Mute or unable to speak; also means hoarse or voiceless. Can describe a person who cannot speak or a voice that has lost its sound.
Usage: Common in words like 哑巴 (mute person) and 哑铃 (dumbbell)

Definition: Bad, broken, or spoiled; describes something of poor quality, not functioning properly, or morally wrong.
Usage: Common in phrases like 坏人 (bad person), 坏了 (broken/spoiled)

Definition: A measure word (classifier) used for large, immovable objects like mountains, buildings, bridges, and statues; also means 'seat' or 'base' as a noun.
Usage: Common in phrases like 一座山 (a mountain), 一座桥 (a bridge), 座位 (seat)

Definition: To hold, grasp, or maintain something; to support or sustain a position or state over time.
Usage: Common in words like 保持 (to maintain), 持续 (to continue), and 支持 (to support)

Definition: A measure word (classifier) used for flowers and clouds. It can also mean a flower or blossom as a noun.
Usage: Used in phrases like 一朵花 (one flower) or 一朵云 (one cloud)

Definition: Pine tree; also means loose, slack, or relaxed (as an adjective or verb meaning to loosen)
Usage: Common in words like 松树 (pine tree), 轻松 (relaxed), and 松开 (to loosen/release)

Definition: To excite, stimulate, or arouse strong emotions or reactions; can also mean intense or radical.
Usage: Commonly found in words like 激动 (excited), 激烈 (intense), and 刺激 (stimulate)

Definition: To love; a deep affection or strong liking for someone or something. Can refer to romantic love, familial love, or fondness for activities and things.
Usage: Used in phrases like 我爱你 (I love you), 爱好 (hobby, interest), 爱吃 (love to eat)

Definition: Father or dad; an informal, affectionate term for one's male parent.
Usage: Most commonly used in 爸爸 (bàba, dad/daddy) or combined with 妈 in 爸妈 (bàmā, parents)

Definition: Crazy, insane, or mad; describes someone or something that is wild, out of control, or mentally unstable.
Usage: Commonly used in expressions like 疯了 (gone crazy) or 发疯 (to go mad)

Definition: A unit of time meaning 'second', as in 1/60th of a minute. Also used colloquially to mean 'instant' or 'moment'.
Usage: Common in time expressions like 三十秒 (30 seconds) or 等一秒 (wait a second)

Definition: To continue or carry on; to succeed or follow after something or someone.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 继续 (jìxù, to continue) and 继承 (jìchéng, to inherit)

Definition: To endure, withstand, or be resistant to something; to be patient or durable.
Usage: Commonly used in compound words like 耐心 (patience), 忍耐 (endurance), and 耐用 (durable)

Definition: Medicine or medication; any substance used to treat illness or disease.
Usage: Common in phrases like 吃药 (take medicine) and 中药 (Chinese medicine)

Definition: To wake up or regain consciousness; to become sober or alert from sleep, drunkenness, or confusion.
Usage: Common in phrases like 醒来 (to wake up), 清醒 (sober/clear-headed), 提醒 (to remind)

Definition: A prefix used before names, kinship terms, or place names to show familiarity or affection, similar to adding a nickname.
Usage: Common in names like 阿姨 (auntie), 阿哥 (older brother), or nicknames like 阿明 (A-Ming)

Definition: To remove, get rid of, or eliminate; also means 'except' or 'besides' when used in certain phrases. In mathematics, it means 'to divide'.
Usage: Common in phrases like 除了 (except for), 除非 (unless), and mathematical expressions

Definition: Short name for Shandong Province in eastern China; also means rude, rough, or rash as an adjective.
Usage: Commonly seen in place names, historical references (like 鲁迅 Lu Xun), and as a literary term for crude behavior

Definition: Foolish, silly, or stupid; describes someone who lacks intelligence or acts in a naive way.
Usage: Commonly used in everyday speech to describe silly behavior or foolish people, like 傻瓜 (fool) or 别傻了 (don't be silly)

Definition: To emit, give off, or send out (steam, smoke, sparks); to risk or brave (danger, cold, etc.)
Usage: Common in phrases like 冒烟 (to emit smoke) and 冒险 (to take risks/adventure)

Definition: To roar, bellow, or shout loudly; describes the loud sound made by animals (like lions or tigers) or people yelling angrily.
Usage: Commonly used for animal roars (狮子吼 - lion's roar) or when someone shouts in anger

Definition: To drink (liquids such as water, tea, coffee, or alcohol)
Usage: Common in everyday phrases like 喝水 (drink water), 喝茶 (drink tea), 喝酒 (drink alcohol)

Definition: To prepare or get ready for something; to have in reserve or keep on hand for future use.
Usage: Common in words like 准备 (zhǔnbèi - to prepare), 备用 (bèiyòng - reserve/backup), and 设备 (shèbèi - equipment)

Definition: Anger, indignation, or resentment; describes feelings of strong displeasure or outrage at perceived injustice or wrongdoing.
Usage: Commonly appears in compound words like 愤怒 (fènnù - angry), 气愤 (qìfèn - indignant), and 义愤 (yìfèn - righteous indignation)

Definition: To hang or suspend something; also means to hang up a phone call or to register (at a hospital).
Usage: Common in phrases like 挂电话 (hang up the phone), 挂号 (register/make an appointment), 挂在墙上 (hang on the wall)

Definition: To place, put, or arrange something in a particular position; to display or set out items.
Usage: Common in phrases like 摆桌子 (set the table), 摆放 (arrange/display), or 摆摊 (set up a street stall)

Definition: To touch or feel something with your hands; to stroke or grope for something.
Usage: Common in phrases like 摸一摸 (touch and feel) or 摸黑 (grope in the dark)

Definition: Clothing or garments; also means to serve, obey, or submit to someone or something.
Usage: Common in words like 衣服 (yīfu - clothes), 服务 (fúwù - to serve/service), and 说服 (shuōfú - to persuade)

Definition: Means 'extremely' or 'utmost/extreme' when used as an adverb or adjective. It intensifies the meaning of adjectives and verbs to express the highest degree.
Usage: Commonly used in phrases like 极好 (extremely good), 极其 (extremely), 北极 (North Pole - extreme north)

Definition: Stone or rock; refers to hard, solid mineral material found in nature.
Usage: Common in words like 石头 (stone), 岩石 (rock), and 宝石 (gemstone)

Definition: To forbid, prohibit, or ban something. Used to indicate that an action or behavior is not allowed.
Usage: Commonly seen in signs like 禁止 (jìnzhǐ - forbidden) and 严禁 (yánjìn - strictly prohibited)

Definition: The back (of the body or an object); as a verb, it means to carry on one's back or to recite from memory.
Usage: Common in words like 背包 (backpack), 后背 (back of body), and 背书 (recite a text)

Definition: Wrong, incorrect, or mistaken; also used as a noun meaning 'mistake' or 'error'.
Usage: Common in phrases like 错了 (made a mistake), 不错 (not bad/pretty good), and 你错了 (you're wrong)

Definition: Dew or moisture that forms on surfaces; also means to reveal, show, or expose something that was hidden.
Usage: As a noun in words like 露水 (dew), or as a verb in phrases like 露出 (to reveal/show)

Definition: To dominate, bully, or rule by force; a tyrant or hegemon who exercises power through strength rather than righteousness.
Usage: Common in words like 霸道 (domineering), 恶霸 (local tyrant), and 霸占 (to forcibly occupy)

Definition: A measure word for meals or occurrences of actions like beatings or scoldings; also means 'to pause' or 'suddenly' as a verb/adverb.
Usage: Most commonly used with meals (一顿饭 - one meal) or to count instances of actions (打了一顿 - gave a beating)

Definition: Nose, the organ used for breathing and smelling on the face.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 鼻子 (bízi, nose) and 鼻涕 (bítì, nasal mucus/snot)

Definition: A measure word used for portions, copies, or servings of things that can be divided into parts. Also means 'share' or 'portion' as a noun.
Usage: Common in phrases like 一份报纸 (one copy of a newspaper), 两份饭 (two servings of food), or 身份 (identity, status)

Definition: Elder brother or older male relative of the same generation. Also used as a respectful form of address between male friends or peers.
Usage: Common in words like 兄弟 (brothers), 大兄 (eldest brother), or as a polite term 老兄 (buddy, pal)

Definition: Noon or midday, referring to the time around 12:00 PM. Also used to indicate the seventh of the twelve Earthly Branches in traditional Chinese timekeeping.
Usage: Most commonly seen in words like 中午 (zhōngwǔ - noon), 上午 (shàngwǔ - morning/AM), and 下午 (xiàwǔ - afternoon/PM)

Definition: Taste or flavor; can also refer to smell or odor. Used to describe the sensory quality of food, drinks, or other substances.
Usage: Common in words like 味道 (taste/flavor), 美味 (delicious), and 气味 (smell/odor)

Definition: Younger brother; can also refer to a male who is younger in a familial or social relationship
Usage: Common in family terms like 弟弟 (younger brother) and 表弟 (younger male cousin)

Definition: To read aloud or recite; to think of, miss, or remember someone or something with feeling
Usage: Common in words like 想念 (to miss someone), 念书 (to study/read), and 纪念 (to commemorate)

Definition: An ancient Chinese weapon similar to a dagger-axe or halberd; also used as a radical in Chinese characters related to weapons or warfare.
Usage: Rarely used alone in modern Chinese, but appears in compounds like 戈壁 (Gobi Desert) and as a character component

Definition: To pat, slap, or hit with the palm of the hand; also means to take (a photo) or shoot (a film).
Usage: Common in phrases like 拍照 (take a photo), 拍电影 (make a movie), or 拍手 (clap hands)

Definition: To change, exchange, or swap one thing for another. Can refer to changing clothes, exchanging money, or replacing something.
Usage: Common in phrases like 换钱 (exchange money), 换衣服 (change clothes), 换工作 (change jobs)

Definition: To pull out, take out, or fish out something from inside a pocket, bag, or container using one's hand.
Usage: Commonly used in phrases like 掏钱 (take out money) or 掏口袋 (reach into one's pocket)

Definition: Dark or dim, lacking light; can also mean hidden, secret, or unclear.
Usage: Common in words like 黑暗 (darkness), 暗示 (hint/imply), and 明暗 (light and dark)

Definition: A cabinet, cupboard, or counter used for storage or display. Commonly refers to furniture pieces or service counters in shops and offices.
Usage: Found in words like 柜子 (cabinet), 衣柜 (wardrobe), 书柜 (bookshelf), and 柜台 (counter/checkout)

Definition: Fierce, violent, or vigorous; describes something done with great force or intensity.
Usage: Commonly used to describe animals (猛兽 fierce beast), actions (猛烈 violent/intense), or sudden forceful movements

Definition: Amber (fossilized tree resin); also used as a component in compound words related to precious stones or translucent materials.
Usage: Most commonly seen in 琥珀 (hǔpò - amber) and in transliterated foreign names like 珀斯 (Pòsī - Perth)

Definition: To stand or to establish; can mean to stand upright physically or to set up/found something like an organization or rule.
Usage: Common in words like 站立 (to stand), 建立 (to establish), 独立 (independent)

Definition: A section, segment, or division of something; also refers to festivals or holidays, and is used as a measure word for class periods or sections.
Usage: Common in words like 节日 (festival), 季节 (season), 一节课 (one class period)

Definition: To install, load, or pack something; also means to pretend or feign. As a noun, it refers to clothing, costume, or装备 (equipment).
Usage: Common in words like 安装 (install), 装饰 (decorate), 服装 (clothing), and 假装 (pretend)

Definition: To untie, loosen, or solve; to understand or explain something. Commonly used for solving problems, understanding concepts, or releasing/undoing physical or abstract things.
Usage: Found in words like 理解 (understand), 解决 (solve/resolve), 解释 (explain)

Definition: To separate, partition, or be apart from something; to have a barrier or distance between things.
Usage: Common in words like 隔壁 (next door), 隔开 (to separate), and 相隔 (to be apart by a distance)

Definition: Happy, joyful, or cheerful; also means to enjoy or take pleasure in something.
Usage: Common in words like 快乐 (kuàilè - happy) and 娱乐 (yúlè - entertainment). Note: also pronounced yuè (music)

Definition: To hand over, deliver, or submit something; to intersect or cross. Also means to make friends or have social interactions.
Usage: Common in words like 交朋友 (make friends), 交作业 (hand in homework), 交通 (traffic/transportation)

Definition: To hit, strike, or attack something with force. Can refer to physical strikes or figurative attacks.
Usage: Common in words like 攻击 (attack), 打击 (strike), and 击败 (defeat)

Definition: Brave, courageous, or bold. Describes someone who has the courage to face danger or difficulty without fear.
Usage: Often used in words like 勇敢 (yǒnggǎn - brave) and 勇气 (yǒngqì - courage)

Definition: An adverb expressing contrast or unexpectedness, meaning 'however', 'yet', or 'but'. It indicates that the following clause contradicts or contrasts with what was previously stated or expected.
Usage: Typically placed before the verb in the second clause, as in 他很累，却还在工作 (He's very tired, yet he's still working)

Definition: Kitchen or a place where food is prepared and cooked. Also refers to a cook or chef.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 厨房 (kitchen) and 厨师 (chef)

Definition: Ancient or old, referring to things from long ago or the distant past. Often contrasted with 今 (jīn, modern/present).
Usage: Common in words like 古代 (ancient times), 古老 (ancient/age-old), and 古典 (classical)

Definition: To bite with the teeth; to snap at or clench between the teeth.
Usage: Used for animals or people biting, as in 狗咬人 (dog bites person) or 咬一口 (take a bite)

Definition: To murmur, mutter, or speak in a low voice; to talk quietly or indistinctly.
Usage: Often used in literary or poetic contexts, commonly seen in compounds like 喃哝 (nán nóng, to murmur)

Definition: To search for, to look for, or to seek something or someone.
Usage: Common in words like 寻找 (xúnzhǎo - to search for) and 寻求 (xúnqiú - to seek)

Definition: Hat or cap; a head covering worn for protection, warmth, or fashion.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 帽子 (màozi - hat/cap), 草帽 (cǎomào - straw hat), 毛线帽 (máoxiànmào - knit cap)

Definition: To be annoyed, irritated, or angry about something. Expresses feelings of vexation or frustration.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 恼火 (annoyed), 烦恼 (vexed/troubled), and 苦恼 (distressed)

Definition: To hold or carry in one's arms; to embrace or hug someone or something.
Usage: Common in expressions like 拥抱 (to hug), 抱歉 (sorry, literally 'hold regret'), and 抱孩子 (to hold a child)

Definition: To carry on a shoulder pole; to bear or take on (responsibility, burden, or worry)
Usage: Common in words like 担心 (to worry) and 担任 (to assume a position)

Definition: To squeeze, push, or crowd together; to force one's way into a tight space.
Usage: Commonly used to describe crowded situations like 挤公交 (squeeze onto a bus) or 人很挤 (very crowded with people)

Definition: To fall, drop, or lose something; also used as a verb complement indicating completion or removal of something.
Usage: Common in phrases like 掉了 (dropped/fell), 扔掉 (throw away), 忘掉 (forget completely)

Definition: To fall down or to throw something down forcefully; to break by dropping or smashing.
Usage: Common in phrases like 摔倒 (to fall down), 摔跤 (to wrestle/fall), or 摔坏了 (broke it by dropping)

Definition: Number or quantity; also means to count or enumerate things.
Usage: Common in words like 数学 (mathematics), 人数 (number of people), and as a verb meaning 'to count'

Definition: To knock, tap, or strike something with a hard object or one's hand. Commonly used for knocking on doors, typing on keyboards, or hitting objects to make a sound.
Usage: Used in phrases like 敲门 (knock on a door), 敲键盘 (type on a keyboard)

Definition: Tooth; the hard, white structures in the mouth used for biting and chewing food.
Usage: Common in words like 牙齿 (teeth), 刷牙 (brush teeth), 牙医 (dentist)

Definition: Wrinkled, creased, or crumpled; describes the appearance of fabric, skin, or paper that has folds or lines.
Usage: Commonly used in 皱纹 (wrinkles on skin) and 皱眉 (to frown, literally 'wrinkle eyebrows')

Definition: A writing instrument such as a pen, pencil, or brush. Also used as a measure word for sums of money, strokes in writing, or deals/transactions.
Usage: Common in words like 铅笔 (pencil), 毛笔 (brush pen), 钢笔 (fountain pen), and phrases like 一笔钱 (a sum of money)

Definition: Department or faculty (in a university or organization); also means to tie, fasten, or connect
Usage: Common in academic contexts like 中文系 (Chinese department) or as a verb meaning to fasten like 系鞋带 (tie shoelaces)

Definition: To continue, resume, or extend something that was previously started or is about to end.
Usage: Common in words like 继续 (jìxù, to continue), 连续 (liánxù, continuous), and 手续 (shǒuxù, procedures)

Definition: Fat, plump, or overweight; describes someone or something with excess body weight or thickness.
Usage: Commonly used to describe people's body types, as in 他很胖 (he is fat) or 胖子 (fat person)

Definition: Upper arm or shoulder; also refers to the wing of a bird or insect.
Usage: Most commonly seen in compounds like 肩膀 (shoulder), 臂膀 (arm), and 翅膀 (wing)

Definition: Grass or herbaceous plants; can also refer to straw or hay.
Usage: Common in words like 草地 (grassland) and 草莓 (strawberry)

Definition: Insect, bug, or worm; a general term for small crawling or flying creatures.
Usage: Common in compound words like 昆虫 (kūnchóng, insect) and 虫子 (chóngzi, bug/worm)

Definition: A traditional Chinese long robe or gown that extends to the ankles or feet, typically worn in ancient or formal contexts.
Usage: Commonly seen in compounds like 旗袍 (qipao/cheongsam) or 长袍 (long robe)

Definition: To try, to test, or to attempt something. Often used when experimenting with something new or taking an examination.
Usage: Common in words like 试试 (try it), 考试 (exam/test), 试验 (experiment)

Definition: Interest, fun, or amusement; refers to something that is interesting or entertaining.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 有趣 (interesting/fun) and 兴趣 (interest/hobby)

Definition: To look after, take care of, or attend to something; also means to turn around and look back.
Usage: Common in words like 照顾 (zhàogù - to take care of) and 顾客 (gùkè - customer/client)

Definition: A formal literary word meaning 'this' or 'here/now', used to refer to the present time or matter at hand.
Usage: Commonly seen in formal written Chinese, especially in phrases like 兹有 (hereby) or 特此 (hereby/herewith)

Definition: To make, manufacture, or create; to establish a system or regulation. Also means 'system' or '制度' when used as a noun.
Usage: Common in words like 制作 (to make/produce), 制度 (system), 控制 (to control)

Definition: To help or assist someone; to aid in accomplishing something.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 帮助 (bāngzhù - to help) and 助理 (zhùlǐ - assistant)

Definition: Guest, visitor, or customer. Refers to someone who comes to a place, whether as a social guest or a paying customer.
Usage: Common in words like 客人 (guest), 顾客 (customer), 游客 (tourist)

Definition: A traditional Chinese unit of length equal to approximately one-third of a meter (about 33 cm); also means ruler (the measuring tool).
Usage: Common in measurements like 三尺 (three chi) or 尺子 (ruler)

Definition: To use up completely, to exhaust, or to reach the limit of something; also means 'to the greatest extent' or 'as much as possible'
Usage: Common in phrases like 尽力 (do one's best), 尽管 (even though), and 尽快 (as soon as possible)

Definition: Courtyard or front yard of a house; also refers to a court of law in formal contexts.
Usage: Common in words like 家庭 (family), 法庭 (court of law), and 庭院 (courtyard)

Definition: To endure, tolerate, or bear something difficult or unpleasant; to hold back or restrain oneself from doing something.
Usage: Common in expressions like 忍不住 (can't help but) and 忍耐 (patience, endurance)

Definition: To forget or fail to remember something. Can refer to forgetting information, objects, or failing to do something.
Usage: Common in phrases like 忘记 (wàngjì - to forget) and 忘了 (wàngle - forgot)

Definition: Quiet, silent, or done secretly without making noise or attracting attention.
Usage: Most commonly seen in compounds like 悄悄 (quietly, secretly) as in 悄悄地走 (to walk quietly)

Definition: To rush at, pounce on, or throw oneself toward something; to flap or flutter.
Usage: Common in words like 扑克 (poker cards) and phrases describing sudden forward movements like 扑过去 (pounce over)

Definition: To twist, turn, or wrench something by rotating or bending it. Can also mean to sprain (a body part) or to turn one's body.
Usage: Common in phrases like 扭伤 (to sprain), 扭头 (to turn one's head), and 扭腰 (to twist one's waist)

Definition: To throw, toss, or cast something; also means to invest (money) or to submit/deliver something.
Usage: Common in words like 投资 (invest), 投票 (vote/cast a ballot), 投球 (throw a ball)

Definition: To cover with one's hand or hands, often to protect, keep warm, or conceal something.
Usage: Commonly used in phrases like 捂住嘴 (cover one's mouth) or 捂耳朵 (cover one's ears)

Definition: A measure word (classifier) used for long, thin objects like pens, pencils, cigarettes, songs, or military units. Also means 'to support' or 'branch' as a verb/noun.
Usage: Common in phrases like 一支笔 (one pen), 两支歌 (two songs), or 支持 (to support)

Definition: Means 'old', 'former', 'reason', or 'therefore/hence'. Most commonly used to indicate cause/reason or to mean 'old/past' in formal contexts.
Usage: Found in words like 故事 (story), 故乡 (hometown), and classical phrases like 因此之故 (for this reason)

Definition: To fight, struggle against, or compete with someone or something. Also means a traditional Chinese unit of dry measure for grain.
Usage: Common in words like 战斗 (zhàndòu - to fight/battle) and 斗争 (dòuzhēng - to struggle)

Definition: Wood or tree; refers to timber, wooden materials, or trees in general.
Usage: Common in compound words like 木头 (wood/log) and 树木 (trees); also one of the Five Elements in Chinese philosophy

Definition: Not yet; indicates that something has not happened or been done up to the present time. Often used in formal or written Chinese as a negative prefix meaning 'not' or 'un-'.
Usage: Common in words like 未来 (future, literally 'not yet come') and 未必 (not necessarily)

Definition: Indicates the source, cause, or agent of an action, meaning 'by', 'from', or 'due to'. Also means 'to follow' or 'to be up to someone' in certain contexts.
Usage: Commonly used in phrases like 由于 (due to), 由...来 (to be done by...), and 由你决定 (up to you to decide)

Definition: To touch, bump into, or collide with something physically; also means to meet or run into someone by chance.
Usage: Common in phrases like 碰到 (to run into/encounter) and 碰见 (to meet by chance)

Definition: To answer or reply to a question or statement; to respond.
Usage: Common in words like 回答 (huídá - to answer) and 答案 (dá'àn - answer/solution)

Definition: To calculate, count, or compute; also means to consider or regard as something, or to count as valid.
Usage: Common in expressions like 算了 (forget it), 打算 (to plan), and 计算 (to calculate)

Definition: Paste or glue (noun); to paste or stick something together (verb). Also means muddled, confused, or burnt/scorched when describing food.
Usage: Common in words like 糊涂 (confused), 浆糊 (paste), and 糊弄 (to deceive/muddle through)

Definition: Cake or pastry; a general term for sweet or savory baked or steamed food made from flour, rice, or other grains.
Usage: Common in words like 蛋糕 (dàngāo, cake), 年糕 (niángāo, rice cake), and 糕点 (gāodiǎn, pastries)

Definition: Bad, terrible, or in a mess; describes something that has gone wrong or is of poor quality.
Usage: Commonly used in expressions like 糟糕 (zāogāo - terrible/awful) and 糟了 (zāole - oh no!)

Definition: A gap, crack, or seam between two surfaces or objects; also means to sew or stitch (when pronounced feng2).
Usage: Common in words like 裂缝 (crack), 缝隙 (gap), or 门缝 (door crack)

Definition: To place, put, or set something in a position; to install or establish something.
Usage: Commonly seen in compounds like 位置 (position), 放置 (to place), 设置 (to set up), and 布置 (to arrange)

Definition: To turn over, flip, or overturn something; also means to translate from one language to another.
Usage: Common in words like 翻译 (translate), 翻书 (flip through a book), 翻倍 (double/multiply)

Definition: Shoulder, the part of the body between the neck and upper arm.
Usage: Common in words like 肩膀 (shoulder), 肩负 (to shoulder responsibility)

Definition: Fee, cost, or expense; can also be used as a verb meaning to spend or consume (money, time, effort).
Usage: Common in words like 学费 (tuition), 费用 (expenses), 浪费 (to waste)

Definition: Late or tardy; delayed in time. Describes being behind schedule or arriving after the expected time.
Usage: Common in phrases like 迟到 (be late), 推迟 (postpone), 迟早 (sooner or later)

Definition: Silk or thread; also refers to anything thin and thread-like, or a tiny bit/trace of something.
Usage: Common in words like 丝绸 (silk fabric), 一丝 (a trace of), and 粉丝 (vermicelli noodles; fans)

Definition: Indicates that something happens immediately after or as soon as another action occurs; can also mean 'then' or 'in that case' to show a logical consequence.
Usage: Commonly used in patterns like 一...便... (as soon as...then...) or 就便 structures to connect sequential actions

Definition: Drama, play, or show; refers to theatrical performances, TV series, or any form of dramatic entertainment.
Usage: Common in words like 电视剧 (TV series), 话剧 (stage play), 戏剧 (drama/theater)

Definition: Hurried or hasty; describes doing something in a rushed manner without enough time.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the word 匆忙 (cōngmáng, hurried) or 匆匆 (cōngcōng, hastily)

Definition: Describes someone or something as dull, slow-witted, or blank in expression; also means to stay or remain in a place.
Usage: Common in words like 发呆 (to stare blankly/daydream) and 呆板 (rigid, inflexible)

Definition: A modal particle used at the end of sentences to indicate a strong tone, exclamation, or to soften a statement. Also used to describe a grinning mouth or to show teeth.
Usage: Common in colloquial speech, especially in northern dialects; also appears in 嘴咧咧 (grinning widely)

Definition: Country or nation; state. One of the most fundamental characters for referring to countries and national concepts.
Usage: Used in words like 中国 (China), 美国 (America), 国家 (country/nation)

Definition: Holy, sacred, or sage; refers to something divine or a person of exceptional wisdom and virtue.
Usage: Common in words like 圣诞节 (Christmas, literally 'holy birth festival') and 圣人 (sage/saint)

Definition: To repeat, return, or restore; also means complex or compound. Commonly used as a prefix meaning 're-' (again) or to indicate complexity.
Usage: Found in words like 复习 (to review), 复杂 (complex), 恢复 (to recover)

Definition: A demon, monster, or evil spirit; can also describe something bewitching or seductive in an eerie way.
Usage: Common in words like 妖怪 (monster), 妖精 (fairy/demon), and 妖艳 (bewitchingly beautiful)

Definition: A traditional Chinese unit of length equal to approximately 3.33 centimeters or about 1.3 inches; also means 'inch' in modern usage.
Usage: Commonly used in measurements, idioms like 寸步难行 (unable to move a single step), and as a radical in characters related to measurement

Definition: A shop or store; a place where goods or services are sold.
Usage: Common in words like 商店 (shop), 书店 (bookstore), 饭店 (restaurant/hotel)

Definition: Busy or occupied with tasks and activities. Describes being engaged with work or having little free time.
Usage: Common in phrases like 很忙 (very busy) or 忙什么 (busy with what)

Definition: To support or help someone by holding them up, typically with one's hand; to assist someone who is weak, elderly, or unsteady.
Usage: Common in phrases like 扶老人 (help an elderly person) or 扶着墙 (lean against the wall for support)

Definition: To collide, bump into, or crash into something or someone. Can refer to physical impacts like car accidents or accidentally running into people.
Usage: Common in phrases like 撞车 (car crash) and 撞见 (bump into/encounter someone)

Definition: To shine or illuminate; to take a photograph or picture. Also commonly used to mean 'according to' or 'in accordance with' when used as a preposition.
Usage: Found in words like 照片 (photograph), 照相 (to take a photo), and 按照 (according to)

Definition: To ache or hurt; to feel pain or soreness in a part of the body. Can also mean to love dearly or dote on someone.
Usage: Common in expressions like 头疼 (headache), 肚子疼 (stomachache), or 疼爱 (to love dearly)

Definition: Eyebrow; the strip of hair growing above the eye.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 眉毛 (eyebrow) and expressions about facial features or emotions

Definition: To receive, accept, or take in; to pay (taxes or fees). Also means to include or incorporate something.
Usage: Common in words like 接纳 (to accept), 纳税 (to pay taxes), and 采纳 (to adopt suggestions)

Definition: End or final; indicates the conclusion or last part of something.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 终于 (finally), 最终 (ultimately), and 始终 (from beginning to end)

Definition: To tie, knot, or bind together; to form or conclude something. Also means a knot or node as a noun.
Usage: Common in words like 结束 (to end), 结果 (result), 结婚 (to marry), and 打结 (to tie a knot)

Definition: Sheep or goat; a common domesticated animal in Chinese culture and agriculture.
Usage: Used in compound words like 山羊 (goat), 绵羊 (sheep), and appears in the Chinese zodiac

Definition: Feather or plume; also refers to wings of birds. Used as a radical in characters related to birds and flight.
Usage: Common in words like 羽毛 (feather), 羽绒 (down feathers), and 羽毛球 (badminton)

Definition: A measure word for shares/stocks in business, or for things in strands, flows, or groups. Also means thigh or a section/portion of something.
Usage: Common in financial contexts like 股票 (stocks/shares) and as a classifier like 一股力量 (a force/stream of power)

Definition: A type of fern or rose plant; commonly refers to the Chinese rose or osmunda fern.
Usage: Primarily used in names (especially female names like 薇薇) and classical/literary contexts

Definition: To win, to gain victory, or to beat an opponent in a competition or game.
Usage: Commonly used in sports, games, and competitive contexts, as in 赢了 (won) or 赢钱 (win money)

Definition: Silver, the precious metal; also refers to money or currency in general.
Usage: Common in words like 银行 (bank), 银色 (silver color), and 金银 (gold and silver)

Definition: Yin (the feminine, dark, or negative principle in Chinese philosophy); also means shade, cloudy, or overcast weather.
Usage: Common in 阴天 (cloudy day), 阴阳 (yin and yang), and 树阴 (shade of a tree)

Definition: To follow, go along with, or accompany; also means 'according to' or 'as one pleases' when indicating flexibility or casualness.
Usage: Common in phrases like 随便 (casual/whatever), 随时 (at any time), and 跟随 (to follow)

Definition: Forehead (the part of the face above the eyebrows); also means 'amount' or 'quota' in formal contexts
Usage: As body part: 额头 (forehead); as amount: 金额 (sum of money), 名额 (quota of people)

Definition: Dragon, a mythical creature that is a powerful symbol in Chinese culture representing power, strength, and good fortune.
Usage: Common in names, idioms, and cultural expressions like 龙年 (Year of the Dragon)

Definition: To imitate, copy, or model after something; to follow a pattern or example.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 仿造 (to imitate/counterfeit) and 模仿 (to imitate/mimic)

Definition: Buddha; Buddhist. Refers to the Buddha, Buddhism, or things related to Buddhist religion and philosophy.
Usage: Common in words like 佛教 (Buddhism), 佛像 (Buddha statue), 拜佛 (worship Buddha)

Definition: To dislike, detest, or be tired of something; to feel disgust or aversion toward something
Usage: Commonly used in words like 厌恶 (to detest), 厌烦 (to be fed up with), and 讨厌 (to dislike/annoying)

Definition: Lucky, auspicious, or fortunate; represents good fortune and positive outcomes.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 吉祥 (auspicious), names, and traditional expressions about good luck

Definition: A modal particle used at the end of sentences to express surprise, emphasis, or to soften a statement or question, making it sound more friendly or casual.
Usage: Common in exclamations like 好呀! (Great!) or questions like 你去哪儿呀? (Where are you going?)

Definition: Product, goods, or article; also means quality, grade, or character. Can be used as a verb meaning to taste or sample carefully.
Usage: Common in words like 产品 (product), 食品 (food products), 品质 (quality), and 品尝 (to taste)

Definition: To cry or weep, expressing sadness, pain, or strong emotion through tears and sounds.
Usage: Common in everyday expressions like 哭了 (cried) or 别哭 (don't cry)

Definition: Firm, strong, or solid; describes something that is hard, sturdy, or unyielding in physical or abstract sense.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 坚强 (strong/resilient), 坚持 (persist), and 坚固 (sturdy)

Definition: To exert oneself vigorously; to strive or work hard with great effort and enthusiasm.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 奋斗 (struggle/strive) and 兴奋 (excited)

Definition: Father's sister (paternal aunt); also used as a respectful term for young women or in compound words relating to female family members.
Usage: Common in family terms like 姑姑 (gūgu, aunt), 姑娘 (gūniang, young woman/girl)

Definition: Refers to twins or being born as a twin. This character is most commonly seen in the compound word 孪生 (luánshēng), meaning twin or twins.
Usage: Primarily used in 孪生兄弟 (twin brothers) or 孪生姐妹 (twin sisters)

Definition: To stay overnight or lodge; also refers to something long-standing or from a previous night/time.
Usage: Common in words like 宿舍 (dormitory), 住宿 (accommodation), and 宿敌 (old enemy)

Definition: A measure word for age, meaning 'years old'. It is used after a number to indicate someone's age.
Usage: Used in phrases like 我五岁 (I am five years old) or 他二十岁 (He is twenty years old)

Definition: Account or bill; also refers to a curtain or tent (simplified form). Most commonly used in financial contexts to mean accounts, records, or bills.
Usage: Found in words like 账单 (bill), 账户 (account), 帐篷 (tent)

Definition: Anger or rage; to be angry or furious. Describes intense feelings of displeasure or wrath.
Usage: Common in words like 愤怒 (angry), 发怒 (to get angry), and 怒火 (fury)

Definition: Pleasant, happy, or joyful; describes a feeling of contentment and cheerfulness.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the word 愉快 (yúkuài) meaning 'pleasant' or 'delightful'

Definition: Household, family, or door; also refers to an account (like a bank account) or registered user.
Usage: Common in words like 户口 (household registration), 用户 (user), 账户 (account)

Definition: To report, announce, or inform; also means newspaper or a written report.
Usage: Common in words like 报纸 (newspaper), 报告 (report), and 报名 (to sign up/register)

Definition: To piece together, join, or spell out by combining parts or components. Also means to risk everything or go all out in an effort.
Usage: Common in words like 拼音 (pinyin, phonetic spelling), 拼图 (jigsaw puzzle), and 拼命 (to risk one's life, to do something desperately)

Definition: To do, make, or engage in something; a versatile colloquial verb meaning to work on, handle, or deal with something.
Usage: Common in everyday speech like 搞什么 (what are you doing?), 搞定 (to get something done), or 搞活动 (to organize an activity)

Definition: Spot, speckle, or mark on a surface; refers to patches or blotches of different colors or textures.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 斑点 (spots/speckles), 斑马 (zebra), and 雀斑 (freckles)
