Definition: To carry out, implement, or put into practice; to bestow or grant something to others.
Usage: Common in formal contexts like 施工 (construction work), 施加 (to exert), 实施 (to implement), and 施舍 (to give alms)

Definition: A mark, sign, or label; also means standard or target. Commonly used in compound words related to marking, labeling, or setting standards.
Usage: Found in words like 标准 (standard), 目标 (goal/target), 商标 (trademark)

Definition: A hole, cave, or hollow opening in something. Can refer to natural caves, holes in objects, or gaps.
Usage: Common in words like 山洞 (cave), 洞口 (cave entrance), 破洞 (a hole/tear)

Definition: Muddy, turbid, or unclear (describing water or liquids); also means 'whole' or 'completely' in certain contexts.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 浑浊 (húnzhuó - muddy/turbid) and 浑身 (húnshēn - whole body)

Definition: To mix or blend things together; to muddle through or get by without real effort or skill
Usage: Common in words like 混合 (to mix), 混乱 (chaotic), and colloquial expressions like 混日子 (to drift through life)

Definition: Excessive, indiscriminate, or overflowing; to abuse or misuse something without proper control or standards.
Usage: Common in words like 泛滥 (to flood/overflow), 滥用 (to abuse/misuse)

Definition: Lacquer or paint; a coating substance used to protect or decorate surfaces, traditionally made from tree sap.
Usage: Common in compounds like 油漆 (yóuqī - paint) and 漆黑 (qīhēi - pitch-black)

Definition: Intense, fierce, or strong; describes something with great force or severity. Often used to describe heat, flames, emotions, or character traits.
Usage: Common in words like 热烈 (enthusiastic), 强烈 (strong/intense), 烈火 (raging fire), and 烈士 (martyr)

Definition: A cover or lid; as a verb, it means to cover, build, or construct something.
Usage: Common in words like 盖子 (lid), 盖房子 (build a house), or 盖章 (stamp/seal)

Definition: To squint or narrow one's eyes; to take a brief nap or doze off.
Usage: Common in phrases like 眯眼 (squint eyes) and 眯一会儿 (take a short nap)

Definition: A cage, coop, or basket used to contain animals or objects; also refers to a steamer basket used in cooking.
Usage: Common in words like 鸟笼 (birdcage), 笼子 (cage), and 蒸笼 (steamer basket)

Definition: To search for, demand, or ask for something; also means rope or cord in classical usage.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 搜索 (search), 索取 (demand/request), and 思索 (ponder)

Definition: The color green. Used to describe plants, traffic lights, environmental concepts, and anything green in color.
Usage: Common in words like 绿色 (green color), 绿茶 (green tea), 绿灯 (green light)

Definition: To give up, abandon, or part with something reluctantly; to be willing to sacrifice or let go of something.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 宿舍 (dormitory), 舍不得 (unwilling to part with), and 舍弃 (to abandon)

Definition: To dance or perform a dance; can also refer to a dance or dancing as a noun.
Usage: Common in words like 跳舞 (tiàowǔ - to dance) and 舞蹈 (wǔdǎo - dance)

Definition: A literary/classical Chinese word meaning 'do not' or 'none/nothing'. Also used as a surname.
Usage: Common in classical expressions like 莫名其妙 (baffling, inexplicable) and literary contexts; rarely used alone in modern spoken Chinese

Definition: To warn, alert, or be vigilant; relates to police and security matters
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 警察 (police), 警告 (warning), and 报警 (call the police)

Definition: To escape, run away, or flee from danger or an undesirable situation.
Usage: Common in words like 逃跑 (to run away), 逃避 (to evade), and 逃走 (to escape)

Definition: To drill, bore into, or penetrate through something; also means to squeeze or push one's way into a tight space.
Usage: Common in contexts like 钻孔 (drill a hole) or 钻进去 (squeeze into)

Definition: Smooth, in the same direction, or going along with something; also means to obey or follow順序 (order).
Usage: Common in words like 顺利 (smoothly), 顺便 (conveniently/by the way), and 顺序 (sequence)

Definition: To eat or food; a formal/literary term for eating or nourishment
Usage: Commonly seen in compound words like 食物 (food), 食品 (food products), or 美食 (delicious food); the everyday spoken word for 'eat' is 吃

Definition: The color yellow. Also commonly used as a surname (Huang).
Usage: Found in words like 黄色 (yellow color), 黄河 (Yellow River), and as a family name

Definition: Silent, quiet, or to remain silent; refers to not speaking or keeping one's thoughts to oneself.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 默默 (silently), 沉默 (silence), and 默写 (to write from memory)

Definition: The number six in Chinese.
Usage: Used in counting, dates, addresses, and phone numbers

Definition: Ice; frozen water in solid form. Can also mean to freeze or make something cold.
Usage: Common in words like 冰水 (ice water), 冰箱 (refrigerator), and 冰淇淋 (ice cream)

Definition: Situation or condition; most commonly seen in the word 况且 (kuàngqiě) meaning 'moreover' or 'besides'
Usage: Frequently used in compound words like 情况 (qíngkuàng - situation) and 状况 (zhuàngkuàng - condition)

Definition: Strength, energy, or force; also refers to vigor, enthusiasm, or the intensity of something.
Usage: Common in phrases like 有劲 (to have strength/energy), 使劲 (to exert force), and 干劲 (enthusiasm for work)

Definition: Medicine or medical treatment; also refers to a doctor or physician who practices medicine.
Usage: Common in words like 医生 (doctor), 医院 (hospital), and 中医 (traditional Chinese medicine)

Definition: To rise, go up, or ascend; also used as a measure word for liters.
Usage: Common in phrases like 上升 (to rise), 升级 (to upgrade), and measuring volume like 一升水 (one liter of water)

Definition: To take, get, or fetch something; to obtain or pick up. Also means to choose or select.
Usage: Common in phrases like 取钱 (withdraw money), 取消 (cancel), 争取 (strive for)

Definition: Right, as in the right-hand side or right direction (opposite of left).
Usage: Used in directional phrases like 右边 (right side) or 向右转 (turn right)

Definition: Each, every, or various; used to indicate individual items or people within a group separately.
Usage: Common in phrases like 各种 (various kinds), 各位 (everyone/ladies and gentlemen), 各自 (each one/respectively)

Definition: An onomatopoeia representing sounds like honking, tooting, or muttering; also describes pouting with protruding lips.
Usage: Common in words like 嘟嘟 (toot toot, beep beep) or 嘟嘴 (to pout)

Definition: To make a hissing sound or hoarse cry; describes the neighing of a horse or a hoarse voice.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 嘶哑 (hoarse) or to describe animal sounds

Definition: A wall, especially an interior wall or vertical surface of a room or cliff face. Can also refer to a barrier or partition.
Usage: Common in words like 墙壁 (wall), 壁画 (mural), 峭壁 (cliff)

Definition: To guard, protect, or defend something; to keep watch over or abide by rules and principles.
Usage: Common in words like 守护 (to guard), 遵守 (to obey/follow), and 守门 (to guard a gate)

Definition: To fear or be afraid of something; to dread or worry about a potential outcome.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 恐怕 (I'm afraid that..., probably) and 恐惧 (fear, terror)

Definition: To tie up, bind, or restrain; also used as a measure word for bundles or bunches of things (like flowers).
Usage: Common in words like 束缚 (to bind/restrain), 一束花 (a bouquet of flowers), 结束 (to end/conclude)

Definition: To check, examine, or investigate something; to look up or search for information.
Usage: Common in words like 检查 (to inspect), 查看 (to look at), and 查字典 (to look up in a dictionary)

Definition: Peach, a sweet fuzzy fruit; also refers to the peach tree itself
Usage: Common in words like 桃子 (peach fruit) and 桃花 (peach blossom)

Definition: Model, pattern, or mold; refers to a standard form or example to be copied or followed.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 模型 (model), 模式 (pattern/mode), and 模仿 (to imitate)

Definition: This; refers to something close or just mentioned, used in formal or written Chinese.
Usage: Common in phrases like 因此 (therefore), 此外 (besides), 如此 (like this)

Definition: A measure word meaning 'the slightest bit' or 'at all'; also a unit of measurement equal to one-tenth of a millimeter. Most commonly used in negative constructions to mean 'not at all' or 'not the slightest.'
Usage: Frequently appears in phrases like 毫无 (not have any), 毫不 (not at all), and 丝毫 (the slightest bit)

Definition: To rise, increase, or go up, typically referring to water levels, prices, or quantities.
Usage: Commonly used in contexts like 涨价 (prices rise) or 涨工资 (salary increases)

Definition: To swim or to travel/tour. Most commonly used to describe swimming in water or traveling for leisure.
Usage: Found in words like 游泳 (swimming), 旅游 (tourism/travel), and 游戏 (game)

Definition: To deep-fry food in oil; also means to explode or blow up
Usage: Common in cooking contexts like 炸鸡 (fried chicken) and 炸薯条 (french fries)

Definition: To guess or make an estimate without being certain; to suppose or conjecture about something unknown.
Usage: Common in phrases like 猜一猜 (take a guess) and 你猜 (guess what)

Definition: Illness, disease, or sickness; can also be used as a verb meaning 'to be sick' or 'to fall ill'
Usage: Common in expressions like 生病 (shēng bìng - to get sick) and 病人 (bìng rén - patient/sick person)

Definition: Broken, damaged, or torn; can also mean to break through or destroy something.
Usage: Common in words like 破了 (it's broken), 打破 (to break), and 突破 (breakthrough)

Definition: To move, shift, or transfer something from one place to another; to change position or location.
Usage: Common in words like 移动 (to move), 转移 (to transfer), and 移民 (to immigrate)

Definition: To sign (a document or name); a signature or slip of paper/bamboo used for writing or drawing lots.
Usage: Common in words like 签名 (sign one's name), 签证 (visa), 签字 (to sign), and 抽签 (draw lots)

Definition: Record, chronicle, or discipline; commonly refers to a period of time (century, era) or written records of events
Usage: Found in words like 世纪 (century), 纪念 (commemorate), 纪律 (discipline)

Definition: Recklessly, wildly, or carelessly; also means non-Han ethnic groups (historically) or used as a surname.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 胡说 (nonsense/talk nonsense) and 胡乱 (carelessly/randomly)

Definition: Egg; also used informally to refer to certain round or oval-shaped objects, or as slang for 'jerk' or 'fool'
Usage: Common in words like 鸡蛋 (chicken egg), 蛋糕 (cake), 笨蛋 (idiot)

Definition: Street or road in a city or town, typically referring to a public thoroughfare with buildings on both sides.
Usage: Common in words like 街道 (street), 商业街 (shopping street), and 过街 (cross the street)

Definition: To speak, talk, or tell; to explain or lecture about something. Also means to negotiate or pay attention to something.
Usage: Common in phrases like 讲话 (to speak), 讲故事 (to tell a story), and 讲课 (to give a lecture)

Definition: Certificate, proof, or evidence; a document that verifies identity, qualifications, or facts.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 证明 (proof/certificate), 身份证 (ID card), 签证 (visa)

Definition: A polite word meaning 'please' or 'to invite/request.' Used to make polite requests or to invite someone to do something.
Usage: Common in phrases like 请进 (please come in), 请坐 (please sit), or 请问 (excuse me, may I ask)

Definition: To talk, discuss, or chat about something. Often used when having conversations or negotiations about specific topics.
Usage: Common in words like 谈话 (to talk), 谈论 (to discuss), 交谈 (to converse)

Definition: Measure word (classifier) specifically used for counting vehicles such as cars, bicycles, trucks, and buses.
Usage: Used in phrases like 一辆车 (one car), 两辆自行车 (two bicycles)

Definition: To be confused, lost, or fascinated by something; can mean to lose one's way or to be obsessed with something
Usage: Used in words like 迷路 (get lost), 球迷 (sports fan), 着迷 (be fascinated)

Definition: To penetrate through, pass through, or see through something; also means thorough or complete.
Usage: Common in words like 透明 (transparent), 看透 (see through/understand completely), and 透过 (through/via)

Definition: Alcoholic beverage or liquor in general, including wine, beer, and spirits.
Usage: Common in words like 啤酒 (beer), 红酒 (red wine), and 喝酒 (to drink alcohol)

Definition: To lean on, lean against, or rely on something or someone for support. Can also mean to get close to or move near something.
Usage: Common in phrases like 靠墙 (lean against the wall) or 靠自己 (rely on oneself)

Definition: A meal or food served at a particular time of day. Used to refer to breakfast, lunch, dinner, or any formal eating occasion.
Usage: Common in words like 早餐 (breakfast), 午餐 (lunch), 晚餐 (dinner), and 餐厅 (restaurant)

Definition: Rat or mouse; a small rodent. Also refers to the Rat, the first animal in the Chinese zodiac.
Usage: Common in words like 老鼠 (mouse/rat) and 鼠年 (Year of the Rat)

Definition: Business, industry, or profession; also refers to a course of study or field of work. Commonly used to describe occupations, enterprises, and professional sectors.
Usage: Found in words like 工业 (industry), 商业 (commerce), 职业 (occupation), 毕业 (graduate)

Definition: Means 'extensive', 'abundant', or 'broad' in knowledge or scope; also means 'to win' or 'to gain'.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 博物馆 (museum), 博士 (doctor/PhD), and 赌博 (to gamble)

Definition: A room or compartment, especially one on the side of a building or vehicle; also refers to a wing or side section of a structure.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 车厢 (train car/carriage) and 包厢 (private room in a restaurant)

Definition: Means 'only' or 'alone', used to emphasize exclusivity or uniqueness. Often appears in formal or literary contexts to indicate 'the only' or 'solely'.
Usage: Common in phrases like 唯一 (wéiyī - the only one) and 唯有 (wéiyǒu - only have/only by)

Definition: An onomatopoeia that represents a sharp, sudden sound like a slap, crack, or snap.
Usage: Commonly used to describe sounds like clapping, hitting, or things breaking

Definition: Disciple, follower, or apprentice; also means 'in vain' or 'only/merely' when used as an adverb.
Usage: Common in words like 徒弟 (apprentice), 信徒 (believer), and 徒劳 (futile effort)

Definition: A badge, emblem, or insignia that represents an organization, group, or achievement. Also refers to Anhui Province (安徽) in abbreviated form.
Usage: Common in words like 国徽 (national emblem), 校徽 (school badge), and 徽章 (badge/insignia)

Definition: To throw or toss something; also means to discard or throw away.
Usage: Common in phrases like 扔垃圾 (throw away trash) or 扔球 (throw a ball)

Definition: To struggle or strive to break free from something; to make an effort to get loose
Usage: Often used in contexts like 挣扎 (to struggle) or when describing physical efforts to break free

Definition: To control, accuse, or charge; also means an enthusiast or fan of something (as a suffix in modern usage)
Usage: Used in words like 控制 (control), 指控 (accuse), and modern slang like 手机控 (phone addict)

Definition: To wipe, rub, or clean something by applying friction with a cloth or hand. Can also mean to apply something by rubbing (like lotion) or to brush past something.
Usage: Common in phrases like 擦桌子 (wipe the table), 擦黑板 (erase the blackboard), 擦药 (apply medicine)

Definition: To grip tightly with the hand; to clench or clutch something firmly in one's fist.
Usage: Often used to describe holding money, objects, or making a fist, as in 攥着钱 (clutching money) or 攥拳头 (clenching a fist)

Definition: To sway, shake, or rock back and forth; to flash or dazzle (of light)
Usage: Common in phrases like 晃动 (to shake) or 晃眼 (dazzling to the eyes)

Definition: Means 'graceful', 'extended', or 'long'; describes something elegant and flowing. Most commonly seen in names and literary expressions.
Usage: Frequently used in transliterations of foreign names like 曼谷 (Bangkok) and 曼哈顿 (Manhattan), and in compound words like 曼妙 (graceful)

Definition: Dream; the images, thoughts, and sensations experienced during sleep, or an aspiration or hope for the future
Usage: Used as a noun (做梦 to have a dream) or in compounds like 梦想 (dream/aspiration)

Definition: Excellent, great, or wonderful; also means a stick or club as a noun. Commonly used as an enthusiastic compliment in everyday conversation.
Usage: Used in expressions like 太棒了 (that's great!) or 你真棒 (you're awesome!)

Definition: A measure word for sections, segments, or periods of something; can also mean a section or paragraph of text, a length of road, or a period of time.
Usage: Common in phrases like 一段时间 (a period of time), 一段路 (a section of road), or 这段话 (this paragraph)

Definition: Steam, vapor, or gas. Most commonly refers to steam or gaseous forms of liquids.
Usage: Frequently used in compounds like 汽车 (qìchē, car/automobile) and 汽水 (qìshuǐ, soda/carbonated drink)

Definition: Gray (the color); also means ash or dust from burning materials
Usage: Common in color descriptions like 灰色 (gray color) and words like 灰尘 (dust) or 烟灰 (cigarette ash)

Definition: A stove, furnace, or oven used for heating or cooking. Can refer to various heating devices from traditional coal stoves to modern kitchen ranges.
Usage: Common in words like 火炉 (huǒlú - fireplace/stove), 烤炉 (kǎolú - oven), and 炉子 (lúzi - stove)

Definition: To explode, burst, or pop; can also mean to quick-fry or stir-fry at high heat in cooking.
Usage: Common in words like 爆炸 (explode), 爆米花 (popcorn), and cooking terms like 爆炒 (stir-fry)

Definition: To climb, crawl, or creep using hands and feet or the body close to the ground. Used for climbing mountains, trees, stairs, or describing how babies and insects move.
Usage: Common in phrases like 爬山 (climb a mountain), 爬树 (climb a tree), 爬楼梯 (climb stairs)

Definition: Alone, single, or solitary; indicates being by oneself or independent from others.
Usage: Common in words like 独自 (alone), 独立 (independent), 孤独 (lonely)

Definition: Electricity or electric power; also short for telephone, telegram, or anything related to electrical devices.
Usage: Common in words like 电话 (telephone), 电脑 (computer), 电视 (television)

Definition: Pain or ache; to hurt. Can describe physical pain or emotional suffering.
Usage: Common in words like 头痛 (headache), 疼痛 (pain), 痛苦 (suffering)

Definition: A plate, dish, or tray; also used as a measure word for disk-shaped objects or coiled things. Can also mean to coil, wind, or examine carefully.
Usage: Common in 盘子 (plate), 一盘菜 (a dish of food), 棋盘 (chessboard), or 盘问 (to interrogate)

Definition: Means 'true', 'accurate', or 'certain'; used to express confirmation or certainty about something.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 确定 (certain/to confirm), 的确 (indeed), and 确实 (really/truly)

Definition: To make an appointment or arrangement to meet someone; also means 'approximately' or 'about' when indicating estimates.
Usage: Common in phrases like 约会 (date/appointment) and 大约 (approximately)

Definition: A line, thread, or wire; refers to any thin, elongated strand or mark.
Usage: Common in words like 电线 (electric wire), 路线 (route), 毛线 (yarn), and 直线 (straight line)

Definition: To unite, unify, or gather together; to have overall control or command. Often used as a prefix meaning 'overall' or 'comprehensive'.
Usage: Common in words like 统一 (unify), 传统 (tradition), 系统 (system), and 总统 (president)

Definition: A boat or ship; any watercraft used for transportation on water.
Usage: Common in words like 船票 (boat ticket), 坐船 (take a boat), 渔船 (fishing boat)

Definition: The color blue. Can be used as both an adjective to describe blue things or as a noun meaning 'blue'.
Usage: Common in phrases like 蓝色 (blue color), 天蓝 (sky blue), 蓝天 (blue sky)

Definition: To be surprised or astonished; to feel wonder or amazement at something unexpected.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the word 惊讶 (jīngyà, surprised/amazed)

Definition: To hide, avoid, or dodge something or someone. Often used when trying to escape from danger, unwanted situations, or people.
Usage: Common in phrases like 躲雨 (take shelter from rain), 躲避 (avoid/evade)

Definition: To transport, carry, or move something from one place to another; also means luck or fortune.
Usage: Common in words like 运动 (sports/exercise), 运输 (transportation), and 幸运 (lucky)

Definition: To move back, retreat, or withdraw; also means to return or refund something.
Usage: Common in words like 退出 (exit/quit), 退休 (retire), and 退款 (refund)

Definition: To pick, gather, or collect (such as flowers, fruits, or information); to adopt or select something.
Usage: Common in words like 采访 (interview), 采取 (adopt/take measures), 采购 (purchase/procure)

Definition: To lead, guide, or receive/collect something. Also refers to a collar (of clothing) or neck area.
Usage: Common in words like 领导 (leader), 领取 (to receive/collect), and 衣领 (collar)

Definition: To ride or sit astride something, such as a horse, bicycle, or motorcycle.
Usage: Common in phrases like 骑马 (ride a horse), 骑车 (ride a bike)

Definition: The number seven.
Usage: Used in counting, dates, time expressions, and mathematical contexts

Definition: A cluster, clump, or thicket of plants growing together; a collection of things gathered densely in one place.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 草丛 (grass cluster), 丛林 (jungle/forest), or 花丛 (flower bed)

Definition: Beautiful, elegant, or magnificent; describes something visually attractive or splendid.
Usage: Commonly used in names (especially female names like 丽丽) and in words like 美丽 (beautiful) and 壮丽 (magnificent)

Definition: To produce, give birth to, or yield; also refers to products or property. Commonly used in words related to production, manufacturing, and assets.
Usage: Found in common words like 生产 (to produce), 产品 (product), 财产 (property)

Definition: To be situated between or in the middle; to introduce or present someone/something. Most commonly seen in compound words related to introduction or intermediary concepts.
Usage: Found in words like 介绍 (jièshào - to introduce), 中介 (zhōngjiè - intermediary/agent)

Definition: To enter, go into, or join. It indicates movement from outside to inside a place, group, or state.
Usage: Common in words like 进入 (to enter), 入口 (entrance), 加入 (to join)

Definition: To arrange in rows or lines; a row, line, or series of items. Also means to list or enumerate things systematically.
Usage: Common in words like 列车 (train), 列表 (list), and 系列 (series)

Definition: To remain or be left over; to have a surplus of something after use or distribution.
Usage: Commonly used in phrases like 剩下 (to be left), 剩饭 (leftover food/rice)

Definition: Thick (in dimension or density); can also mean generous, deep, or rich when describing relationships, flavors, or kindness.
Usage: Used to describe physical thickness (厚书 thick book) or abstract qualities (深厚 deep/profound)

Definition: To hold something in the mouth (like an animal carrying something with its teeth or beak)
Usage: Commonly used to describe dogs, birds, or other animals carrying objects in their mouths, like 狗叼着骨头 (dog holding a bone in its mouth)

Definition: To contain, hold, or include something within; to keep something in one's mouth without swallowing.
Usage: Common in words like 包含 (to include), 含有 (to contain), and 含义 (meaning/implication)

Definition: An onomatopoeia representing a clicking, tapping, or rattling sound, such as the sound of a machine gun, horse hooves, or typing. Also used as a cute particle at the end of sentences in informal online speech.
Usage: Common in sound effects like 哒哒哒 (rat-a-tat) or as a playful ending particle in casual text messages

Definition: An onomatopoeia expressing discontent, disdain, or mild annoyance; can also mean to hum or snort.
Usage: Often used as an interjection to show displeasure or skepticism, like '哼,我才不信呢!' (Hmph, I don't believe it!)

Definition: The Tang Dynasty (618-907 CE), one of China's most prosperous historical periods; also used to refer to China or Chinese people in some contexts.
Usage: Commonly seen in 唐朝 (Tang Dynasty), 唐人街 (Chinatown), and 唐诗 (Tang poetry)

Definition: A modal particle used at the end of sentences to express emotion, emphasis, or to soften tone. It can convey surprise, realization, admiration, or make statements sound more gentle and friendly.
Usage: Common in exclamations like 好啊 (great!), questions like 是吗啊 (really?), and casual statements

Definition: Throat or voice; refers to the vocal organs used for speaking and singing.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 嗓子 (throat/voice) and 嗓音 (voice quality)

Definition: Quiet, silent, or lonely; describes a state of stillness or desolation with few people or sounds.
Usage: Commonly appears in compound words like 寂寞 (jìmò - lonely) and 寂静 (jìjìng - quiet/silent)

Definition: Cold or chilly, referring to low temperature or cold weather. Can also describe poverty or a feeling of coldness.
Usage: Common in words like 寒冷 (cold weather), 严寒 (severe cold), and 寒假 (winter vacation)

Definition: Illusion, fantasy, or something unreal and imaginary. Refers to things that appear real but are not, or exist only in imagination.
Usage: Common in words like 幻想 (fantasy/illusion), 幻觉 (hallucination), and 梦幻 (dreamlike)

Definition: A crossbow, an ancient mechanical bow weapon that shoots arrows using a trigger mechanism.
Usage: Mainly used in historical, military, or literary contexts; common in phrases like 弓弩 (bows and crossbows)

Definition: Polite and respectful form of 'you' (singular), used to show courtesy and respect to elders, superiors, or strangers.
Usage: Common in formal situations, customer service, and when addressing people of higher status or age

Definition: To drag, pull, or haul something along a surface; to delay or postpone something.
Usage: Common in phrases like 拖地 (to mop the floor) and 拖延 (to procrastinate/delay)

Definition: Palm of the hand; also means to control, manage, or be in charge of something.
Usage: Common in words like 手掌 (palm), 掌握 (to grasp/master), and 鼓掌 (to applaud)

Definition: To push or shove something forward with force; also means to postpone, delay, or recommend.
Usage: Common in phrases like 推门 (push a door), 推迟 (postpone), and 推荐 (recommend)

Definition: To receive, collect, or gather something; also means to put away or store items.
Usage: Common in words like 收到 (receive), 收拾 (tidy up), and 收入 (income)

Definition: To break, snap, or cut off; to interrupt or discontinue something. Can refer to physical breaking or abstract interruption.
Usage: Common in words like 断线 (connection broken), 中断 (interrupt), 判断 (judge/determine)

Definition: Dark, dim, or dusky; also means muddled, confused, or to lose consciousness (faint).
Usage: Common in words like 昏迷 (coma), 黄昏 (dusk), and 头昏 (dizzy)

Definition: Adverb meaning 'once' or 'formerly', indicating that something happened at some point in the past
Usage: Commonly used in phrases like 曾经 (once, formerly) to describe past experiences

Definition: Bright, clear, or loud; describes something that is well-lit, distinct, or resonant.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 朗读 (to read aloud), 开朗 (cheerful/outgoing), and 晴朗 (clear/sunny)

Definition: Machine or device; also means opportunity or chance. Most commonly used as a suffix in compound words related to machinery and equipment.
Usage: Found in words like 飞机 (airplane), 手机 (cell phone), 电脑机 (computer), and 机会 (opportunity)

Definition: A measure word (classifier) used for counting trees and other plants with a trunk or stem.
Usage: Used in phrases like 一棵树 (one tree), 三棵白菜 (three cabbages)

Definition: To owe money or a debt to someone; to lack or be short of something.
Usage: Common in phrases like 欠钱 (owe money) and 欠缺 (to lack)

Definition: To wash or clean something with water or other liquid. This is the primary verb used for washing hands, clothes, dishes, hair, and bathing.
Usage: Common in everyday phrases like 洗手 (wash hands), 洗澡 (take a bath), 洗衣服 (wash clothes)

Definition: To slip away, sneak off, or slide; also means to stroll or take a walk. Can describe smooth, sliding movements or quietly leaving a place.
Usage: Common in phrases like 溜走 (slip away), 溜达 (take a stroll), or 溜冰 (ice skating)

Definition: To float or drift on water; to move along on the surface of liquid without sinking.
Usage: Common in contexts like 漂流 (to drift/float downstream) or describing objects floating on water

Definition: Hot or warm in temperature; can also mean enthusiastic, popular, or passionate about something.
Usage: Used to describe weather (天气很热 - the weather is hot), food temperature, or popularity (热门 - popular/hot topic)

Definition: Burnt or scorched; anxious or worried. Describes something that has been overcooked or charred, or a state of mental anxiety.
Usage: Common in words like 焦虑 (anxious), 焦急 (worried), and 烧焦 (burnt)

Definition: Flame or blaze; the visible part of fire that rises up and gives off light and heat.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 火焰 (huǒyàn - flame) and 气焰 (qìyàn - arrogance, literally 'air flame')

Definition: Ripe, cooked, or well-done (for food); familiar or well-acquainted (for people or things). Describes something that has reached a mature or ready state.
Usage: Common in phrases like 熟人 (acquaintance), 成熟 (mature), 熟悉 (familiar), and 煮熟 (cooked through)

Definition: A noble rank or title of nobility in ancient China; also refers to a type of ancient bronze wine vessel with three legs.
Usage: Commonly seen in historical contexts like 爵位 (noble title) or 封爵 (to confer a title of nobility)

Definition: Ruthless, fierce, or harsh; describes someone or something that is severe, merciless, or extreme in action or attitude.
Usage: Often used in phrases like 狠心 (heartless), 下狠手 (strike ruthlessly), or 很狠 (very fierce/harsh)

Definition: To wash one's hands and face; a formal or literary term for washing or cleansing.
Usage: Mainly seen in formal contexts like 盥洗室 (bathroom/washroom) or classical Chinese texts

Definition: To investigate, examine, or study something thoroughly; to get to the bottom of a matter.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 研究 (research), 追究 (investigate), and 究竟 (after all, actually)

Definition: Vertical or upright; to stand something up or erect it. Can also refer to a vertical stroke in Chinese calligraphy.
Usage: Common in words like 竖立 (to stand upright) and 横竖 (horizontal and vertical)

Definition: To carry something level with both hands; also means 'end' or 'extremity' of something. As a verb, it commonly refers to holding or bringing items like plates or bowls carefully.
Usage: Often used in contexts like 端茶 (carry tea) or 端盘子 (carry a plate); as a noun in 两端 (both ends)

Definition: An arrow, the projectile shot from a bow. Also refers to arrow-like objects or symbols, such as directional arrows.
Usage: Common in words like 弓箭 (bow and arrow), 火箭 (rocket), and 箭头 (arrowhead/arrow symbol)

Definition: To tower upward or stand tall; to rise high or stick up prominently.
Usage: Commonly used to describe tall buildings, mountains, or shoulders being raised (耸肩 shrug shoulders)

Definition: To resemble or be similar to; most commonly used as a surname or in the word 生肖 (Chinese zodiac)
Usage: Frequently seen in 生肖 (shēngxiào - zodiac animal) and as a family name

Definition: Dirty, filthy, or unclean. Describes something that is physically soiled or messy.
Usage: Commonly used to describe dirty clothes (衣服很脏), dirty hands (手脏), or messy rooms

Definition: Neck; the part of the body connecting the head to the shoulders.
Usage: Almost always used in the compound word 脖子 (bózi) meaning 'neck'

Definition: Means 'to arrive at' or 'to reach'; also used to indicate 'until' or 'up to' a certain point in time or space.
Usage: Common in phrases like 至少 (at least), 自...至... (from...to...), and 至于 (as for)

Definition: A suffix meaning 'kind' or 'sort' that indicates similarity or manner, equivalent to 'like' or '-like' in English.
Usage: Most commonly seen in compounds like 一般 (yībān - ordinary/general) and 这般 (zhèbān - like this)

Definition: Dark blue, gray, or pale in color; often describes the sky, sea, or something aged and weathered.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 苍天 (the heavens), 苍老 (aged/elderly), and 苍白 (pale)

Definition: Tea, referring to both the beverage and the tea plant/leaves used to make it.
Usage: Common in phrases like 喝茶 (drink tea), 茶叶 (tea leaves), and 绿茶 (green tea)

Definition: To discuss, deliberate, or comment on something; also means opinion or proposal
Usage: Common in words like 会议 (meeting), 建议 (suggestion), and 议论 (to discuss)

Definition: To discuss, debate, or talk about something; to determine or judge based on certain criteria
Usage: Common in words like 讨论 (discuss), 理论 (theory), 论文 (thesis/paper), and 无论 (no matter/regardless)

Definition: Elephant; also means appearance, image, or phenomenon. Commonly used as a verb meaning 'to resemble' or 'to be like'.
Usage: Found in words like 大象 (elephant), 现象 (phenomenon), 好象/好像 (to seem like)

Definition: To stick, paste, or attach something to a surface; to glue or affix closely to something.
Usage: Common in everyday contexts like 贴纸 (sticker), 贴海报 (put up a poster), or 贴邮票 (affix a stamp)

Definition: A thief or robber; someone who steals. In colloquial usage, can also mean 'very' or 'extremely' as an adverb.
Usage: Common in phrases like 小贼 (petty thief) or colloquially 贼好吃 (extremely delicious)

Definition: Trace, track, or footprint; refers to marks or signs left behind that show where someone or something has been.
Usage: Most commonly seen in compounds like 踪迹 (zōngjì - traces/tracks) and 失踪 (shīzōng - to go missing)

Definition: Speed, velocity, or rate; describes how fast something moves or happens.
Usage: Commonly used in compounds like 速度 (speed), 快速 (fast/rapid), and 高速 (high-speed)

Definition: To release, let go, or set free; to explain or interpret the meaning of something
Usage: Common in words like 解释 (to explain), 释放 (to release), and 诠释 (to interpret)

Definition: Feeling bored, depressed, or stuffy; describes a heavy, oppressive feeling in one's mood or atmosphere.
Usage: Common in expressions like 闷热 (stuffy/humid weather) or 心里很闷 (feeling down/depressed)

Definition: Edge, border, or boundary; often used to mean 'between' or 'inter-' in compound words relating to relationships or connections.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 国际 (guójì - international), 实际 (shíjì - actual/practical), and 交际 (jiāojì - social interaction)

Definition: Fog or mist; a thick cloud of tiny water droplets suspended in the air near the ground that reduces visibility.
Usage: Common in weather descriptions like 大雾 (heavy fog) or 雾天 (foggy day)

Definition: A building or establishment that serves a specific public function, such as a museum, library, restaurant, or hotel. It is used as a suffix to indicate various types of public venues or facilities.
Usage: Common in words like 图书馆 (library), 博物馆 (museum), 饭馆 (restaurant), 宾馆 (hotel)

Definition: To pay or hand over money; to give payment for goods or services.
Usage: Common in words like 付钱 (to pay money) and 支付 (payment)

Definition: A measure word for groups of people, often with a collective or informal sense; can also mean 'partner' or 'companion'.
Usage: Commonly seen in 伙伴 (huǒbàn - partner/companion) and 一伙人 (yì huǒ rén - a group of people)

Definition: To steal or take something secretly without permission; can also mean to do something secretly or stealthily.
Usage: Common in phrases like 偷东西 (steal things) or 偷偷地 (secretly, stealthily)

Definition: To allow, permit, or consent to something. It means to give permission or approval for an action or request.
Usage: Commonly seen in formal contexts like 允许 (yǔnxǔ - to permit) and 答应 (dāying - to promise/agree)

Definition: Phoenix, a mythical Chinese bird symbolizing good fortune, prosperity, and the empress. Often paired with dragon (龙) in traditional Chinese culture.
Usage: Common in names, idioms like 龙凤呈祥 (dragon and phoenix bring prosperity), and cultural references

Definition: Merit, achievement, or skill; also refers to effort or work put into something. Commonly used to describe accomplishments,功夫 (kung fu/skill), or success in endeavors.
Usage: Found in words like 成功 (success), 功课 (homework/lessons), and 功夫 (kung fu/skill)

Definition: To exert oneself or make an effort; to strive or work hard toward a goal.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the word 努力 (nǔlì, to work hard/make an effort)

Definition: To lie down or recline; to be in a horizontal resting position.
Usage: Common in words like 卧室 (bedroom, literally 'lying room') and 卧铺 (sleeping berth on a train)

Definition: To sigh or exclaim, expressing emotions like sadness, regret, or admiration through an audible breath or utterance.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 叹气 (to sigh) and 感叹 (to exclaim with emotion)

Definition: To exhale or sigh; to appeal or call out for something urgently.
Usage: Often seen in formal written expressions like 呼吁 (to appeal/call for)

Definition: To roar or bellow loudly, typically describing the fierce sound made by animals like lions or tigers, or angry shouting by people.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the word 咆哮 (páoxiào) meaning 'to roar'

Definition: An onomatopoeia representing a clicking, snapping, or cracking sound.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 咔嚓 (kāchā, click/snap sound) or to mimic mechanical sounds

Definition: Throat; refers to the passage in the neck used for breathing and swallowing
Usage: Almost always used in the compound word 喉咙 (hóulóng, throat)

Definition: To roar, howl, or wheeze; describes loud, forceful breathing sounds or animal roars.
Usage: Most commonly seen in 哮喘 (xiàochuǎn, asthma) and describing roaring sounds like wind or beasts

Definition: Modal particle that combines 了 (le) and 啊 (a), used at the end of sentences to indicate a change of state or completion with an exclamatory or casual tone.
Usage: Common in spoken Chinese to soften statements or express enthusiasm, as in 好啦 (alright then) or 我走啦 (I'm leaving now)

Definition: Throat; the passage in the neck through which food and air pass. Refers to the anatomical structure used for breathing, swallowing, and speaking.
Usage: Commonly appears in medical contexts and compound words like 喉咙 (throat) and 咽喉 (pharynx and larynx)

Definition: To spray, spurt, or gush out; to eject liquid or gas forcefully from an opening.
Usage: Common in words like 喷泉 (fountain), 喷水 (spray water), or describing actions like sneezing or spraying perfume

Definition: A round mass or ball; also means group, organization, or团体 (团 is commonly used to refer to organized groups or团队).
Usage: Found in words like 团队 (team), 集团 (group/corporation), 饭团 (rice ball)

Definition: Round or circular in shape; also means complete or satisfactory. Can refer to a circle or sphere as a noun.
Usage: Common in words like 圆形 (circular shape), 团圆 (family reunion), and 圆满 (perfect/complete)

Definition: Wonderful, excellent, or marvelous; describes something clever, ingenious, or remarkably good.
Usage: Common in expressions like 美妙 (beautiful/wonderful) and 奇妙 (amazing/magical)

Definition: To entrust, appoint, or delegate responsibility to someone; also means to shift blame or shirk responsibility.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 委托 (entrust), 委员 (committee member), and 委屈 (feel wronged)

Definition: Layer, level, or floor of a building. Used as a measure word for things that are stacked or arranged in layers.
Usage: Common in expressions like 一层 (first floor), 三层楼 (three-story building), or 一层意思 (one layer of meaning)

Definition: A narrow lane, alley, or small street, typically found in residential areas or between buildings.
Usage: Common in words like 小巷 (small alley) and 巷子 (lane)

Definition: Degree or extent; a measure of temperature, angles, or intensity. Also means 'to spend/pass' time or to measure.
Usage: Common in words like 温度 (temperature), 态度 (attitude), 速度 (speed), and 度过 (to spend time)

Definition: Royal court or imperial court; refers to the place where a monarch conducts official business and holds audiences.
Usage: Mainly appears in formal or classical contexts, such as 朝廷 (imperial court) or 宫廷 (royal palace/court)

Definition: Color or variety of colors; also refers to applause, praise, or lottery/prize winnings.
Usage: Most commonly seen in words like 彩色 (colored), 精彩 (wonderful), and 彩票 (lottery ticket)

Definition: To know in detail or be fully informed about something; to be familiar with all aspects of a matter.
Usage: Commonly seen in formal or literary contexts, such as 熟悉 (familiar with) and 悉知 (to know fully)

Definition: To tie, bind, or fasten something together; to prick or pierce into something.
Usage: Common in words like 扎头发 (tie hair) or 扎针 (give an injection)

Definition: To poke, stab, or thrust with a pointed object; to prod or jab something with force.
Usage: Often used for physical actions like poking a hole (捅破) or stabbing, and figuratively for causing trouble or exposing secrets (捅娄子 - stir up trouble)

Definition: To arrange or line up in a row; also means a row or line of things/people. Can also mean to rehearse (as in a play) or to exclude/discharge.
Usage: Common in words like 排队 (line up), 排球 (volleyball), 排练 (rehearse)

Definition: To rotate, revolve, or spin around; to turn in a circular motion
Usage: Common in words like 旋转 (xuánzhuǎn - to rotate) and 螺旋 (luóxuán - spiral)

Definition: Easy, simple; also means to change or exchange. As an adjective, it describes something that is not difficult to do or understand.
Usage: Common in words like 容易 (easy), 简易 (simple), 交易 (transaction/trade), and 变易 (change)

Definition: A pillar, column, or post used to support a structure. Can also refer to anything shaped like a column or used as a support.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 柱子 (zhùzi - pillar) and 石柱 (shízhù - stone pillar)

Definition: Dense forest or woods; also means numerous, dense, or dark (like a thick forest). The character visually shows three trees (木) together to represent a forest.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 森林 (sēnlín - forest) and 阴森 (yīnsēn - gloomy/eerie)

Definition: Forever, eternal, or permanent. Expresses the idea of something lasting indefinitely or never ending.
Usage: Common in words like 永远 (forever), 永久 (permanent), and 永恒 (eternal)

Definition: To weep or sob quietly; to cry silently with tears flowing down one's face.
Usage: More literary or formal than 哭 (kū); often appears in written Chinese and classical expressions

Definition: To send, dispatch, or assign someone to do something; also refers to a faction, school of thought, or style (as in '派别').
Usage: Common in contexts like 派人 (send someone), 派遣 (dispatch), or 流派 (school/style)

Definition: To flow or stream; refers to the movement of liquids, air, or people in a continuous manner.
Usage: Common in words like 流水 (flowing water), 流行 (popular/trending), and 交流 (exchange/communicate)

Definition: Slippery or smooth in texture; to slide or glide across a surface
Usage: Common in words like 滑冰 (ice skating), 光滑 (smooth), and 滑倒 (to slip and fall)

Definition: A lamp, light, or lantern; any device that produces illumination.
Usage: Common in words like 电灯 (electric light), 红绿灯 (traffic light), and 台灯 (desk lamp)

Definition: To shine, sparkle, or glitter; describes bright, flickering light or something that gleams.
Usage: Commonly seen in literary expressions like 闪烁 (shǎnshuò - to twinkle) or 烁烁 (shuòshuò - sparkling)

Definition: To burn, to cook with fire or heat; can also mean to have a fever (when referring to body temperature).
Usage: Common in cooking contexts like 红烧 (braised) and medical contexts like 发烧 (to have a fever)

Definition: To hunt or chase wild animals. Also used metaphorically for pursuing or seeking something actively.
Usage: Common in words like 猎人 (hunter), 打猎 (to hunt), and 猎取 (to hunt for/seek)

Definition: King or monarch; also an extremely common Chinese surname (Wang)
Usage: As a title means 'king' (国王), but most frequently encountered as a family name

Definition: A bottle or vase; a container typically made of glass or plastic with a narrow neck used for holding liquids.
Usage: Commonly used as a measure word counter, as in 一瓶水 (a bottle of water) or 花瓶 (flower vase)

Definition: A measure word (classifier) used for counting written works, articles, essays, and compositions.
Usage: Used in phrases like 一篇文章 (one article) or 三篇作文 (three essays)

Definition: Type, kind, or category; used to classify things into groups based on shared characteristics.
Usage: Common in words like 种类 (zhǒnglèi - type/kind), 人类 (rénlèi - humanity), and as a suffix meaning '-type' or '-kind'

Definition: To maintain, preserve, or keep something in a certain state; also means 'dimension' in technical contexts.
Usage: Common in words like 维持 (maintain), 维护 (safeguard), and 思维 (thinking/thought process)

Definition: To shine brightly, to dazzle, or to show off. Can refer to light radiating brilliantly or displaying something proudly.
Usage: Common in words like 荣耀 (glory/honor) and 闪耀 (to sparkle/shine)

Definition: To raise, nurture, or educate; to give birth to or cultivate growth and development.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 教育 (education), 体育 (physical education/sports), and 育儿 (child-rearing)

Definition: Tone, accent, or manner of speaking; also refers to a cavity or hollow space in the body.
Usage: Common in words like 口腔 (oral cavity), 腔调 (accent/tone), and 唱腔 (singing style)

Definition: Knee, the joint in the middle of the leg where it bends.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the word 膝盖 (xī gài, knee) and phrases like 跪下 (kneel down)

Definition: Arm, referring to the upper limb from shoulder to hand. Also used in compound words to describe arm-like extensions or branches.
Usage: Common in words like 手臂 (arm), 臂膀 (arm/shoulder), and 左右臂 (right-hand man)

Definition: To hide, conceal, or store something away from view. Can also mean to collect or hoard.
Usage: Common in words like 躲藏 (to hide), 收藏 (to collect), 隐藏 (to conceal)

Definition: To look at, watch, or observe; to view or examine something carefully. Also means a view, perspective, or outlook on something.
Usage: Common in words like 参观 (visit/tour), 观看 (watch), 观点 (viewpoint), and 乐观 (optimistic)

Definition: Birth or to be born; often used in formal or literary contexts to refer to someone's birth or birthday.
Usage: Most commonly seen in 诞生 (dànshēng - to be born/come into being) and 圣诞 (Shèngdàn - Christmas, literally 'holy birth')

Definition: To force, compel, or press someone to do something; to be urgent or pressing.
Usage: Common in words like 迫切 (urgent), 压迫 (oppress), and 逼迫 (force/coerce)

Definition: To chase, pursue, or run after someone or something. Also commonly used to mean pursuing romantic interest in someone or catching up with something (like a TV show).
Usage: Used in phrases like 追人 (chase someone), 追剧 (binge-watch a series), 追求 (pursue/seek)

Definition: To suit, fit, or be appropriate for something; to be comfortable or suitable. Also means 'to go to' in classical Chinese.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 适合 (suitable), 舒适 (comfortable), 适应 (adapt to)

Definition: A bell or small ringing device that makes a tinkling sound when shaken or struck.
Usage: Commonly found in compounds like 门铃 (doorbell), 铃声 (ringtone), and 风铃 (wind chime)

Definition: To close or shut something, such as a door, window, eyes, or mouth.
Usage: Common in words like 关闭 (to close), 闭嘴 (shut up), and 闭眼 (close eyes)

Definition: To shake, vibrate, or shock; refers to earthquakes or strong trembling movements that cause impact or surprise.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 地震 (earthquake), 震动 (vibration), and 震惊 (shocked/astonished)

Definition: Mold or mildew; also refers to bad luck or misfortune in colloquial usage.
Usage: Common in words like 发霉 (to become moldy) and 倒霉 (to have bad luck)

Definition: To bow deeply or bend over as a sign of respect; also refers to raising or nurturing (in literary contexts).
Usage: Most commonly seen in the phrase 鞠躬 (jū gōng, to bow) and 鞠养 (jū yǎng, to raise/nurture)

Definition: Bone; the hard structural parts of the skeleton in humans and animals.
Usage: Common in words like 骨头 (bone), 骨折 (fracture), and 骨气 (moral integrity/backbone)

Definition: A drum (noun); to beat or strike a drum, or to encourage/inspire someone (verb)
Usage: Common in words like 打鼓 (play the drum) and 鼓励 (encourage)

Definition: The number ten thousand (10,000); a large numerical unit in the Chinese counting system
Usage: Essential for expressing large numbers, like 三万 (30,000) or 一万块钱 (10,000 yuan)

Definition: A conjunction meaning 'and' or 'moreover' that connects clauses or ideas; also used to mean 'for now' or 'temporarily' in certain contexts.
Usage: Common in formal or written Chinese, as in 而且 (moreover) or 并且 (and also)

Definition: Long (in duration of time); refers to a lengthy period or extended time span.
Usage: Common in phrases like 很久 (very long time), 好久不见 (long time no see)

Definition: To urge, promote, or hurry someone to do something; also means short or brief in time or space.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 促进 (to promote), 促使 (to urge), and 短促 (brief/short)

Definition: A measure word for objects with specific forms, such as corpses, coffins, or sets of items; also means 'tool' or 'to possess/have' in formal contexts.
Usage: Commonly seen in 一具尸体 (one corpse), 工具 (tool), or 具有 (to possess/have)

Definition: To gather together, collect, or pool (money, people, or things); to move close to something or someone.
Usage: Common in phrases like 凑钱 (pool money together) and 凑合 (make do with what's available)

Definition: Female phoenix in Chinese mythology, representing the empress or feminine imperial power. Always used in the compound 凤凰 (fènghuáng), where 凤 is the male phoenix and 凰 is the female phoenix.
Usage: Rarely used alone; almost exclusively appears in the word 凤凰 (phoenix)

Definition: A spoon or key; a utensil for eating or scooping, or an instrument for opening locks.
Usage: Commonly seen in compounds like 钥匙 (yàoshi - key) and 汤匙 (tāngchí - spoon)

Definition: To occupy or take up (space, time, or a position); to account for or constitute (a proportion or percentage).
Usage: Common in phrases like 占地方 (take up space) and 占百分之十 (account for 10 percent)

Definition: Means 'namely', 'that is', or 'immediately/right away'. Often used in formal writing to clarify or specify something, or to indicate immediacy.
Usage: Common in phrases like 即使 (even if), 立即 (immediately), 即将 (about to)

Definition: Means 'opposite', 'contrary', or 'anti-'; also used as a verb meaning 'to oppose' or 'to reverse'
Usage: Common in words like 反对 (oppose), 相反 (opposite), and 反应 (reaction/response)

Definition: An onomatopoeia representing gurgling, cooing, or murmuring sounds. Often used to mimic sounds made by birds, stomachs, or bubbling liquids.
Usage: Commonly appears in reduplicated forms like 咕咕 (gūgū) for bird cooing or 咕噜 (gūlu) for stomach rumbling

Definition: A modal particle used at the end of sentences to indicate a light, casual tone or to soften a statement, similar to 'well' or 'you know' in English.
Usage: Often used in spoken Mandarin to make statements sound friendlier or less direct, as in 好咯 (alright then)

Definition: A character used to represent murmuring or muttering sounds, typically soft and indistinct speech.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the compound word 喃喃 (nán nán) meaning 'to murmur' or in 呢喃 (ní nán) describing soft whispers or bird chirping

Definition: An onomatopoeia that represents a whooshing or whistling sound, typically describing something moving swiftly through the air.
Usage: Often used to describe the sound of wind, arrows, or objects passing by quickly, as in 嗖的一声 (with a whoosh)

Definition: To clip, pinch, or hold something between two objects or surfaces; to place something in between.
Usage: Common in phrases like 夹菜 (to pick up food with chopsticks) and 夹子 (clip, clamp)

Definition: A measure word for sets or collections of things that go together; also means 'to cover' or 'to slip on' as a verb.
Usage: Used for counting sets like 一套书 (a set of books), 一套房子 (an apartment/suite), or as a verb like 套上 (to put on/slip over)

Definition: Awkward, embarrassing, or uncomfortable; describes situations or feelings that are socially awkward or cringeworthy.
Usage: Most commonly seen in modern slang like 尴尬 (gān gà - awkward) or 尬聊 (gà liáo - awkward conversation)

Definition: Embarrassed or awkward; describes a feeling of discomfort in social situations.
Usage: Most commonly used in the compound word 尴尬 (gān gà) meaning 'embarrassed' or 'awkward'

Definition: Fart or flatulence; also used colloquially to mean 'nonsense' or 'nothing at all'.
Usage: Common in informal speech, such as 放屁 (fàng pì - to fart/talk nonsense) or 屁话 (pì huà - nonsense/bullshit)

Definition: Left, as in the left side or left direction, opposite of right (右).
Usage: Common in directional phrases like 左边 (left side), 左手 (left hand), or 向左转 (turn left)

Definition: Skillful, clever, or ingenious; describes someone who is good with their hands or has a talent for making things well.
Usage: Common in words like 技巧 (skill/technique), 巧克力 (chocolate - phonetic), and 灵巧 (dexterous)

Definition: A warehouse, storehouse, or repository where things are stored. Also commonly used in compound words related to storage and databases.
Usage: Found in words like 仓库 (warehouse), 数据库 (database), 车库 (garage)

Definition: Huge, enormous, or gigantic in size or scale. Also commonly used as a surname.
Usage: Most frequently seen in compounds like 庞大 (pángdà - huge/enormous) and 庞然大物 (pángrán dàwù - colossus/behemoth)

Definition: To build, construct, or establish something. Used for both physical structures and abstract concepts like organizations or systems.
Usage: Common in words like 建立 (establish), 建设 (construct), 建议 (suggest/propose)

Definition: Different, unusual, or strange; indicates something that differs from the normal or expected.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 异常 (abnormal), 差异 (difference), and 奇异 (peculiar)

Definition: To hang or suspend in the air; to be unresolved or pending
Usage: Common in words like 悬挂 (to hang up), 悬念 (suspense), and 悬而未决 (pending/unresolved)

Definition: To bear, undertake, or receive; to承认 (admit) or承担 (take responsibility for something). Often used in formal contexts to express承接 (continuing/inheriting) or承受 (enduring/bearing).
Usage: Common in compounds like 承认 (chéngrèn - to admit), 承担 (chéngdān - to undertake), 承受 (chéngshòu - to bear/endure)

Definition: To pick up or gather something from the ground, especially something that has been dropped or discarded.
Usage: Commonly used in phrases like 捡垃圾 (pick up trash) or 捡到钱 (find/pick up money)

Definition: According to; based on. Used to cite sources or indicate the basis for information or claims.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the phrase 据说 (jùshuō - it is said that) and 根据 (gēnjù - according to)

Definition: To hold, grasp, or grip something with the hand; to clasp or shake hands.
Usage: Commonly used in 握手 (shake hands) and 把握 (grasp/seize an opportunity)

Definition: To scatter, sprinkle, or spread something loosely (like seeds, salt, or powder). Also means to let go or release.
Usage: Common in phrases like 撒种 (scatter seeds), 撒盐 (sprinkle salt), or 撒手 (let go)

Definition: To attack or assault; to study or specialize in a particular subject.
Usage: Common in military contexts (进攻 - to attack) and academic contexts (攻读 - to study for a degree)

Definition: Travel or journey; refers to taking a trip or being away from home for tourism or exploration.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 旅行 (travel), 旅游 (tourism), and 旅客 (traveler/passenger)

Definition: Morning or early morning, specifically the time around dawn or sunrise.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 早晨 (zǎochén - morning) and 清晨 (qīngchén - early morning)

Definition: Scenery, view, or landscape; can also refer to a situation or scene. Often used to describe natural or urban views and sights.
Usage: Common in words like 风景 (fēngjǐng - scenery), 景色 (jǐngsè - landscape), and 背景 (bèijǐng - background)

Definition: Heat or hot weather, especially the intense heat of summer.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 暑假 (summer vacation) and 中暑 (heatstroke)

Definition: A pronoun meaning 'certain' or 'some' used to refer to an unspecified person, place, or thing. Often used when the speaker doesn't want to or cannot specify exactly who or what they're referring to.
Usage: Common in phrases like 某人 (a certain person/someone), 某地 (a certain place/somewhere), 某天 (a certain day/someday)

Definition: State, condition, or appearance of something; also means shape or form.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 状态 (state/condition), 状况 (situation), and 形状 (shape)

Definition: Crazy, wild, or mad; describes extreme, uncontrolled behavior or enthusiasm. Can also mean arrogant or fanatical.
Usage: Common in words like 疯狂 (fēngkuáng - crazy/wild) and 狂热 (kuángrè - fanatical)

Definition: A ring, circle, or loop-shaped object; can also mean to surround or encircle something.
Usage: Common in words like 环境 (environment, literally 'surrounding'), 耳环 (earring), and 循环 (cycle)

Definition: To look at or see; an informal, colloquial way to say 'look' or 'see'
Usage: Common in spoken Chinese, often used in phrases like 瞧一瞧 (take a look) or 你瞧 (look!)

Definition: To wish or express good wishes; to offer blessings or congratulations to someone.
Usage: Commonly used in greetings and celebrations like 祝你生日快乐 (wish you happy birthday) or 祝贺 (congratulate)

Definition: Auspicious, lucky, or fortunate; refers to good omens and prosperity.
Usage: Commonly found in names and traditional expressions like 吉祥 (jíxiáng - auspicious) and 慈祥 (cíxiáng - kindly)

Definition: An adverb expressing surprise or unexpectedness, meaning 'unexpectedly', 'actually', or 'to one's surprise'.
Usage: Often used in phrases like 竟然 (unexpectedly) to emphasize that something happened contrary to expectations

Definition: To test or examine; to take or give an exam. Also means to investigate or think over carefully.
Usage: Common in words like 考试 (exam), 高考 (college entrance exam), and 考虑 (to consider)

Definition: The chest or breast area of the body; the front part of the torso between the neck and abdomen.
Usage: Common in words like 胸口 (chest area), 胸部 (chest/breast), and 心胸 (mind/breadth of mind)

Definition: To take off, remove, or shed (clothing, shoes, or outer layers); to escape or break away from something.
Usage: Common in everyday expressions like 脱衣服 (take off clothes), 脱鞋 (take off shoes)

Definition: Comfortable, relaxed, or at ease; describes a pleasant physical or mental state free from stress or discomfort.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 舒服 (comfortable) and 舒适 (cozy)

Definition: To think over, consider, or worry about something carefully. Often refers to concerns or anxieties about future situations.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 考虑 (kǎolǜ - to consider), 顾虑 (gùlǜ - misgivings), and 忧虑 (yōulǜ - to worry)

Definition: A spiral-shelled creature like a snail or conch; also refers to螺旋 (spiral) shapes and螺丝 (screw) in compound words.
Usage: Common in words like 海螺 (sea snail), 螺丝 (screw), and 螺旋 (spiral)

Definition: Sock or stocking; a piece of clothing worn on the foot and lower leg.
Usage: Commonly used in 袜子 (wàzi, socks) and 丝袜 (sīwà, stockings)

Definition: To wrap, bind, or bundle something up by covering it completely from all sides.
Usage: Commonly used for wrapping objects, food (like dumplings), or bundling oneself in clothing, as in 包裹 (package) or 裹着毯子 (wrapped in a blanket)

Definition: To read aloud or to study; refers to the act of reading text or attending school.
Usage: Common in phrases like 读书 (to read books/to study) and 读大学 (to attend university)

Definition: A Chinese surname; also an archaic term meaning 'merchant' or 'to trade'
Usage: Most commonly encountered as a family name, as in 贾宝玉 (Jia Baoyu), the protagonist of the classic novel Dream of the Red Chamber

Definition: A wheel or circular object; also used as a measure word for rounds, turns, or cycles of events.
Usage: Common in words like 车轮 (wheel), 轮流 (take turns), and phrases like 第一轮 (first round)

Definition: To welcome, greet, or go to meet someone or something. Also means to move toward or face something approaching.
Usage: Common in phrases like 欢迎 (welcome), 迎接 (to meet/greet)

Definition: A trace, mark, or sign left behind by something; evidence or indication of past presence or activity.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 痕迹 (hénjì - trace/mark), 足迹 (zújì - footprint), and 奇迹 (qíjì - miracle)

Definition: To pass, hand over, or deliver something to someone. Commonly used when giving objects from one person to another.
Usage: Used in phrases like 递给我 (pass to me) or 递交 (submit/hand in)

Definition: To meet or encounter someone or something, often by chance or unexpectedly. Can also mean to experience or come across a situation.
Usage: Common in words like 遇到 (yù dào - to run into), 相遇 (xiāng yù - to meet), and 遭遇 (zāo yù - to encounter/experience)

Definition: Key, as in the tool used to open locks. This character is almost always used in the compound word 钥匙 (yàoshi).
Usage: Rarely used alone; typically appears in 钥匙 (key)

Definition: Money or currency in general form. One of the most essential everyday words for financial transactions and discussing costs.
Usage: Used in phrases like 多少钱 (how much money), 有钱 (to have money/be wealthy), 花钱 (to spend money)

Definition: To rush or barge in; to break through or force one's way into a place. Also means to venture out or make one's way in the world through bold action.
Usage: Common in phrases like 闯进 (to barge into) and 闯祸 (to cause trouble)

Definition: A step or stair; also refers to rank, level, or grade in a hierarchy or system.
Usage: Common in words like 楼梯 (stairs), 阶段 (stage/phase), and 阶级 (social class)

Definition: Means 'special', 'specialized', or 'focused on one thing'; often indicates concentration or expertise in a particular area.
Usage: Common in words like 专业 (major/profession), 专家 (expert), and 专门 (specially/exclusively)

Definition: Great, mighty, or grand in scale or importance. Used to describe impressive achievements, people, or things of exceptional significance.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 伟大 (wěidà - great/mighty) and names like 毛泽东 (Máo Zédōng)

Definition: Father's elder brother (uncle); also used as a respectful term for elderly men or in titles to indicate seniority or rank.
Usage: Common in family terms like 伯父 (uncle) and names like 伯爵 (earl/count)

Definition: Value or worth; can also mean 'to be worth' or 'to be on duty'. Most commonly used to express the value or price of something.
Usage: Found in words like 价值 (value), 值得 (worthwhile), and 值班 (on duty)

Definition: To fill, to be full of, or to act as/serve as. Also means to charge (a battery or phone) or to top up (an account).
Usage: Common in words like 充电 (charge a battery), 充满 (be full of), 充当 (act as)

Definition: A pocket or pouch; as a verb, it means to wrap up, hold in a bag, or go around in a circle.
Usage: Common in words like 裤兜 (pants pocket) and 兜风 (go for a drive/ride)

Definition: The number eight. In Chinese culture, eight is considered a lucky number because it sounds similar to the word for prosperity (发).
Usage: Used in counting, dates, addresses, and phone numbers

Definition: To cut with scissors or shears; to trim or clip something using a cutting tool.
Usage: Common in phrases like 剪头发 (cut hair), 剪纸 (paper cutting)

Definition: A suffix meaning 'to change into' or 'to transform'; also means '-ize' or '-ify' when creating verbs from nouns or adjectives.
Usage: Common in words like 文化 (culture), 变化 (change), 现代化 (modernize), 美化 (beautify)

Definition: The number one thousand (1,000). Used in counting, measurements, and expressing large quantities.
Usage: Common in phrases like 千米 (kilometer), 三千 (three thousand), and 成千上万 (thousands upon thousands)

Definition: South; the cardinal direction opposite to north. Also used to refer to southern regions or areas.
Usage: Common in directional terms like 南方 (south/southern region), 东南 (southeast), and place names like 湖南 (Hunan)

Definition: To chant, recite, or hum poetry or verses in a rhythmic, melodious way. Often refers to the traditional Chinese practice of reciting classical poetry aloud.
Usage: Commonly seen in literary contexts like 吟诗 (chant poetry) or 呻吟 (groan/moan)

Definition: To kiss; a kiss. Used for romantic kisses as well as affectionate kisses between family members.
Usage: Common in phrases like 接吻 (to kiss) and 亲吻 (to kiss affectionately)

Definition: To groan or moan, typically expressing pain, discomfort, or distress through vocal sounds.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the word 呻吟 (shēnyín, to groan/moan)

Definition: An onomatopoeia that represents hissing, snickering, or laughing sounds. It mimics sounds like air escaping, steam releasing, or suppressed laughter.
Usage: Commonly seen in compounds like 哧哧 (hissing sound) or 哧笑 (to snicker/giggle)

Definition: An onomatopoeia representing clanging, jingling, or metallic ringing sounds.
Usage: Commonly appears in compound words like 叮叮啷啷 (ding ding lang lang - jingling sound) or 啷当 (lang dang - clanging sound)

Definition: A crucible, which is a heat-resistant container used for melting metals or other substances at very high temperatures.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the compound word 坩埚 (gānguō), meaning crucible, used in scientific and industrial contexts

Definition: To bury or hide something underground or beneath a surface; to cover up completely.
Usage: Common in phrases like 埋葬 (to bury the dead) and 埋头 (to immerse oneself in work)

Definition: A crucible or pot used for melting metals or other materials at high temperatures in industrial or laboratory settings.
Usage: Commonly seen in technical contexts like 坩埚 (gānguō - crucible)

Definition: To seize, grab, or take by force; to compete for and win something.
Usage: Common in words like 夺取 (seize), 争夺 (fight for), and 夺冠 (win a championship)

Definition: Milk or breast milk; also refers to grandmother (paternal) or a term for breasts
Usage: Common in words like 牛奶 (cow's milk), 奶奶 (paternal grandmother), and 奶茶 (milk tea)

Definition: Woman, especially a married woman or wife. Often used in formal or compound words relating to women.
Usage: Common in words like 妇女 (women), 主妇 (housewife), 夫妇 (married couple)

Definition: A hole, opening, or aperture in an object. Also refers to Confucius (as a surname) in classical contexts.
Usage: Common in words like 孔洞 (hole/cavity) and 毛孔 (pore); also in 孔子 (Confucius)

Definition: To live, reside, or dwell in a place; to occupy a position or status.
Usage: Common in words like 居住 (to reside), 居民 (resident), and 居然 (unexpectedly)

Definition: Mountain or hill; a natural elevation of the earth's surface.
Usage: Common in place names and compound words like 山上 (on the mountain) or 爬山 (to climb a mountain)

Definition: A mat or seat; also used as a measure word for banquets, feasts, or席位 (seats at formal gatherings).
Usage: Common in words like 出席 (attend), 主席 (chairman), and 酒席 (banquet)

Definition: A measure word used for counting paintings, scrolls, cloth, and other flat rectangular items; also means width or extent.
Usage: Common in phrases like 一幅画 (a painting) or 幅度 (range, extent)

Definition: Bent, curved, or crooked; can also mean to bend or curve something. Describes anything that is not straight, from roads to objects.
Usage: Common in words like 弯路 (curved road), 转弯 (turn/make a turn), 弯腰 (bend over)

Definition: A path, trail, or small road; also refers to diameter in geometry or a direct route/way of doing something.
Usage: Common in words like 小径 (small path), 直径 (diameter), and 径直 (directly)

Definition: To remember, recall, or think back on past events or experiences
Usage: Commonly used in words like 回忆 (huíyì - to recall/memory) and 记忆 (jìyì - memory)

Definition: To resent, blame, or hold a grudge against someone; to complain about unfair treatment or misfortune.
Usage: Common in words like 抱怨 (bàoyuàn - to complain) and 怨恨 (yuànhèn - resentment)

Definition: To restore, recover, or return to a previous state. Most commonly seen in the word 恢复 (huīfù), meaning to restore or resume.
Usage: Typically used in compound words like 恢复健康 (recover health) or 恢复正常 (return to normal)

Definition: War, battle, or fight; to fight or engage in combat. Also means to tremble or shiver (from fear or cold).
Usage: Common in words like 战争 (war), 战斗 (battle), 挑战 (challenge)

Definition: To turn (a corner); to kidnap or abduct someone, especially children. Also refers to a crutch or walking stick.
Usage: Common in directions like 拐弯 (turn a corner) and warnings about 拐卖 (human trafficking)

Definition: To pull out, pull up, or extract something from where it is fixed or embedded, often with force.
Usage: Common in phrases like 拔牙 (pull a tooth), 拔草 (pull weeds), 拔河 (tug of war)

Definition: Fist; a clenched hand. Also refers to martial arts techniques or boxing.
Usage: Common in words like 拳头 (fist), 太极拳 (Tai Chi), and 拳击 (boxing)

Definition: To hug or embrace someone with your arms; to hold someone close
Usage: Commonly used for physical affection like 搂着 (holding in arms) or 搂抱 (to embrace)

Definition: To rub, stroke, or touch lightly with the hand; to scrape or graze against something.
Usage: Commonly seen in compounds like 摩擦 (friction), 按摩 (massage), and 摩托车 (motorcycle)

Definition: Spacious, wide open, or uncovered; describes a place or space that is broad and unobstructed.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 敞开 (to open wide) and 宽敞 (spacious)

Definition: Old, used, or worn out; refers to things that have existed for a long time or are no longer new. Can also mean former or past when describing relationships or situations.
Usage: Common in phrases like 旧书 (old book), 旧朋友 (old friend), 旧衣服 (old clothes)

Definition: Power, authority, or right to do something. Also refers to权利 (rights) and 权力 (power/authority) in legal and political contexts.
Usage: Common in words like 人权 (human rights), 权力 (power), 权利 (rights), 有权 (have the right to)

Definition: A branch or twig of a tree or plant; also used as a measure word for long, thin objects like flowers, pens, or candles.
Usage: Common in phrases like 树枝 (tree branch) or as a counter in 一枝花 (one flower/stem)

Definition: A frame, border, or box that surrounds or contains something. Can also mean to frame or enclose something.
Usage: Common in words like 框架 (framework), 相框 (picture frame), 框子 (frame/box), and 方框 (square box)

Definition: Plum or plum blossom; refers to the plum tree, its fruit, or its flowers which are an important symbol in Chinese culture.
Usage: Commonly seen in names, poetry, and phrases like 梅花 (plum blossom)

Definition: Poison or toxin; something harmful or deadly that can cause injury or death. Can also mean cruel, vicious, or malicious.
Usage: Common in words like 中毒 (poisoned), 毒品 (drugs), 病毒 (virus)

Definition: Sand or sandy; refers to small granular particles found on beaches, deserts, or riverbeds.
Usage: Common in words like 沙滩 (beach), 沙漠 (desert), and 沙发 (sofa - phonetic borrowing)

Definition: Ocean or sea; also means foreign or Western (especially in historical contexts)
Usage: Common in words like 海洋 (ocean), 洋人 (foreigner), 太平洋 (Pacific Ocean)

Definition: Lake; a large body of water surrounded by land.
Usage: Common in place names like 西湖 (West Lake) and compound words like 湖泊 (lakes)

Definition: To spread or overflow; to be all over or everywhere. Also means unrestrained, free, or casual.
Usage: Common in words like 漫画 (manga/comics), 浪漫 (romantic), and 漫长 (very long)

Definition: Rotten, spoiled, or decayed; also means broken, worn out, or of poor quality. Can describe food that has gone bad or things that are badly done or falling apart.
Usage: Common in phrases like 烂了 (has rotted/broken), 烂苹果 (rotten apple), or 太烂了 (it's terrible/awful)

Definition: Pig or hog; a common domesticated farm animal raised for meat.
Usage: Used in words like 猪肉 (pork) and appears in the Chinese zodiac as one of the twelve animals

Definition: Very, extremely; to an excessive degree. Also means 'what' or 'why' in classical Chinese.
Usage: Commonly seen in formal or literary expressions like 甚至 (even), 甚好 (very good)

Definition: Thin, skinny, or lean; describes a person or animal with little body fat, or meat with little fat.
Usage: Commonly used to describe body type (她很瘦 - she is thin) or meat quality (瘦肉 - lean meat)

Definition: To glance at or catch a glimpse of something briefly; to look quickly at something out of the corner of one's eye.
Usage: Commonly used in the phrase 瞥见 (piē jiàn) meaning 'to catch sight of' or 瞥一眼 (piē yī yǎn) meaning 'to take a quick glance'

Definition: An onomatopoeia representing a loud bang, thud, or crashing sound, similar to 'bang' or 'boom' in English.
Usage: Commonly used to describe sounds of explosions, doors slamming, or objects hitting hard surfaces, as in 砰的一声 (with a bang)

Definition: Hard, stiff, or firm in texture or quality; opposite of soft. Can also mean tough, strong-willed, or forceful when describing attitudes or actions.
Usage: Common in phrases like 硬币 (hard currency/coin), 坚硬 (hard/solid), or 硬要 (insist on)

Definition: A branch of study, department, or subject area; also refers to a category or division in classification systems.
Usage: Common in academic contexts like 科学 (science), 学科 (academic subject), or 外科 (surgery department)

Definition: To shrink, contract, or withdraw; to become smaller or pull back in size or extent.
Usage: Common in words like 缩小 (to reduce/shrink), 收缩 (to contract), and 退缩 (to retreat/withdraw)

Definition: Wing or fin of a bird, insect, or fish; the appendage used for flying or swimming.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 翅膀 (chìbǎng, wing) and 鸡翅 (jīchì, chicken wing)

Definition: Solemn, serious, or respectful; also means to eliminate or purge (in formal contexts)
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 严肃 (serious/solemn) and 肃静 (quiet and respectful)

Definition: A pointed tip or awn (the bristle-like extension on grain); also refers to mango fruit in compounds.
Usage: Commonly seen in 芒果 (mángguǒ - mango) and 光芒 (guāngmáng - rays of light)

Definition: A character referring to the lotus flower or hibiscus flower, primarily used in literary or poetic contexts.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the compound word 芙蓉 (furong, lotus/hibiscus) or in names

Definition: Bitter in taste; also means suffering, hardship, or painful experiences.
Usage: Used to describe bitter flavors (苦瓜 bitter melon) or difficult situations (辛苦 hard work, 痛苦 painful)

Definition: Describes something vast, boundless, or unclear; conveys a sense of being lost or confused in a vast space.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 茫茫 (boundless), 迷茫 (confused/lost), and 茫然 (at a loss)

Definition: Means wild, desolate, or barren, describing uncultivated land or wasteland. Also means absurd or ridiculous when describing ideas or situations.
Usage: Common in words like 荒地 (wasteland), 荒谬 (absurd), and 饥荒 (famine)

Definition: Refers to the hibiscus flower; also commonly used as a poetic name for the city of Chengdu (成都, known as 'Rong City').
Usage: Often appears in place names, personal names, and classical poetry

Definition: Spider. This character is almost always used in the compound word 蜘蛛 (zhīzhū), meaning spider.
Usage: Rarely used alone; typically appears in 蜘蛛 (spider) or 蜘蛛网 (spider web)

Definition: A character component meaning spider, used almost exclusively in the compound word 蜘蛛 (zhīzhū), which means spider.
Usage: Rarely used alone; appears in 蜘蛛 (spider) and related terms like 蜘蛛网 (spider web)

Definition: To mend, repair, or patch something; to supplement or make up for a deficiency.
Usage: Common in words like 补习 (tutoring/make-up classes), 补充 (to supplement), and 弥补 (to remedy)

Definition: Words, speech, or something that is said. In modern Chinese, it is mainly used in formal or literary contexts and in compound words.
Usage: Common in words like 语言 (language), 发言 (to speak/make a statement), 名言 (famous saying)

Definition: To ask for, beg, or demand something; also means to invite or provoke (often negative consequences).
Usage: Common in words like 讨厌 (tǎoyàn - annoying/to dislike) and 讨论 (tǎolùn - to discuss)

Definition: To transfer, move, or shift (someone or something to a different place or position); to adjust or regulate settings.
Usage: Common in contexts like 调动 (transfer personnel), 调整 (adjust/modify), or 强调 (emphasize)

Definition: To be defeated, to lose, or to fail in a competition, battle, or endeavor. Can also mean to decay or spoil.
Usage: Common in words like 失败 (to fail), 打败 (to defeat), and 败坏 (to ruin)

Definition: To choose, select, or pick from among options or alternatives. Also means to elect someone to a position.
Usage: Common in phrases like 选择 (to choose), 选手 (contestant), and 选举 (election)

Definition: To hear or to smell; also means news or reputation. This versatile verb covers both auditory and olfactory perception.
Usage: Common in phrases like 新闻 (news), 闻名 (famous/well-known), and 听闻 (to hear of)

Definition: To block, hinder, or obstruct something from happening or moving forward. It means to prevent or stop progress or movement.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 阻止 (to prevent), 阻碍 (to hinder), and 阻挡 (to block)

Definition: To descend, fall, or drop; to lower or reduce something. Commonly used to describe decreasing levels, prices, temperatures, or standards.
Usage: Found in words like 下降 (to decline), 降低 (to reduce), 降温 (temperature drop)

Definition: Prosperous, grand, or thriving; also describes a loud rumbling sound. Often used to convey abundance, magnificence, or deep booming noises.
Usage: Common in words like 隆重 (grand/solemn), 兴隆 (prosperous), and 轰隆 (rumbling sound)

Definition: To gather, collect, or assemble together; also used as a measure word for sets, collections, or episodes of TV shows and books.
Usage: Common in words like 收集 (collect), 集合 (gather/assemble), and counting episodes like 第一集 (episode 1)

Definition: Face or facial appearance; also means color or countenance. Often used in literary or formal contexts to refer to one's face or complexion.
Usage: Common in words like 颜色 (yánsè - color) and 容颜 (róngyán - face/appearance)

Definition: To replace, substitute, or act on behalf of someone; also refers to a generation or historical period/era.
Usage: Common in words like 代表 (represent), 现代 (modern era), 古代 (ancient times), and 一代 (one generation)

Definition: Price or value of something. Most commonly seen in the word 价格 (jiàgé, price) and compounds related to cost.
Usage: Used in expressions like 价钱 (price), 物价 (commodity prices), 降价 (reduce price)

Definition: The number five in formal or financial contexts, used to prevent alteration on checks and official documents. Also used as a surname and in military terms meaning 'squad' or 'team of five'.
Usage: Commonly seen on receipts, contracts, and currency to write '5' (instead of 五)

Definition: Excellent, superior, or outstanding; indicates high quality or being better than others.
Usage: Common in words like 优秀 (excellent), 优点 (advantage/merit), and 优先 (priority)

Definition: Side or flank of something; can also mean to incline or lean to one side.
Usage: Common in words like 侧面 (side view), 左侧 (left side), 右侧 (right side)
