Definition: To store, save, or reserve something for future use; to accumulate or stockpile.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 储存 (to store), 储蓄 (to save money), and 储备 (reserves/stockpile)

Definition: Proud or arrogant; describes someone who has an excessively high opinion of themselves or shows disdain toward others.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 骄傲 (proud), 傲慢 (arrogant), and 高傲 (haughty)

Definition: Clean or pure; also means 'only' or 'nothing but' when describing something exclusively. Can also mean 'net' (as in net weight or net profit).
Usage: Common in words like 干净 (clean), 净重 (net weight), or 净说 (only talk/do nothing but talk)

Definition: To congeal, condense, or solidify; to concentrate or focus (attention, gaze, etc.)
Usage: Common in words like 凝视 (to gaze intently), 凝固 (to solidify), and 凝聚 (to condense/unite)

Definition: Power, force, or momentum; also refers to a situation, trend, or influential position. Commonly describes the strength or势态 (state/tendency) of something.
Usage: Found in words like 趋势 (trend), 优势 (advantage), 形势 (situation), and 势力 (power/influence)

Definition: To divine or predict the future using ancient fortune-telling methods; also a surname.
Usage: Mainly seen in compound words like 占卜 (zhānbǔ - divination) or as a family name

Definition: To roll up or curl; also refers to a roll, scroll, or volume of something (like a test paper or book).
Usage: Common in words like 试卷 (test paper), 卷起 (to roll up), and 卷发 (curly hair)

Definition: A fork or any pronged tool; also means to cross or intersect in an X-shape.
Usage: Common in words like 叉子 (fork) and 交叉 (to intersect)

Definition: History or historical records; can also refer to a historian or official recorder in ancient China.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 历史 (lìshǐ - history), 史书 (shǐshū - history book), and 史前 (shǐqián - prehistoric)

Definition: To take charge of or manage; a department or division. Also used as a component in words related to companies, drivers, and officials.
Usage: Commonly seen in compounds like 公司 (gōngsī - company), 司机 (sījī - driver), and 上司 (shàngsī - boss)

Definition: To blow (air from the mouth) or to play a wind instrument. Can also mean to boast or brag in informal contexts.
Usage: Common in phrases like 吹风 (wind blows), 吹笛子 (play the flute), or 吹牛 (to brag)

Definition: Lip, the fleshy outer part of the mouth. Used in both literal anatomical contexts and figurative expressions.
Usage: Common in words like 嘴唇 (zuǐchún, lips) and 唇膏 (chúngāo, lipstick)

Definition: An onomatopoeia that represents a buzzing, humming, or droning sound, like that made by bees, machinery, or engines.
Usage: Commonly used to describe continuous low-pitched sounds, as in 嗡嗡声 (buzzing sound)

Definition: A device, tool, instrument, or container used for a specific purpose. Often appears as a suffix in compound words to indicate various types of equipment or utensils.
Usage: Common in words like 武器 (weapon), 机器 (machine), 乐器 (musical instrument), 容器 (container)

Definition: An onomatopoeia describing a sharp cracking or splitting sound, like wood breaking or lightning striking.
Usage: Almost always used in the compound 噼啪 (pī pā) or the four-character phrase 噼里啪啦 (pī li pā lā) to describe crackling sounds

Definition: Garden, park, or yard; a place where plants are grown or people gather for recreation.
Usage: Common in words like 公园 (park), 花园 (garden), 幼儿园 (kindergarten)

Definition: A circle, ring, or loop; can also mean to draw a circle around something or to enclose.
Usage: Used for circular shapes (圆圈 circle) or social groups (朋友圈 friend circle/social network)

Definition: A flat, level piece of ground or open space; also used as a measure word for area (especially in Taiwan, equivalent to approximately 3.3 square meters).
Usage: Common in compound words like 草坪 (lawn), 停车坪 (parking lot), or when discussing property size in Taiwan

Definition: Foundation, base, or basis of something; the fundamental part upon which other things are built or developed.
Usage: Commonly used in compound words like 基础 (foundation), 基本 (basic/fundamental), and 基地 (base/headquarters)

Definition: Ink, especially traditional Chinese ink used for calligraphy and painting. Can also refer to something black or dark in color.
Usage: Common in words like 墨水 (ink), 笔墨 (pen and ink/writing), and 墨西哥 (Mexico)

Definition: Summer, the hottest season of the year. Also used as a surname and in the name of the ancient Xia Dynasty.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 夏天 (summer) and 夏季 (summer season)

Definition: To examine, investigate, or review carefully; to put on trial or judge.
Usage: Commonly used in legal contexts (审判 trial, 审查 examine) and formal review processes

Definition: A screen or partition used to divide space or block views; also refers to display screens like computer or phone screens.
Usage: Common in words like 屏幕 (screen), 屏风 (folding screen), 荧屏 (TV screen)

Definition: Secluded, quiet, or dim; describes places that are hidden, dark, or remote from activity.
Usage: Common in words like 幽默 (humor), 幽静 (quiet and secluded), 幽暗 (dim and dark)

Definition: Loyal, faithful, or devoted; refers to unwavering allegiance and dedication to a person, cause, or duty.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 忠诚 (loyal), 忠心 (faithful heart), and 忠实 (devoted)

Definition: To worry, be anxious, or feel concerned about something. Expresses a state of mental distress or unease about potential problems.
Usage: Often appears in compounds like 忧虑 (worry), 担忧 (be concerned), or 忧愁 (melancholy)

Definition: To pity, feel compassion for, or show mercy toward someone or something. Expresses sympathy or tender feelings for those who are suffering or in a difficult situation.
Usage: Often seen in literary contexts and compounds like 可怜 (kělián - pitiful, poor thing)

Definition: To hate or to resent; a strong feeling of dislike or hostility toward someone or something.
Usage: Often used in expressions like 恨他 (hate him) or 仇恨 (hatred)

Definition: To be pleased, delighted, or happy; to bring joy or satisfaction to someone.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 喜悦 (joy), 愉悦 (pleasant), and 悦耳 (pleasant to the ear)

Definition: To be cautious, alert, or vigilant; to guard against potential danger or problems.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the word 警惕 (jǐngtì - to be vigilant/alert)

Definition: To be accustomed to or used to something; to spoil someone (especially a child) through indulgence
Usage: Common in phrases like 习惯 (habit), 惯了 (gotten used to), or 惯坏 (to spoil)

Definition: To be flustered, nervous, or panicked; feeling anxious and losing composure in a stressful situation.
Usage: Commonly used in expressions like 慌张 (flustered), 恐慌 (panic), or 不要慌 (don't panic)

Definition: To regret or feel remorse; a feeling of disappointment or dissatisfaction about something that cannot be changed.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the word 遗憾 (yíhàn, regret/pity) and formal written contexts

Definition: To pull or tug; to chat or talk casually. In colloquial usage, it also means to talk nonsense or make something up.
Usage: Common in phrases like 扯淡 (to talk nonsense) and 闲扯 (to chat idly)

Definition: To break, snap, or fold something; also means a discount or reduction in price.
Usage: Common in shopping contexts like 打折 (dǎzhé - to give a discount) and physical actions like 折断 (zhéduàn - to break off)

Definition: To gently stroke, caress, or comfort with the hand; to soothe or console someone emotionally.
Usage: Often used in contexts like 抚摸 (to stroke/caress) or 安抚 (to comfort/pacify)

Definition: To recruit, to hire, or to attract; also means to beckon or wave (as a gesture). Can also refer to a move or trick in martial arts or strategy.
Usage: Common in words like 招聘 (recruit/hire), 招手 (wave hand), 招待 (receive guests)

Definition: To pick up or gather something from the ground; also the formal/financial form of the number ten (10) used in documents to prevent fraud.
Usage: Common in phrases like 拾起 (pick up) and on receipts/checks as the complex form of 十

Definition: To block, obstruct, or stop something from passing through; to ward off or keep out.
Usage: Common in phrases like 挡住 (to block), 阻挡 (to obstruct), or 挡风 (to block the wind)

Definition: To explore, investigate, or search for something; to visit or look into a matter.
Usage: Common in words like 探索 (explore), 探望 (visit someone), and 探讨 (discuss/investigate)

Definition: To insert, stick in, or plug something into something else. Can refer to physical insertion like plugging in a device or placing flowers in a vase.
Usage: Common in words like 插座 (electrical outlet), 插花 (flower arrangement), 插入 (to insert)

Definition: To save, rescue, or help someone in danger or difficulty.
Usage: Common in emergency contexts like 救命 (save a life, help!) or 救人 (rescue someone)

Definition: Violent, fierce, or sudden; can also mean to expose or reveal something suddenly.
Usage: Common in words like 暴力 (violence), 暴雨 (rainstorm), and 暴露 (to expose)

Definition: To replace, substitute for, or do something on behalf of someone else; to take the place of.
Usage: Common in phrases like 替我 (for me/on my behalf) or 替换 (to replace)

Definition: Outstanding, exceptional, or distinguished; refers to a person of remarkable talent or achievement.
Usage: Commonly used in names and phrases like 英杰 (hero/outstanding person) or 杰出 (outstanding/excellent)

Definition: A pillow; a cushion used to support the head while sleeping or resting.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 枕头 (zhěntou, pillow) and can also be used as a verb meaning 'to rest one's head on'

Definition: A bucket, barrel, or pail; a cylindrical container used for holding liquids or other materials.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 水桶 (water bucket), 垃圾桶 (trash can), or as a measure word for bucket-loads

Definition: The color brown; refers to a brownish or tan color similar to palm tree fibers.
Usage: Commonly used in 棕色 (brown color) and 棕熊 (brown bear)

Definition: A song or melody; can also be used as a verb meaning 'to sing'.
Usage: Common in words like 唱歌 (to sing), 歌手 (singer), and 国歌 (national anthem)

Definition: A blanket or rug; a piece of thick fabric used for warmth or as floor covering.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 毛毯 (máotǎn, blanket) and 地毯 (dìtǎn, carpet/rug)

Definition: To ask for, request, or seek something; to beg or plead for help or favor.
Usage: Common in words like 请求 (to request), 要求 (to demand), and 求助 (to ask for help)

Definition: Refers to the Han Chinese people (the largest ethnic group in China) or the Han Dynasty. Also used as a component meaning 'Chinese' in compound words.
Usage: Common in words like 汉语 (Chinese language), 汉字 (Chinese characters), and 汉族 (Han ethnicity)

Definition: Wet, damp, or moist. Describes something that contains water or moisture.
Usage: Common in weather descriptions and everyday situations like 湿衣服 (wet clothes) or 潮湿 (humid/damp)

Definition: Fox; a wild canine animal known for being cunning and clever in Chinese culture.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the word 狐狸 (húli, fox) and idioms like 狐狸精 (fox spirit)

Definition: An archaic or rare character referring to a type of wild cat or feline animal found in historical Chinese texts.
Usage: Rarely used in modern Chinese; primarily appears in classical literature or specialized zoological contexts

Definition: A character meaning glass, used primarily in the compound word 玻璃 (bōli).
Usage: Rarely used alone; almost always appears in 玻璃 (glass) as in 玻璃杯 (glass cup) or 玻璃窗 (glass window)

Definition: A type of colored glaze or glass; refers to a lustrous, glass-like material.
Usage: Almost always appears in the compound word 玻璃 (bōli) meaning 'glass', or 琉璃 (liúli) meaning 'glazed tile' or 'colored glaze'

Definition: To draw or paint; a picture, painting, or drawing. As a verb, it means to create images with a pen, pencil, or brush.
Usage: Common in phrases like 画画 (to draw/paint) and 一幅画 (a painting)

Definition: A mark, trace, or scar left behind by something, such as a wound, stain, or impression.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 伤痕 (scar/wound mark), 痕迹 (trace/mark), 泪痕 (tear stains)

Definition: The number one hundred (100). Also used to mean 'numerous' or 'all kinds of' in certain expressions.
Usage: Common in numbers like 一百 (one hundred), 三百 (three hundred), and phrases like 百姓 (common people)

Definition: To pay attention to or acknowledge someone; to take notice of or respond to someone.
Usage: Most commonly used in negative form 不睬 (bù cǎi) meaning 'to ignore' or 'to not pay attention to'

Definition: Short in length, height, or duration; the opposite of 长 (long).
Usage: Used to describe physical length (短裤 shorts), time periods (短期 short-term), or height (他很短 he is short)

Definition: To show or display; elegant, beautiful, or excellent. Also commonly used in modern Chinese to mean 'show' (as in a performance or display).
Usage: Found in words like 时装秀 (fashion show), 优秀 (excellent), and 秀丽 (beautiful/elegant)

Definition: To exhaust, use up completely, or drain dry; to do one's utmost or best effort.
Usage: Commonly seen in formal expressions like 竭尽全力 (do one's utmost) and 枯竭 (dried up/exhausted)

Definition: To introduce or to carry on; to continue or inherit something from the past.
Usage: Most commonly seen in 介绍 (jièshào - to introduce) and place names like 绍兴 (Shàoxīng)

Definition: Thread, clue, or train of thought; most commonly refers to emotions, feelings, or state of mind.
Usage: Frequently appears in compounds like 情绪 (qíngxù - emotions/mood) and 思绪 (sīxù - train of thought)

Definition: To burst open or split; most commonly used to describe flowers blooming or smiles appearing on faces.
Usage: Frequently seen in expressions like 绽放 (zhànfàng, to bloom) and 绽开笑容 (zhànkāi xiàoróng, to break into a smile)

Definition: Slow, gradual, or unhurried; to postpone or delay something. Often describes a gentle, relaxed pace or the act of easing tension.
Usage: Common in words like 缓慢 (slow), 缓解 (to relieve/ease), and 延缓 (to postpone)

Definition: Beautiful or pretty; also means America (short for 美国/Měiguó)
Usage: Used to describe attractive things or people, and commonly appears in words related to the United States

Definition: To unite, join, or connect together; to form an alliance or association.
Usage: Common in words like 联系 (contact/connection), 联合 (unite), and 联盟 (alliance)

Definition: Smelly, stinky, or having a bad odor; can also mean bad reputation or poor quality in a figurative sense.
Usage: Commonly used to describe unpleasant smells like 臭豆腐 (stinky tofu) or to criticize something as terrible

Definition: To send, deliver, or convey (greetings, regards, or messages); to cause or bring about a result.
Usage: Commonly seen in formal expressions like 致辞 (deliver a speech), 致敬 (pay respects), 导致 (lead to/cause)

Definition: A formal or literary word meaning 'if' or 'as if', used to express conditions or comparisons. Also means 'like' or 'such as' when comparing things.
Usage: Common in written Chinese and set phrases like 若是 (if), 假若 (supposing), 宛若 (as if)

Definition: To swing or sway back and forth; to wash away or cleanse thoroughly.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 荡秋千 (to swing on a swing) and 扫荡 (to sweep away/mop up)

Definition: The stem or calyx of a flower or fruit; the part that connects the fruit or flower to the plant.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 瓜蒂 (melon stem), 花蒂 (flower calyx), and 根深蒂固 (deep-rooted)

Definition: Bee or wasp; a flying insect that produces honey or has a stinger.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 蜜蜂 (mìfēng, honeybee) and 黄蜂 (huángfēng, wasp)

Definition: A toad; specifically refers to toads in Chinese, particularly in the compound word 蟾蜍 (chánchú).
Usage: Rarely used alone; almost always appears in the word 蟾蜍 (toad)

Definition: A toad, specifically referring to the Chinese toad or moon toad in traditional culture. Often appears in the compound word 蟾蜍 (chánchú) meaning toad.
Usage: Commonly used in literary or poetic contexts, and frequently associated with the moon in Chinese mythology (蟾宫 - moon palace)

Definition: To ridicule, mock, or satirize someone or something in a critical way.
Usage: Commonly seen in compounds like 讥笑 (jīxiào - to sneer at) and 讥讽 (jīfěng - to satirize)

Definition: A word or term in language; also refers to a type of classical Chinese poetry form (ci poetry).
Usage: Commonly seen in compounds like 词汇 (vocabulary), 生词 (new word), 单词 (word)

Definition: Detailed, thorough, or comprehensive. Often used to describe information, explanations, or descriptions that are complete and specific.
Usage: Common in words like 详细 (detailed), 详情 (details), and 详述 (to elaborate)

Definition: Chaste, virtuous, or loyal, especially referring to moral integrity and fidelity in traditional Chinese culture. Often describes steadfast character or unwavering principles.
Usage: Commonly seen in classical texts and names, such as 贞洁 (chastity) or 坚贞 (steadfast/loyal)

Definition: To step across, stride over, or cross from one side to another; also means to span or extend across (time, space, or boundaries).
Usage: Common in words like 跨越 (to cross over), 跨国 (cross-border/international), and 跨年 (spanning the new year)

Definition: To jump up or leap suddenly; to shoot up rapidly (often describing sudden upward movement or rapid increase in prices, flames, etc.)
Usage: Commonly used for sudden movements like 火苗蹿起来 (flames shoot up) or 价格蹿升 (prices skyrocket)

Definition: To bow or bend one's body; one's own body or person (formal/literary usage)
Usage: Commonly seen in formal expressions like 鞠躬 (to bow) and 事必躬亲 (to attend to everything personally)

Definition: Soft, flexible, or not hard to the touch; can also mean weak or gentle in character or manner.
Usage: Common in describing textures (软床 soft bed), food (软面包 soft bread), or personality traits (心软 soft-hearted)

Definition: To return or go back to a previous place or state; to give back something.
Usage: Common in words like 返回 (return/go back) and 往返 (round trip)

Definition: To leave behind, lose, or omit something; also means something left behind by predecessors or from the past.
Usage: Common in words like 遗忘 (to forget), 遗憾 (regret), 遗产 (inheritance/heritage)

Definition: A lock (noun) or to lock (verb). Refers to a device that secures doors, boxes, or other objects, or the action of securing something with a lock.
Usage: Common in phrases like 锁门 (lock the door) or 开锁 (unlock)

Definition: Sun, sunshine, or the bright/warm side; also represents the yang principle in Chinese philosophy (masculine, positive, light energy as opposed to yin)
Usage: Common in words like 太阳 (sun), 阳光 (sunshine), and 阴阳 (yin and yang)

Definition: Means 'in advance' or 'beforehand'; indicates something done or planned ahead of time.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 预习 (preview/prepare lessons), 预定 (reserve/book), and 预报 (forecast)

Definition: Wind; moving air in the atmosphere. Also refers to style, manner, or customs in extended meanings.
Usage: Common in weather expressions like 刮风 (windy) and compound words like 风景 (scenery)

Definition: Black or dark in color; also refers to a crow or raven.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 乌鸦 (crow) and 乌云 (dark clouds)

Definition: To practice, study, or review something repeatedly in order to learn it well. Also means habit or custom.
Usage: Most commonly seen in 学习 (to study/learn) and 练习 (to practice)

Definition: Prefix meaning 'Asia' or 'second/inferior to'. Most commonly used in compound words related to the Asian continent.
Usage: Found in words like 亚洲 (Asia), 东亚 (East Asia), and 亚军 (runner-up/second place)

Definition: To die, perish, or lose; to flee or escape. Often used in formal or literary contexts to mean death, destruction, or loss of a nation or dynasty.
Usage: Common in words like 死亡 (death), 灭亡 (perish/destruction), 亡国 (fallen nation), and 逃亡 (flee/escape)

Definition: A colloquial term for a man or fellow, often used in regional dialects. Can also refer to people from specific regions or occupations when combined with other characters.
Usage: Common in compounds like 老佬 (old fellow), 阔佬 (rich man), or 广东佬 (Cantonese person)

Definition: Stiff, rigid, or frozen in position; unable to move or bend. Can describe physical stiffness or a deadlocked situation.
Usage: Common in words like 僵硬 (stiff/rigid) and 僵局 (deadlock/stalemate)

Definition: To divide, to delimit, or to transfer (money/resources); to mark boundaries or allocate something into categories.
Usage: Common in words like 划分 (to divide), 计划 (plan), and 划算 (worthwhile)

Definition: A conjunction meaning 'then' or 'in that case' that shows consequence or contrast between clauses. Also used in formal writing to mean 'rule' or 'regulation' as a noun.
Usage: Common in if-then statements like 有志者事竟成，无志者则一事无成 (those with ambition succeed, those without then achieve nothing)

Definition: A measure word for medicines, drugs, or chemical preparations; also means dose or dosage.
Usage: Commonly used in compounds like 药剂 (medicine/pharmaceutical), 洗涤剂 (detergent), 消毒剂 (disinfectant)

Definition: A seal or stamp used for official purposes; also means to print or imprint something.
Usage: Common in words like 印章 (seal/stamp), 打印 (to print), and 印象 (impression)

Definition: To betray, rebel against, or turn against someone or something, especially authority or one's country/group.
Usage: Common in words like 叛徒 (traitor), 背叛 (to betray), 叛乱 (rebellion)

Definition: Number, date, or size designation; commonly used for dates (day of the month), house numbers, sizes, and sequential numbering.
Usage: Used in expressions like 三号 (the 3rd day), 电话号码 (phone number), 大号 (large size)

Definition: To swallow (food, liquid, or saliva); also refers to the throat or pharynx as a body part.
Usage: Commonly used in medical contexts or when describing the action of swallowing, as in 咽下 (to swallow down)

Definition: An onomatopoeia that represents a loud crashing, banging, or clanging sound, like metal hitting metal or something heavy falling.
Usage: Often used in written Chinese to describe sudden, loud metallic or impact sounds, such as 哐当 (kuāngdāng)

Definition: Older brother; also used as a respectful term to address young men who are older than you or of similar age.
Usage: Used in family contexts (哥哥 - older brother) and as a friendly or respectful form of address

Definition: To spit or saliva/spit (the substance). This character refers both to the act of spitting and the saliva itself.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 唾液 (saliva) and 唾弃 (to despise/reject with contempt)

Definition: To smell or sniff something, typically by using the nose to detect odors or scents.
Usage: Often used for animals sniffing or people deliberately smelling something, as in 嗅觉 (sense of smell) or 狗在嗅地面 (the dog is sniffing the ground)

Definition: An onomatopoeia that represents the sound of air or liquid bursting out, like a puff, spray, or spurt.
Usage: Commonly used to describe laughing sounds (噗哧 pūchī - giggling) or things popping/spraying

Definition: To shout, yell, or make a loud noise; to create a commotion or disturbance by speaking loudly.
Usage: Often used to describe noisy arguing or complaining, as in 大声嚷嚷 (to shout loudly)

Definition: A bag, sack, or pouch; something shaped like a bag or pocket.
Usage: Often appears in compound words like 胶囊 (capsule), 皮囊 (skin/body), or 囊括 (to include everything)

Definition: Sleepy or tired; can also mean to trap or surround, or to be in difficulty.
Usage: Most commonly used to express sleepiness (我很困 - I'm very sleepy) or being trapped in a difficult situation

Definition: Means 'solid', 'firm', or 'fixed'; also used to mean 'stubborn' or 'persistently'. Can function as an adverb meaning 'of course' or 'admittedly' in formal contexts.
Usage: Common in words like 固定 (fixed/regular), 固体 (solid), and 顽固 (stubborn)

Definition: A grave or tomb; a burial site where a deceased person is laid to rest.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 墓地 (cemetery) and 坟墓 (grave/tomb)

Definition: Evening or dusk; the time when the sun is setting. This character depicts the moon or sunset and represents the evening time of day.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 夕阳 (setting sun) and 除夕 (New Year's Eve)

Definition: A reward, prize, or award given for achievement or excellence; can also be used as a verb meaning 'to reward' or 'to award'.
Usage: Common in words like 奖金 (bonus), 得奖 (win a prize), 奖励 (reward)

Definition: Wife; a married woman in relation to her spouse.
Usage: Formal term used in compounds like 妻子 (qīzi, wife) or 夫妻 (fūqī, husband and wife)

Definition: Elder sister or a respectful term for a young woman slightly older than oneself. Can be used alone or in compounds like 姐姐 (jiějie, older sister).
Usage: Used as a family term or polite address for women, such as 大姐 (eldest sister) or 小姐 (miss)

Definition: Ginger, a common cooking spice and ingredient in Chinese cuisine. Also used as a Chinese surname.
Usage: Found in cooking contexts like 生姜 (fresh ginger) and in names

Definition: To flatter, fawn over, or try to please someone in an ingratiating way; to charm or be charming (often with negative connotation of being overly flattering).
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 谄媚 (chǎnmèi - to flatter), 媚俗 (mèisú - to pander to vulgar tastes), and 妩媚 (wǔmèi - charming, seductive)

Definition: A formal feast, banquet, or dinner party, typically held for special occasions or to entertain guests.
Usage: Common in words like 宴会 (banquet), 晚宴 (dinner party), and 酒宴 (drinking feast)

Definition: Dust or dirt; fine particles of matter that settle on surfaces or float in the air.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 灰尘 (huīchén - dust) and 尘土 (chéntǔ - dust and dirt)

Definition: A corpse or dead body. This character is also commonly used as a radical component in other Chinese characters.
Usage: Often seen in compound words like 尸体 (shītǐ, corpse) and as a radical in characters related to the body or dwelling

Definition: Fortune, luck, or happiness; also means 'fortunately' or 'luckily'. Conveys the sense of being blessed or experiencing good fortune.
Usage: Common in words like 幸福 (happiness), 幸运 (lucky), and 幸好 (fortunately)

Definition: Style, type, or form; a pattern or model of something. Often used as a suffix to indicate a particular style or system.
Usage: Common in compound words like 中式 (Chinese-style), 正式 (formal), 方式 (method/way)

Definition: To lead, guide, or draw someone/something in a particular direction; to cause or trigger something to happen.
Usage: Common in words like 引起 (to cause/trigger), 引导 (to guide), and 吸引 (to attract)

Definition: To fill, spread, or permeate; to become more intense or extensive. Often used in literary or formal contexts to describe something that fills a space or becomes widespread.
Usage: Common in words like 弥漫 (to fill the air/permeate) and 弥补 (to make up for/remedy)

Definition: Weak, feeble, or inferior in strength, ability, or quality. Describes physical weakness, poor performance, or disadvantaged position.
Usage: Common in phrases like 弱点 (weakness), 强弱 (strong and weak), 弱小 (weak and small)

Definition: Favor, benefit, or kindness; often used in formal contexts to describe special discounts or gracious acts.
Usage: Common in business terms like 优惠 (discount/preferential treatment) and polite expressions like 惠顾 (your patronage)

Definition: To fear or be afraid of something; to feel dread or terror about a situation or outcome.
Usage: Often used in formal or written contexts, commonly seen in compounds like 恐惧 (kǒngjù - fear) and 畏惧 (wèijù - to be afraid of)

Definition: Foolish, stupid, or ignorant. This character describes someone who lacks wisdom or intelligence.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 愚蠢 (yúchǔn - foolish) and 愚人 (yúrén - fool)

Definition: To comfort, console, or soothe someone who is sad, worried, or in distress.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 安慰 (ānwèi - to comfort) and 慰问 (wèiwèn - to express sympathy/visit to console)

Definition: To understand or comprehend something. Used when someone grasps the meaning or knows about a subject.
Usage: Common in questions like 你懂吗? (Do you understand?) and statements like 我不懂 (I don't understand)

Definition: To criticize or comment on; also used as a measure word for groups or batches of things.
Usage: Common in phrases like 批评 (criticize), 一批学生 (a group of students), or 批改作业 (grade homework)

Definition: To embrace, hug, or hold in one's arms; to possess or have (something desirable)
Usage: Common in words like 拥抱 (embrace/hug) and 拥有 (to possess/own)

Definition: To push aside, move with hands or fingers; to dial (a phone number) or allocate (funds/resources).
Usage: Common in phrases like 拨电话 (dial a phone), 拨款 (allocate funds), or 拨开 (push aside)

Definition: To choose, select, or pick from among options or alternatives.
Usage: Common in words like 选择 (xuǎnzé - to choose) and 抉择 (juézé - to make a decision)

Definition: To pull, drag, or haul something forcefully with your hand or arm.
Usage: Often used for physically pulling objects or people, like 拽着我的手 (pulling my hand)

Definition: To stroke or smooth something with the hand, moving from one end to the other in a single direction. Often used for actions like smoothing hair, beard, or sleeves.
Usage: Common in phrases like 捋胡子 (stroke one's beard) or 捋袖子 (roll up one's sleeves)

Definition: To rub, knead, or massage something with the hands using circular or back-and-forth motions.
Usage: Commonly used for rubbing eyes (揉眼睛), kneading dough (揉面), or massaging sore muscles

Definition: To twitch, spasm, or convulse; describes involuntary muscle contractions or jerking movements
Usage: Most commonly seen in medical contexts or in the compound word 抽搐 (chōuchù, to have convulsions/spasms)

Definition: Means 'already' or 'since' when indicating something that has happened or is established. Most commonly used in the pattern 既...又... (both...and...) or 既然 (since/now that).
Usage: Common in formal writing and set patterns like 既然你来了 (since you've come)

Definition: To reflect, shine, or project light; to show or display (as in showing a film or creating a reflection).
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 反映 (to reflect/mirror), 放映 (to show a film), and 映照 (to shine upon)

Definition: To feel dizzy, faint, or lightheaded; can also refer to a halo or ring of light around the sun or moon.
Usage: Commonly used in expressions like 头晕 (tóuyūn - dizzy/lightheaded) or 晕车 (yūnchē - carsick)

Definition: Clear, distinct, or easy to understand. This character is rarely used alone and almost always appears in the compound word 清晰 (qīngxī), meaning 'clear' or 'distinct'.
Usage: Most commonly seen in 清晰 (qīngxī) to describe clear images, sounds, or explanations

Definition: A song, melody, or tune; also refers to a musical composition or piece of music.
Usage: Common in words like 歌曲 (song), 乐曲 (musical composition), 曲子 (tune)

Definition: A measure word for machines, vehicles, or instruments (like planes, cameras, pianos); also means 'frame', 'shelf', or 'to support/prop up'
Usage: Common in phrases like 一架飞机 (one airplane), 书架 (bookshelf), or 架子 (frame/shelf)

Definition: Relating to military, martial, or physical force; the opposite of civil or literary (文).
Usage: Common in words like 武术 (martial arts), 武器 (weapon), and 武力 (military force)

Definition: Foam, froth, or bubbles that form on the surface of liquids. Refers to the light, bubbly substance created by soap, waves, or other agitated liquids.
Usage: Commonly seen in compounds like 泡沫 (pàomò - foam/bubbles) and 唾沫 (tuòmò - saliva/spit)

Definition: Oil or fat, including cooking oil, petroleum, and other oily substances. Can also mean greasy or oily as an adjective.
Usage: Common in words like 石油 (petroleum), 汽油 (gasoline), 酱油 (soy sauce), and 油炸 (deep-fried)

Definition: To go along or follow the edge/border of something; along the side of.
Usage: Commonly used in phrases like 沿着河 (along the river) or 沿海 (coastal, along the coast)

Definition: Shallow, not deep; can refer to physical depth (like water) or abstract concepts (like knowledge or color intensity).
Usage: Common in words like 浅色 (light color), 深浅 (depth), and 肤浅 (superficial)

Definition: To float on water or in air; superficial or not deep. Can also describe something temporary, unstable, or appearing on the surface.
Usage: Common in words like 浮动 (fluctuate), 漂浮 (float), and 浮躁 (impetuous)

Definition: To apply, spread, or smear something (like paint, cream, or butter) onto a surface; to scribble or daub.
Usage: Common in phrases like 涂口红 (apply lipstick), 涂油漆 (paint/apply paint), 涂抹 (smear/spread)

Definition: Light, pale, or weak in color, flavor, or intensity; not strong or concentrated.
Usage: Commonly used to describe bland food (淡而无味), light colors (淡蓝色 - light blue), or weak tea/coffee

Definition: Warm or mild in temperature; can also describe a gentle or温和 (moderate) manner or personality.
Usage: Common in words like 温度 (temperature), 温暖 (warm), and 气温 (air temperature)

Definition: Cannon or artillery; also refers to firecrackers in traditional contexts.
Usage: Common in military contexts (大炮 - cannon) and celebrations (鞭炮 - firecrackers)

Definition: A candle or torch used for lighting and illumination.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 蜡烛 (làzhú, candle) and classical expressions

Definition: Smoke or cigarette. Refers to the visible vapor from burning materials or tobacco products.
Usage: Common in words like 抽烟 (to smoke), 香烟 (cigarette), 烟雾 (smoke/fumes)

Definition: Still, yet, or as if; indicates that something continues or remains in a certain state, or expresses comparison.
Usage: Commonly seen in literary or formal expressions like 犹如 (just like), 犹豫 (hesitate), or 记忆犹新 (memory still fresh)

Definition: Beautiful jade; precious and rare. Used to describe something extraordinary or remarkable.
Usage: Commonly appears in names and literary expressions like 瑰琦 (magnificent) or 琦丽 (exquisitely beautiful)

Definition: A roof tile, typically made of clay or ceramic material used in traditional Chinese architecture. Also used as a unit of electrical power (watt).
Usage: Common in words like 瓦片 (roof tile) and 千瓦 (kilowatt)

Definition: The first in a series or sequence, equivalent to 'A' in alphabetical ordering or 'first-class/grade A'. Also refers to armor or shell in classical contexts.
Usage: Commonly seen in 甲乙丙丁 (A, B, C, D ordering), 指甲 (fingernail), or 甲方 (Party A in contracts)

Definition: A measure word used for actions, efforts, or occurrences, meaning 'a round of' or 'a kind of'. Also means 'foreign' or 'barbarian' in classical Chinese.
Usage: Common in phrases like 一番 (yī fān - once, a round of) as in 一番努力 (a great effort)

Definition: A basin, pot, or tub-shaped container used for holding water, plants, or other items. Can also refer to a pelvis in anatomical contexts.
Usage: Common in words like 花盆 (flower pot), 脸盆 (wash basin), and 盆地 (basin/valley)

Definition: A measure word (classifier) used for counting lamps, lights, and small cup-like vessels. Can also refer to a small cup or lamp itself.
Usage: Common in phrases like 一盏灯 (one lamp) or 一盏茶 (a cup of tea)

Definition: A box or case, typically a small container with a lid used for storing or packaging items.
Usage: Common in words like 盒子 (box), 饭盒 (lunch box), 火柴盒 (matchbox)

Definition: To research, study deeply, or grind/polish something. Most commonly seen in the word 研究 (yánjiū) meaning 'research' or 'to study'.
Usage: Frequently used in academic and scientific contexts, such as 研究生 (graduate student) or 研发 (research and development)

Definition: To smash, break, or pound something with force; to strike or hit heavily.
Usage: Common in contexts like 砸碎 (smash to pieces), 砸门 (pound on a door), or 砸锅 (ruin something/mess up)

Definition: A bowl, typically used for eating rice, soup, or noodles. Also serves as a measure word for counting bowls of food.
Usage: Common in phrases like 一碗饭 (a bowl of rice) or 吃碗面 (eat a bowl of noodles)

Definition: To show, display, or demonstrate something to others; to indicate or reveal information.
Usage: Commonly used in formal contexts and compound words like 表示 (to express), 显示 (to display), 指示 (to instruct)

Definition: Organization, society, or association; refers to groups of people united for a common purpose.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 社会 (society), 公司 (company), 社区 (community), and 社团 (club/association)

Definition: Powder or noodles made from starch; also means pink (the color) or to be a fan of someone/something.
Usage: Common in words like 米粉 (rice noodles), 粉色 (pink color), and 粉丝 (fans/vermicelli)

Definition: The color purple or violet. It can refer to anything with a purple/violet hue.
Usage: Common in color descriptions like 紫色 (purple color) and compound words like 紫外线 (ultraviolet rays)

Definition: Tired or exhausted; feeling physically or mentally fatigued from work or activity.
Usage: Commonly used to express being worn out, as in 我很累 (I'm very tired)

Definition: To practice, train, or drill in order to improve a skill or ability. Often used for physical exercises, language learning, or developing any competency through repetition.
Usage: Common in words like 练习 (practice), 训练 (training), 练功 (practice martial arts)

Definition: To organize or form into a group; a group, team, or set of things. Also used as a measure word for sets or groups of items.
Usage: Common in words like 小组 (small group), 组织 (organization), and 一组 (a set/group of)

Definition: To trip or stumble over something; to cause someone to fall by catching their foot.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 绊倒 (bàndǎo - to trip and fall) and 羁绊 (jībàn - bonds/ties that restrain)

Definition: Soft, continuous, or unbroken; describes something cotton-like in texture or something that extends continuously without interruption.
Usage: Common in words like 绵羊 (sheep), 绵延 (stretch continuously), and 绵软 (soft and weak)

Definition: To stretch tight or pull taut; to bind or wrap tightly around something.
Usage: Commonly used for fabric, skin, or bandages being stretched tight, as in 绷带 (bandage) or 脸绷得紧紧的 (face stretched tight)

Definition: Fate, destiny, or predestined relationship between people; also refers to a karmic connection or bond that brings people together.
Usage: Common in phrases like 缘分 (yuánfèn - fate/destiny), 有缘 (yǒuyuán - destined to meet), and 姻缘 (yīnyuán - marriage fate)

Definition: To wind, wrap, or coil around something; to pester or bother someone persistently.
Usage: Used for physical wrapping (缠绕 - to wind around) or describing someone being clingy or annoying (纠缠 - to pester)

Definition: A suffix that turns verbs or adjectives into nouns meaning 'person who' or 'one who does something'. It creates agent nouns similar to '-er' or '-ist' in English.
Usage: Common in formal or written Chinese, as in 学者 (scholar), 作者 (author), 读者 (reader)

Definition: Intelligent, clever, or bright; describes someone with quick understanding and sharp mental abilities.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the word 聪明 (cōngmíng) meaning 'smart' or 'intelligent'

Definition: Meat or flesh, referring to the edible tissue of animals. Can also refer to the fleshy part of fruits or the human body.
Usage: Common in food contexts like 猪肉 (pork), 牛肉 (beef), 鸡肉 (chicken)

Definition: Belly, abdomen, or stomach; the part of the body between the chest and legs.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 肚子 (dùzi - stomach/belly) and 肚皮 (dùpí - belly skin)

Definition: Fetus, embryo, or unborn baby; also refers to tire (as in car tire) or birth order of pregnancy.
Usage: Common in words like 怀胎 (to be pregnant), 轮胎 (tire), 胎儿 (fetus), and 头胎 (first pregnancy)

Definition: A biological cell or a suffix meaning 'born of the same parents' (siblings). Most commonly seen in compound words related to biology or kinship.
Usage: Used in words like 细胞 (xìbāo - cell), 同胞 (tóngbāo - compatriot/sibling), 侨胞 (qiáobāo - overseas compatriot)

Definition: Crispy, crunchy, or brittle in texture; can also mean fragile or easily broken.
Usage: Commonly used to describe food texture (脆饼 crispy crackers) or fragile objects

Definition: The waist or lower back area of the body; the part between the ribs and hips.
Usage: Common in phrases like 腰痛 (lower back pain) and 弯腰 (to bend at the waist)

Definition: To obtain, gain, or win something through effort or achievement.
Usage: Commonly used in formal contexts like 获得 (to obtain), 获奖 (to win a prize), 获胜 (to win/achieve victory)

Definition: A particle indicating a continuous state or action in progress, similar to '-ing' in English; also means 'to touch' or 'to be affected by' as a verb.
Usage: Commonly seen in written Chinese as a verb suffix (e.g., 看著 watching, 坐著 sitting) or in compounds like 著急 (anxious)

Definition: To dip something into a liquid or sauce before eating or using it.
Usage: Commonly used when eating, like 蘸酱 (dip in sauce) or 蘸水 (dip in water)

Definition: Wax or candle; refers to the waxy substance produced by bees or used for making candles.
Usage: Common in words like 蜡烛 (candle) and 蜂蜡 (beeswax)

Definition: Stupid, foolish, or dumb; describes someone or something lacking intelligence or acting in a silly way.
Usage: Often used to criticize someone's actions or decisions, as in 蠢人 (stupid person) or 真蠢 (really stupid)

Definition: To attack or raid suddenly; to strike or assail unexpectedly. Also means to inherit or follow (a tradition or position).
Usage: Common in words like 袭击 (xíjí - to attack), 空袭 (kōngxí - air raid), and 世袭 (shìxí - hereditary)

Definition: Rule, regulation, or standard that governs behavior or procedures. Often used in compound words related to rules, norms, and established practices.
Usage: Common in words like 规定 (regulation), 规则 (rule), 法规 (law/statute)

Definition: To train, instruct, or teach; also means to admonish or lecture someone. Can refer to teachings or instructions passed down.
Usage: Common in words like 训练 (training), 教训 (lesson/lecture), and 培训 (to train)

Definition: To satirize, mock, or criticize indirectly through irony or sarcasm.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 讽刺 (fěngcì - to satirize) and 讽刺性 (satirical)

Definition: To thank or express gratitude; also used as a surname.
Usage: Most commonly seen in 谢谢 (xièxie, thank you) and polite expressions

Definition: Short name for Henan Province in central China; also means 'hesitant' or 'to hesitate' in classical Chinese
Usage: Most commonly seen in 河南省 (Henan Province) abbreviated as 豫, such as on license plates

Definition: To gamble or bet; to wager money or something of value on an uncertain outcome.
Usage: Common in words like 赌博 (gambling) and phrases like 打赌 (to make a bet)

Definition: To kneel or get down on one's knees. This action traditionally shows respect, submission, or supplication in Chinese culture.
Usage: Common in phrases like 跪下 (kneel down) or 下跪 (to kneel)

Definition: Restless, agitated, or impatient; describes a state of being irritable or unable to stay calm.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 急躁 (impatient), 烦躁 (irritable), and 焦躁 (anxious/restless)

Definition: To let down, disappoint, or fail to live up to someone's expectations or kindness; to wrong or betray someone's trust.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the phrase 辜负 (gūfù) meaning 'to fail to live up to' or 'to let down'

Definition: Means rapid, swift, or fast, describing something that happens or moves with great speed.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 迅速 (xùnsù - rapid/swift) and 迅猛 (xùnměng - swift and fierce)

Definition: To suffer, encounter, or meet with (usually something unfortunate or negative). Often used to describe experiencing disasters, setbacks, or bad situations.
Usage: Common in words like 遭遇 (to encounter), 遭受 (to suffer), 遭殃 (to meet with disaster)

Definition: Evil, wicked, or heretical; refers to something morally wrong, improper, or deviant from the correct path.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 邪恶 (evil), 邪教 (cult), and 歪门邪道 (crooked ways)

Definition: Cool, awesome, or stylish; describes something or someone fashionable and impressive. Can also mean cruel or harsh in formal contexts, though this meaning is less common in everyday speech.
Usage: Popular among young people to express admiration, as in 太酷了 (so cool!)

Definition: An ancient Chinese cooking pot or cauldron, typically made of metal with a round bottom. This character is now mainly seen in classical texts and set phrases.
Usage: Commonly appears in the idiom 破釜沉舟 (to burn one's boats/bridges)

Definition: A shop or store, typically a small retail establishment. Can also refer to a bunk or bed.
Usage: Common in words like 店铺 (shop), 铺子 (small store), 卧铺 (sleeping berth)

Definition: A pavilion, tower, or elevated building; also used in formal contexts to refer to a cabinet (government) or as a respectful term in titles.
Usage: Common in words like 内阁 (cabinet/government), 阁下 (Your Excellency), and 楼阁 (pavilion/tower)

Definition: The number zero; also used to mean 'fractional' or 'odd' when referring to numbers with decimals or extra units
Usage: Used in phone numbers, temperatures, decimals (like 三点零五 3.05), and ages (like 十零岁 10-something years old)

Definition: The cheek, referring to the fleshy side part of the face below the eye.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 脸颊 (liǎnjiá, cheek) and 面颊 (miànjiá, cheek)

Definition: A measure word (classifier) used for small, round objects like pearls, teeth, seeds, stars, and hearts.
Usage: Common in phrases like 一颗星星 (one star), 一颗心 (one heart), 一颗牙齿 (one tooth)

Definition: To forgive, spare, or show mercy to someone; also means abundant or plentiful.
Usage: Commonly seen in phrases like 饶恕 (forgive) and 求饶 (beg for mercy)

Definition: Hungry; to be hungry or to starve. Describes the physical state of needing food.
Usage: Commonly used in phrases like 我饿了 (I'm hungry) or 饿死了 (I'm starving)

Definition: Head or chief; also used as a measure word for counting songs and poems
Usage: Common in words like 首都 (capital city), 首先 (first/firstly), and when counting: 一首歌 (one song)

Definition: Fresh, not stale or spoiled; often used to describe food that is newly made or recently caught/picked.
Usage: Common in food contexts like 新鲜 (xīnxiān - fresh) or 鲜鱼 (xiānyú - fresh fish)

Definition: Bird; a feathered animal with wings that typically can fly
Usage: Used in compound words like 小鸟 (small bird) or 鸟类 (birds as a category)

Definition: Tooth or teeth; the hard, bony structures in the mouth used for biting and chewing.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 牙齿 (yáchǐ - teeth) and 齿轮 (chǐlún - gear/cogwheel)

Definition: A surname (one of the most common in China); also means 'fourth' in the traditional sequence or 'adult male/person' in classical Chinese.
Usage: Most commonly encountered as a family name, like 丁先生 (Mr. Ding)

Definition: Ugly or unattractive in appearance; can also refer to shameful or disgraceful.
Usage: Commonly used to describe physical appearance (丑陋 - ugly) or as the opposite of 美 (beautiful)

Definition: To lose or misplace something; to throw away or discard.
Usage: Common in everyday expressions like 丢了 (lost it) or 丢人 (lose face, be embarrassed)

Definition: To face, approach, or be on the verge of something; to arrive at or be present at a place or moment.
Usage: Common in words like 临时 (temporary, at the time), 面临 (to face/confront), and 来临 (to arrive/approach)

Definition: The number nine. It is considered a lucky number in Chinese culture due to its association with longevity.
Usage: Used in counting, dates, phone numbers, and addresses

Definition: Means 'only', 'merely', or 'just', indicating limitation or a small amount. Used to emphasize that something is restricted to what is mentioned and nothing more.
Usage: Common in phrases like 仅仅 (merely), 不仅 (not only), and 仅此而已 (only this and nothing more)

Definition: To fall forward; to stumble or topple over face-first.
Usage: Often used in literary or formal contexts; commonly seen in compound words like 前仆后继 (one stepping into the breach as another falls)

Definition: Many people; a crowd or multitude. Often used to refer to the masses or general public.
Usage: Common in words like 群众 (the masses), 观众 (audience), and 大众 (the public)

Definition: Refers to human relationships, ethics, or logical order; commonly seen in words related to morality and social norms.
Usage: Found in compounds like 伦理 (ethics), 伦敦 (London), and 无与伦比 (incomparable)

Definition: To accompany or keep someone company; a companion or partner who stays with you.
Usage: Common in words like 伙伴 (partner/companion), 陪伴 (to accompany), and 伴侣 (life partner/spouse)

Definition: To assist or help; an assistant or aide. Also means 'to accompany' or 'to support' in formal contexts.
Usage: Commonly seen in formal compounds like 辅佐 (to assist a ruler) or in Japanese-influenced words like 佐料 (condiment, seasoning)

Definition: To repair, fix, or mend something that is broken or damaged; also means to build, study, or cultivate (as in self-cultivation).
Usage: Common in words like 修理 (repair), 修建 (construct), and 修改 (revise/modify)

Definition: To bend down or lower one's head and body; to look down from a higher position.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 俯视 (look down at), 俯身 (bend down), and 俯瞰 (overlook from above)

Definition: Tired, weary, or fatigued, especially from prolonged activity or effort. Often describes both physical exhaustion and mental weariness.
Usage: Common in words like 疲倦 (pí juàn - tired/weary) and 厌倦 (yàn juàn - bored/fed up with)

Definition: Army or military; refers to armed forces or troops. Also used to mean a large organized group.
Usage: Common in words like 军人 (soldier), 军队 (army), 红军 (Red Army)

Definition: A hat or crown; also refers to a champion or first place position.
Usage: Common in words like 冠军 (champion) and 王冠 (crown)

Definition: Dark, obscure, or relating to the underworld and death. Often refers to the netherworld or things that are mysterious and hidden.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 冥想 (meditation), 冥王星 (Pluto), and 冥府 (underworld)

Definition: To freeze or be frozen; to feel very cold. Can describe water turning to ice, food being frozen, or a person feeling extremely cold.
Usage: Common in words like 冰冻 (frozen), 冻结 (freeze), 冷冻 (refrigerate), and 冻死了 (freezing to death/extremely cold)

Definition: Means 'every', 'all', or 'any' when used to indicate totality or universality; also means 'ordinary' or 'worldly' in certain contexts.
Usage: Commonly appears in formal or literary expressions like 凡是 (all those who/whatever) and 平凡 (ordinary)

Definition: To rely on or depend on something; to use something as proof or evidence
Usage: Common in phrases like 凭什么 (on what basis?) and 凭证 (certificate/proof)

Definition: A stool or bench; a backless seat typically used for sitting.
Usage: Commonly seen in compounds like 板凳 (wooden stool) or 凳子 (stool)

Definition: Fierce, violent, or inauspicious; describes something dangerous, aggressive, or bringing bad luck.
Usage: Common in words like 凶手 (murderer), 凶猛 (ferocious), and 吉凶 (good or bad fortune)

Definition: To make an effort or strive to do something; to encourage or urge someone to do their best
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 勉强 (miǎnqiǎng - reluctantly, barely) and 勉励 (miǎnlì - to encourage)

Definition: A district, area, or region; a designated section or zone within a larger space such as a city or administrative division.
Usage: Commonly used in place names like 朝阳区 (Chaoyang District) or to describe different zones like 住宅区 (residential area)

Definition: To guard, protect, or defend; also means guard or defender as a noun.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 卫生 (hygiene, literally 'guard health'), 保卫 (to defend), and 卫星 (satellite, literally 'guard star')

Definition: To experience or go through something; to pass through successive stages or events in time.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 历史 (history), 经历 (experience), and 历年 (successive years)

Definition: To chatter or talk incessantly; to be talkative or long-winded in speech.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the compound word 唠叨 (láodao) meaning 'to nag' or 'to chatter'

Definition: To summon, call together, or convene; to recruit or enlist people for a purpose.
Usage: Commonly seen in formal contexts like 召开会议 (to convene a meeting) or 召集 (to call together)

Definition: Leaf; the flat, typically green part of a plant that grows from a stem or branch.
Usage: Common in words like 树叶 (tree leaf) and 叶子 (leaf)

Definition: An onomatopoeia representing chirping, squeaking, or chattering sounds, especially those made by small birds or insects.
Usage: Commonly used in reduplicated form 叽叽 (jījī) to describe continuous chirping or murmuring sounds

Definition: To spit out or vomit; to expel something from the mouth or stomach.
Usage: Common in expressions like 呕吐 (to vomit) and 吐痰 (to spit phlegm)

Definition: To swallow something whole without chewing; to devour or engulf something completely.
Usage: Often used literally for swallowing food or figuratively for annexing territory or embezzling money

Definition: A negative word meaning 'not' or 'no', used primarily in formal or written Chinese to negate or deny something.
Usage: Commonly appears in questions like 是否 (whether or not) and formal expressions; less common in everyday speech than 不

Definition: An onomatopoeia representing squeaking, creaking, or chirping sounds made by small animals, doors, or objects.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 吱吱 (zhīzhī, squeaking sound) or 吱声 (zhīshēng, to utter a sound)

Definition: To be noisy or loud; to quarrel or argue with someone
Usage: Common in phrases like 吵架 (to quarrel), 吵闹 (noisy), or 别吵 (be quiet/stop arguing)

Definition: Grief, sorrow, or mourning; expresses deep sadness or lamentation, often related to death or loss.
Usage: Common in formal or literary contexts, such as 哀悼 (to mourn) or 悲哀 (sadness)

Definition: To tremble or shiver, typically from cold or fear. Most commonly seen in the reduplicative form 哆嗦 (duōsuo).
Usage: Primarily used in the compound word 哆嗦, meaning to shiver or tremble

Definition: To call out to someone or summon; to wake someone up by calling their name.
Usage: Often used in literary or formal contexts, as in 呼唤 (to call out) or 唤醒 (to awaken)

Definition: Business, commerce, or trade; also refers to a merchant or businessperson.
Usage: Common in words like 商店 (shop), 商人 (merchant), and 电商 (e-commerce)

Definition: A character used primarily in the word for beer (啤酒 píjiǔ). It is a phonetic transliteration from the English word 'beer' and rarely appears outside this context.
Usage: Almost exclusively used in 啤酒 (beer)

Definition: An onomatopoeia representing the chirping or chattering sound made by birds or insects.
Usage: Commonly used in reduplicated form 喳喳 (zhāzhā) to describe bird sounds or noisy chatter

Definition: To suck or slurp; describes the action of drawing something into the mouth, often used for eating noodles or making a sucking sound.
Usage: Commonly seen in 啰嗦 (luōsuo - wordy/long-winded) and when describing eating noodles

Definition: An onomatopoeia representing a short, sharp sound like a beep, honk, or drip. Often used to describe sounds made by horns, alarms, or water droplets.
Usage: Commonly seen in reduplicated form 嘀嘀 (dīdī) for car horns or 嘀咕 (dígū) meaning to mutter or whisper

Definition: An onomatopoeia representing abrupt, sharp sounds like honking, quacking, or creaking noises.
Usage: Commonly used to describe duck sounds (嘎嘎 gāgā) or sudden stopping sounds

Definition: Bad, evil, or terrifying; describes something frightening or nightmarish.
Usage: Most commonly seen in 噩梦 (è mèng) meaning 'nightmare'

Definition: To block, obstruct, or stop up something; to be blocked or congested.
Usage: Commonly used for traffic jams (堵车) or blocking passages

Definition: A pot, kettle, or vessel with a spout and handle used for holding and pouring liquids, especially tea or water.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 茶壶 (teapot) and 水壶 (water kettle)

Definition: Center or middle; also means to beg or request earnestly.
Usage: Most commonly seen in compounds like 中央 (center/central) and 央求 (to beg/implore)

Definition: Profound, mysterious, or deep; often used to mean 'Olympics' as a shortened form of 奥林匹克 (Àolínpǐkè).
Usage: Commonly seen in 奥运会 (Olympics) and place names like 奥地利 (Austria)

Definition: Younger sister. Can also refer to a young girl or be used as a suffix in compound words related to young females.
Usage: Common in family terms like 妹妹 (younger sister) and 姐妹 (sisters)

Definition: A historical term meaning 'concubine' or 'court lady'; also used as a surname and in the Zhou Dynasty royal family name.
Usage: Commonly appears in historical texts, classical literature, and as a family name in modern Chinese

Definition: A child, baby, or young kid. Often used informally or in regional dialects to refer to children.
Usage: Common in compounds like 娃娃 (wáwa, doll/baby) and 小娃 (xiǎowá, little child)

Definition: To exist, to store, or to deposit. Commonly used to mean keeping something in a place for safekeeping, especially money in a bank.
Usage: Found in words like 存在 (to exist), 保存 (to preserve), and 存钱 (to deposit money)

Definition: Alone, lonely, or solitary; describes someone or something that is isolated or without companions.
Usage: Common in words like 孤独 (lonely), 孤单 (solitary), and literary expressions

Definition: Palace or temple; a large, grand building used by royalty or for religious purposes. Also refers to the imperial court or a note in traditional Chinese music.
Usage: Common in words like 故宫 (Forbidden City/Imperial Palace) and 天宫 (heavenly palace)

Definition: Guest or visitor; someone who is received or entertained by a host.
Usage: Common in words like 宾客 (guests), 来宾 (visitors), and 宾馆 (hotel/guesthouse)

Definition: To send or mail something (like a letter or package); to entrust something to someone's care.
Usage: Commonly used in 寄信 (send a letter), 寄包裹 (mail a package), or 寄宿 (lodge/board)

Definition: Bureau, office, or department; also means situation, game, or set (in sports). Used as a measure word for games and situations.
Usage: Common in words like 邮局 (post office), 结局 (ending/outcome), 棋局 (chess game)

Definition: A drawer or sliding compartment in furniture such as desks, cabinets, or dressers; also refers to a steamer tray used in cooking.
Usage: Commonly seen in 抽屉 (chōuti, drawer) and 蒸屉 (zhēngti, steamer tray)

Definition: To unfold, spread out, or extend; to display or exhibit something.
Usage: Common in words like 展览 (exhibition), 发展 (develop), and 展开 (unfold)

Definition: To belong to or be part of a category; to be born in a particular Chinese zodiac year
Usage: Common in phrases like 属于 (belong to) and when asking someone's zodiac sign: 你属什么? (What's your zodiac animal?)

Definition: A piece of cloth used for wiping or covering, such as a towel, napkin, or handkerchief.
Usage: Commonly seen in compounds like 毛巾 (towel), 纸巾 (tissue), and 围巾 (scarf)

Definition: Currency or money; a general term for any form of monetary unit.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 人民币 (RMB, Chinese yuan), 硬币 (coin), and 外币 (foreign currency)

Definition: A curtain, screen, or hanging drape used to cover windows, doors, or divide spaces.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 窗帘 (window curtain), 门帘 (door curtain), and 竹帘 (bamboo screen)

Definition: Emperor or supreme ruler; refers to the highest sovereign authority in imperial China or a deity.
Usage: Found in words like 皇帝 (emperor), 上帝 (God), and 帝国 (empire)

Definition: A curtain or screen, typically made of cloth, used to divide spaces or provide privacy. Often refers to large hanging drapes in traditional or formal settings.
Usage: Commonly seen in classical Chinese and formal contexts, such as 帷幕 (curtain/screen)

Definition: A curtain, screen, or backdrop; also refers to an act or scene in a play or performance.
Usage: Common in theater contexts like 开幕 (opening ceremony) or 闭幕 (closing ceremony), and in 幕后 (behind the scenes)

Definition: Wide, broad, or extensive in scope or area. Also used as a radical component in characters related to buildings or structures.
Usage: Common in words like 广场 (plaza/square), 广大 (vast), and 广告 (advertisement)

Definition: A projectile or ammunition, such as a bullet, shell, or bomb. Also refers to something shaped like a ball or pellet.
Usage: Common in words like 子弹 (bullet), 炸弹 (bomb), 导弹 (missile)

Definition: That, the other, or those (referring to someone or something distant or previously mentioned); often contrasted with 此 (this).
Usage: Commonly used in formal or literary contexts, such as 彼此 (each other) or 知己知彼 (know yourself and know your enemy)

Definition: State, condition, or attitude; refers to the way something or someone appears or behaves.
Usage: Commonly used in compounds like 状态 (state/condition), 态度 (attitude), 形态 (form/shape), and 生态 (ecology)

Definition: To forgive or pardon someone; to show understanding and tolerance toward others' mistakes or offenses.
Usage: Often used in formal contexts like 恕我直言 (forgive my bluntness) or 宽恕 (to forgive)

Definition: Frightened, terrified, or fearful; describes a feeling of being scared or alarmed.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the compound word 恐怖 (kǒngbù) meaning 'horror' or 'terror', and 毛骨悚然 (máogǔsǒngrán) meaning 'hair-raising'

Definition: Describes something that is long, distant, or leisurely in time or space; conveys a sense of being unhurried, relaxed, or far-reaching.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 悠久 (long-standing), 悠闲 (leisurely), and 悠扬 (melodious)

Definition: Sad, sorrowful, or grief-stricken; describes feelings of deep sadness or tragedy.
Usage: Common in words like 悲伤 (bēishāng - sad), 悲剧 (bēijù - tragedy), and 悲观 (bēiguān - pessimistic)

Definition: To confuse, bewilder, or mislead; to be puzzled or uncertain about something.
Usage: Commonly seen in compounds like 迷惑 (míhuò - confused/puzzled), 疑惑 (yíhuò - doubtful/puzzled), and 困惑 (kùnhuò - perplexed)

Definition: To provoke, cause, or stir up (trouble, anger, or problems); to attract or invite (unwanted attention or consequences).
Usage: Commonly used in phrases like 惹麻烦 (to cause trouble) or 惹人生气 (to make someone angry)

Definition: To worry, be anxious, or feel distressed about something. Describes a state of sadness or melancholy caused by concerns or troubles.
Usage: Often used in literary contexts and expressions like 发愁 (to worry) or 愁眉苦脸 (worried expression)

Definition: Surprised, astonished, or startled, typically describing a sudden feeling of shock or amazement.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the compound word 愕然 (èrán, 'astonished') or 惊愕 (jīng'è, 'shocked and surprised')

Definition: Kind, loving, and compassionate, especially describing parental love or mercy. Often refers to maternal affection or benevolent care toward others.
Usage: Common in words like 慈母 (loving mother), 慈善 (charity), and 慈悲 (compassion/mercy)

Definition: Lazy; unwilling to work or make an effort. Describes someone who avoids activity or prefers to do nothing.
Usage: Common in phrases like 懒人 (lazy person) or 我很懒 (I'm very lazy)

Definition: Drama, play, or theatrical performance; can also refer to opera or any form of staged entertainment.
Usage: Common in words like 京剧 (Beijing opera), 看戏 (watch a play), 游戏 (game)

Definition: To hold, grasp, or carry out; to execute or implement something
Usage: Common in words like 执行 (to execute/implement) and 坚持 (to persist/insist)

Definition: To drape over one's shoulders or to wear loosely; to spread out or open up something.
Usage: Commonly used in 披着 (draping/wearing), 披萨 (pizza - phonetic), and 披露 (to reveal/disclose)

Definition: To resist, oppose, or withstand something; also means to arrive at or reach a destination, or to be equivalent to/offset something.
Usage: Common in words like 抵抗 (resist), 抵达 (arrive at), and 抵消 (offset/cancel out)

Definition: To lean on or support oneself with something, typically a cane or stick.
Usage: Most commonly seen in 拄拐杖 (to lean on a crutch/cane)

Definition: Refers to the thumb or big toe; the first and largest digit on the hand or foot.
Usage: Most commonly seen in 拇指 (mǔzhǐ - thumb) and 大拇指 (dà mǔzhǐ - thumb/big toe)

Definition: To tie up or fasten something (usually an animal) with a rope or cord to prevent it from moving away.
Usage: Commonly used with animals like dogs or horses, as in 拴马 (tie up a horse) or 拴狗 (tie up a dog)

Definition: To press or push down with the hand or finger; also means 'according to' or 'in accordance with'
Usage: Used for physical pressing (按按钮 press a button) or following rules/plans (按时 on time, according to schedule)

Definition: To carry something with a pole on one's shoulder; to choose or select carefully.
Usage: Common in expressions like 挑选 (to select) and 挑担 (to carry loads on a shoulder pole)

Definition: An adverb meaning 'quite' or 'rather' used to indicate a moderate to high degree of something, often expressing mild emphasis or approval.
Usage: Commonly used in spoken Chinese, as in 挺好 (quite good) or 挺贵 (rather expensive)

Definition: To pinch, squeeze, or knead something with fingers or hands. Also means to mold or shape something soft like clay or dough.
Usage: Common in contexts like 捏泥人 (to mold clay figures) or 捏一下 (to pinch once)

Definition: To arrange, handle, or manage something; to place or set up. Most commonly seen in compound words related to taking action or implementing measures.
Usage: Frequently used in words like 措施 (cuōshī - measures/steps) and 举措 (jǔcuò - move/action)

Definition: To put together, join, or build by combining parts; to travel by or take (a form of transportation).
Usage: Common in words like 搭配 (to match/pair), 搭建 (to build/construct), and 搭车 (to hitch a ride/take a vehicle)

Definition: To stack or pile things up; also used as a measure word for stacked items like a pile or stack of books, plates, or papers.
Usage: Common in phrases like 一摞书 (a stack of books) or 把碗摞起来 (stack the bowls up)

Definition: To tear or rip something apart with your hands, such as paper, fabric, or other materials.
Usage: Common in phrases like 撕纸 (tear paper) or 撕破 (tear to pieces)

Definition: To blow one's nose by forcefully expelling air through the nostrils.
Usage: Commonly used in the phrase 擤鼻涕 (xǐng bítì) meaning 'to blow one's nose'

Definition: To scatter, disperse, or break up; to come apart or fall apart. Also means loose or scattered (not organized together).
Usage: Common in words like 散步 (take a walk), 分散 (disperse), or 散装 (sold loose/in bulk)

Definition: Honest, sincere, or earnest; also means to urge or press someone to do something.
Usage: Often seen in formal contexts and place names like 敦煌 (Dunhuang)

Definition: Material or ingredient used to make something; can also mean to expect or anticipate something.
Usage: Common in compounds like 材料 (material), 饮料 (beverage), 调料 (seasoning), or 料到 (to anticipate)

Definition: 族 means 'clan', 'ethnic group', or 'tribe'. It is also used as a suffix to describe groups of people with shared characteristics or lifestyles.
Usage: Common in words like 民族 (ethnic group), 家族 (family clan), and modern terms like 上班族 (office workers) or 低头族 (people always looking at phones)

Definition: Means 'yesterday' or 'past/previous' when referring to time. Used as a prefix to indicate the day before or a recent past time period.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 昨天 (zuótiān, yesterday), 昨日 (zuórì, yesterday), and 昨晚 (zuówǎn, last night)

Definition: Mixed, miscellaneous, or diverse; describes things that are varied, disorderly, or not pure/uniform.
Usage: Common in words like 复杂 (complicated), 杂志 (magazine), and 混杂 (mixed together)

Definition: A village or small rural settlement, typically smaller than a town. Refers to countryside communities with agricultural or traditional lifestyles.
Usage: Common in words like 村子 (village) and 农村 (countryside/rural area)

Definition: A measure word (classifier) used for counting small objects like coins, stamps, medals, badges, and missiles.
Usage: Common in phrases like 一枚硬币 (one coin), 两枚邮票 (two stamps)

Definition: A fence, railing, or barrier made of wooden or metal bars arranged in a row. Refers to structures like picket fences, railings, or grated barriers.
Usage: Common in words like 栅栏 (fence), 铁栅 (iron railing), and 围栅 (enclosure)

Definition: A railing, fence, or barrier; also refers to a column or section in a publication or form.
Usage: Common in compounds like 栏杆 (railing), 专栏 (column in newspaper), 填写栏 (fill-in section)

Definition: To check, examine, or inspect something carefully. Often used in formal or official contexts related to testing, reviewing, or investigating.
Usage: Common in words like 检查 (jiǎnchá - to inspect), 体检 (tǐjiǎn - physical examination), 检验 (jiǎnyàn - to test/verify)

Definition: A shed, shack, or temporary shelter structure with a simple roof. Also refers to a canopy, awning, or booth made of simple materials.
Usage: Common in words like 大棚 (greenhouse), 凉棚 (awning), 牛棚 (cattle shed)

Definition: To be happy, joyful, or delighted; to appreciate or admire something with pleasure.
Usage: Commonly used in compound words like 欣赏 (appreciate), 欣喜 (delighted), and 欣然 (gladly)

Definition: Desire or want; to wish to do something. In classical Chinese and formal contexts, it means 'to want' or 'to be about to.'
Usage: Common in literary expressions like 欲望 (desire), 食欲 (appetite), and classical phrases like 欲罢不能 (unable to stop even if one wants to)

Definition: Crooked, tilted, or not straight; can describe physical objects that are askew or ideas/methods that are improper or devious.
Usage: Common in expressions like 歪头 (tilt one's head) or 歪理 (twisted logic)

Definition: Means incomplete, damaged, or cruel; describes something that is broken, leftover, or brutal.
Usage: Common in words like 残疾 (disability), 残忍 (cruel), 残留 (remaining/leftover)

Definition: Mud, clay, or any soft, wet earth-like substance. Can also refer to paste-like materials such as cement or plaster.
Usage: Common in words like 泥土 (mud/soil), 水泥 (cement), and 泥巴 (mud)

Definition: Tears; the drops of liquid that come from your eyes when you cry or when your eyes are irritated.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 眼泪 (yǎnlèi - tears) and 流泪 (liúlèi - to shed tears)

Definition: Gradually; progressively; by degrees. Indicates a slow, step-by-step change or development over time.
Usage: Commonly used in compounds like 渐渐 (jiànjiàn, gradually) and 逐渐 (zhújiàn, progressively)

Definition: To grow, multiply, or nourish; to cause or produce something (often used in formal or literary contexts)
Usage: Commonly seen in compounds like 滋味 (taste/flavor), 滋养 (nourish), and 滋生 (breed/produce)

Definition: To roll, tumble, or rotate; also used as a rude command meaning 'get lost' or 'scram'
Usage: Common in phrases like 滚开 (roll away/get lost) and 翻滚 (to roll over)

Definition: A drop or droplet of liquid; can also be used as a verb meaning to drip or let fall in drops.
Usage: Common in expressions like 一滴水 (a drop of water) or 滴水 (dripping water)

Definition: To leak, drip, or let something escape through a hole; also means to leave out or omit something unintentionally.
Usage: Common in phrases like 漏水 (water leak), 漏掉 (to miss/omit), and 遗漏 (to leave out)

Definition: To pour liquid into something; to fill or irrigate by pouring.
Usage: Common in words like 灌水 (to irrigate/water), 灌溉 (irrigation), and 灌木 (shrub/bush)

Definition: To extinguish, put out, or destroy; to become extinct or disappear completely.
Usage: Common in words like 消灭 (eliminate), 灭火 (put out a fire), and 毁灭 (destroy)

Definition: Brilliant, splendid, or dazzling; describes something that shines brightly or is magnificently radiant.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 灿烂 (cànlàn - brilliant/splendid) to describe bright light, smiles, or achievements

Definition: To roast, bake, or grill food using dry heat, typically over fire or in an oven.
Usage: Common in food-related contexts like 烤鸭 (roast duck), 烤肉 (barbecue), 烤面包 (toast bread)

Definition: To stop or end abruptly; also means evil spirit or malign influence in traditional Chinese culture.
Usage: Commonly seen in compounds like 煞车 (brake), 煞风景 (spoil the fun), and 煞气 (evil aura)

Definition: Claw, talon, or paw of an animal; also refers to a bird's or animal's foot with sharp nails.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 爪子 (claw/paw) and 鸡爪 (chicken feet)

Definition: Male (of animals); most commonly seen in the word for peony flower.
Usage: Primarily used in 牡丹 (mǔdān, peony) and to indicate male livestock like 牡牛 (bull)

Definition: To commit (a crime, error, or offense); to violate or break (a rule or law).
Usage: Common in phrases like 犯罪 (commit a crime), 犯错 (make a mistake), 犯法 (break the law)

Definition: A character meaning 'agate' (a type of gemstone), but most commonly used as a transliteration component in foreign names and loanwords.
Usage: Frequently seen in names like 玛丽 (Mary), 玛格丽特 (Margaret), and 玛瑙 (agate stone)

Definition: To throw, fling, or swing something with force; to shake off or cast aside.
Usage: Commonly used for physical actions like swinging arms (甩手) or ditching/dumping someone in relationships (甩了他)

Definition: To be paralyzed or unable to move; to collapse or slump down from exhaustion or weakness.
Usage: Common in medical contexts (瘫痪 paralysis) and colloquially to describe extreme tiredness (累瘫了 exhausted to the point of collapse)

Definition: Benefit, advantage, or profit; also means to increase or add to something.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 利益 (benefit/interest), 有益 (beneficial), and 益处 (advantage)

Definition: To supervise, monitor, or oversee something or someone. Also means prison or jail when used as a noun.
Usage: Common in words like 监督 (supervise), 监视 (monitor), 监狱 (prison)

Definition: To hope for, to look forward to, or to expect something eagerly. Expresses anticipation or longing for a desired outcome or event.
Usage: Common in phrases like 盼望 (to hope for) and 期盼 (to look forward to)

Definition: To grind, polish, or rub something to make it smooth or fine; to wear down through friction or repeated action.
Usage: Common in words like 磨刀 (sharpen a knife), 折磨 (torment), and 磨练 (temper/train through hardship)

Definition: Disaster, calamity, or misfortune; refers to harmful events or trouble that brings suffering.
Usage: Often appears in words like 灾祸 (disaster), 祸害 (scourge), and the idiom 祸不单行 (misfortunes never come singly)

Definition: Private, personal, or secret; also means selfish when describing behavior or attitudes.
Usage: Common in words like 私人 (private/personal) and 自私 (selfish)

Definition: Sparse, thin, or watery; describes something that is not dense or concentrated.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 稀饭 (rice porridge), 稀少 (rare/scarce), and 稀奇 (rare/strange)

Definition: A journey, distance, or course; also refers to a process, procedure, or degree/extent of something.
Usage: Common in words like 过程 (process), 课程 (course/curriculum), 路程 (distance of a journey), and 程度 (degree/extent)

Definition: A nest or den where animals live; also refers to a hideout or any small, cozy dwelling place.
Usage: Common in words like 鸟窝 (bird's nest), 狗窝 (dog house), or 被窝 (under the covers/bedding)

Definition: Stupid, foolish, or clumsy; describes someone who is slow to understand or awkward in their actions.
Usage: Often used to describe people's intelligence or physical coordination, as in 笨蛋 (idiot) or 笨手笨脚 (clumsy)

Definition: A fence or hedge, typically made of bamboo, wood, or woven branches used to enclose or separate areas.
Usage: Commonly seen in compounds like 篱笆 (líba, fence) and 藩篱 (fānlí, barrier/fence)

Definition: Excrement, feces, or manure; waste matter discharged from the body or used as fertilizer.
Usage: Commonly seen in compounds like 粪便 (feces) or 肥粪 (manure/fertilizer)

Definition: Sugar or candy; any sweet substance used for food or confection.
Usage: Common in words like 糖果 (candy), 白糖 (white sugar), 冰糖 (rock sugar)

Definition: To correct, rectify, or point out errors; to gather together or entangle.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 纠正 (to correct), 纠纷 (dispute), and 纠结 (tangled/conflicted)

Definition: Pure, unmixed, or genuine; describes something without impurities or additions.
Usage: Common in words like 纯净 (pure/clean), 纯粹 (purely), and 单纯 (simple/naive)

Definition: To wind around, wrap around, or circle something; to make a detour or go around.
Usage: Common in phrases like 绕路 (take a detour), 绕圈 (go in circles), 围绕 (revolve around)

Definition: Rope, cord, or string used for tying, binding, or pulling things together.
Usage: Common in words like 绳子 (rope), 跳绳 (jump rope), and 绳索 (cable)

Definition: A cover, shade, or hood that goes over something to protect or conceal it; can also mean to cover or envelop something.
Usage: Common in words like 口罩 (kǒuzhào - face mask), 灯罩 (dēngzhào - lampshade), and 笼罩 (lǒngzhào - to envelop/shroud)

Definition: To droop or hang down loosely, typically describing ears, eyelids, or head hanging downward.
Usage: Most commonly seen in 耷拉 (dā la) meaning to droop or let hang down

Definition: To swell, expand, or feel bloated. Describes something becoming larger due to internal pressure or fullness.
Usage: Commonly used for physical sensations like 肚子胀 (bloated stomach) or objects expanding like 膨胀 (to expand/inflate)

Definition: To threaten, coerce, or intimidate someone into doing something against their will.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 威胁 (wēixié - to threaten) and 胁迫 (xiépò - to coerce)

Definition: Internal organs of the body, specifically referring to the hollow organs in traditional Chinese medicine (such as stomach, intestines, bladder, and gallbladder).
Usage: Most commonly seen in the set phrase 五脏六腑 (wǔ zàng liù fǔ) meaning 'all the internal organs'

Definition: Wrist; the joint connecting the hand to the forearm.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 手腕 (shǒuwàn - wrist) and 腕表 (wànbiǎo - wristwatch)

Definition: To rise, soar, or jump up; to make room or clear space for something
Usage: Common in words like 奔腾 (galloping/surging), 腾空 (to soar into the air), and 腾出 (to make room/clear out)

Definition: The interior cavity or chamber of something, especially the barrel of a gun or the chest cavity of the body.
Usage: Commonly seen in compounds like 枪膛 (gun barrel) and 胸膛 (chest)

Definition: The stem or stalk of a plant, the main structural part that supports leaves and flowers.
Usage: Commonly used in botanical contexts, such as 茎叶 (stems and leaves) or 花茎 (flower stem)

Definition: Soft, fine hair or down; describes something fluffy, fuzzy, or covered with fine hairs like velvet or new plant growth.
Usage: Often seen in compounds like 茸毛 (fine hair/down) or 鹿茸 (deer antler velvet)

Definition: Refers to a faint, shimmering light or glow, like fluorescent light or the glimmer of fireflies.
Usage: Most commonly seen in compounds like 荧光 (fluorescent light) and 荧屏 (screen, monitor)

Definition: Jasmine (the flower); primarily used as a component in names, especially female given names
Usage: Most commonly seen in 茉莉 (mòlì, jasmine) and personal names like 莉莉 (Lìlì)

Definition: To cover, deceive, or suffer; also means ignorant or uncivilized. Can also refer to Mongolia or receiving (a favor).
Usage: Common in words like 启蒙 (enlighten), 蒙骗 (deceive), 内蒙古 (Inner Mongolia)

Definition: A type of wild grass or weed; also describes something disheveled, messy, or tangled in appearance.
