Usage: Commonly seen in words like 蓬松 (fluffy, puffy) and 蓬勃 (vigorous, flourishing)

Definition: To despise, scorn, or look down upon someone or something with contempt.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the compound word 蔑视 (mièshì, to despise/scorn)

Definition: Empty, void, or unreal; also means weak or in poor health. Often describes something lacking substance or being false/modest.
Usage: Common in words like 虚伪 (hypocritical), 虚弱 (weak), 谦虚 (modest)

Definition: Honey; a sweet, thick liquid produced by bees. Also used to describe something sweet or intimate.
Usage: Common in words like 蜂蜜 (fēngmì, honey) and 甜蜜 (tiánmì, sweet/happy)

Definition: Fly (the insect). A common pest insect often found around food and waste.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the compound word 苍蝇 (cāngying, housefly)

Definition: Sleeve of a garment, the part of clothing that covers the arm.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 袖子 (sleeve), 长袖 (long sleeves), 短袖 (short sleeves)

Definition: To split, crack, or break apart into pieces. Describes something breaking open or tearing along a line.
Usage: Common in words like 分裂 (split/divide), 破裂 (rupture), and 裂缝 (crack/fissure)

Definition: To cover, overturn, or capsize; also means to repeat or reply (in formal contexts).
Usage: Common in words like 覆盖 (cover), 颠覆 (overturn), and 答覆 (reply)

Definition: A Chinese surname; also means to talk excessively or chatter in classical Chinese.
Usage: Most commonly encountered as a family name, as in 詹姆斯 (Zhānmǔsī, James)

Definition: To count, calculate, or compute; also means a plan or strategy.
Usage: Common in words like 计划 (plan), 计算 (calculate), and 统计 (statistics)

Definition: Sincere, honest, or truthful; refers to being genuine and earnest in one's words and actions.
Usage: Commonly appears in words like 诚实 (honest), 真诚 (sincere), and 诚意 (sincerity)

Definition: To forgive, excuse, or understand someone's situation; to show consideration or tolerance.
Usage: Commonly seen in formal expressions like 谅解 (understanding/forgiveness) and 原谅 (to forgive)

Definition: To congratulate or celebrate; to express good wishes for happy occasions or achievements.
Usage: Commonly used in phrases like 祝贺 (congratulate), 贺卡 (greeting card), and 庆贺 (celebrate)

Definition: To exceed, surpass, or go beyond a limit; also used as a prefix meaning 'super' or 'ultra'.
Usage: Common in words like 超市 (supermarket), 超过 (to exceed), and colloquially as 超好 (super good)

Definition: A measure word for trips, journeys, or round trips; also used to count occurrences of going somewhere and returning.
Usage: Common in phrases like 走一趟 (make a trip) or 去一趟 (go there once)

Definition: To fall down or tumble; to drop or decline (in price, value, or level).
Usage: Common in contexts like 跌倒 (to fall down) or 股票跌了 (stocks fell)

Definition: A fall or stumble; refers to losing one's balance and falling down
Usage: Most commonly used in the phrase 摔跤 (shuāi jiāo) meaning 'to fall down' or 'wrestling'

Definition: To step on, tread on, or walk on something with one's foot. Can also mean to go through or experience something.
Usage: Common in words like 踏步 (march in place), 踏实 (steady/reliable), and 踏青 (spring outing)

Definition: To step on, tread on, or trample something with one's foot. Can refer to both accidental stepping and deliberate trampling.
Usage: Common in phrases like 踩到 (step on accidentally) or 踩脚 (step on someone's foot)

Definition: To step on, kick, or pedal with the foot or feet. Can also mean to push against something with one's legs.
Usage: Common in contexts like 蹬自行车 (to pedal a bicycle) or 蹬腿 (to kick one's legs)

Definition: An adverb meaning 'relatively' or 'comparatively', used to indicate a moderate degree of comparison. Often appears in the pattern 较 + adjective to mean 'rather' or 'quite'.
Usage: Common in written Chinese, as in 较好 (relatively good) or 较大 (comparatively large)

Definition: Generation or lifetime; a measure word for groups of people of the same age or status level. Also refers to seniority ranking in family or social relationships.
Usage: Common in words like 一辈子 (whole lifetime), 长辈 (elder/senior generation), 晚辈 (younger generation)

Definition: Spicy or hot (in taste), describing food that has a burning sensation like chili peppers. Can also mean harsh or ruthless when describing a person's character or methods.
Usage: Commonly used to describe Sichuan cuisine (四川菜很辣) or to ask if food is spicy (辣不辣?)

Definition: To violate, disobey, or go against rules, laws, or principles; to be contrary to something.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 违法 (break the law), 违反 (violate), and 违背 (go against)

Definition: To stroll, browse, or wander around leisurely, especially for window shopping or sightseeing without a specific purpose.
Usage: Commonly used in phrases like 逛街 (go shopping/stroll the streets) and 逛商场 (browse the mall)

Definition: To make, build, or create something; to manufacture or construct.
Usage: Common in words like 制造 (manufacture), 创造 (create), and 建造 (construct)

Definition: To force, compel, or pressure someone to do something against their will.
Usage: Common in expressions like 逼迫 (to coerce) and 压逼 (to pressure). Can also mean 'to approach closely' or 'urgent'

Definition: To cover, block, or hide something from view; to shield or obstruct.
Usage: Common in words like 遮住 (to cover up), 遮挡 (to block), and 遮阳 (to shade from sun)

Definition: To avoid, evade, or keep away from something undesirable or dangerous.
Usage: Common in words like 避免 (avoid), 逃避 (escape from), 躲避 (hide from)

Definition: Sharp, keen, or acute; describes something with a pointed edge or penetrating quality. Can refer to physical sharpness or metaphorical sharpness like keen insight or intense energy.
Usage: Common in words like 锐利 (sharp/keen), 敏锐 (acute/perceptive), and 锐气 (vigor/drive)

Definition: To make noise, cause a disturbance, or be noisy; can also mean to suffer from or experience (an illness or problem).
Usage: Common in words like 热闹 (lively/bustling), 闹钟 (alarm clock), and phrases like 闹肚子 (have an upset stomach)

Definition: To attach, add, or append something to something else; to be close to or near.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 附近 (nearby), 附加 (additional), and 附件 (attachment)

Definition: Crude, shabby, or inferior in quality; also refers to something that is narrow-minded or lacking in refinement.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 简陋 (simple and crude), 陋习 (bad habit), and 丑陋 (ugly)

Definition: To accompany or keep someone company; to be with someone during an activity or period of time.
Usage: Common in phrases like 陪我 (accompany me), 陪伴 (to accompany), 陪同 (to escort)

Definition: Rain; precipitation that falls from clouds as water droplets.
Usage: Used in weather expressions like 下雨 (xià yǔ - to rain) and compound words related to rain

Definition: Snow; frozen precipitation that falls as white flakes from the sky.
Usage: Common in weather expressions like 下雪 (to snow) and 雪天 (snowy day)

Definition: A page, as in a book, document, or website. It refers to a single sheet or side of paper in printed or digital materials.
Usage: Common in words like 网页 (webpage), 页面 (page), 首页 (homepage)

Definition: To float, drift, or flutter in the air, typically describing light objects moved by wind or air currents.
Usage: Commonly used with leaves, snow, flags, or hair, as in 雪花飘 (snowflakes drift) or 头发飘 (hair flutters)

Definition: To decorate or adorn; also refers to ornaments, accessories, or decorations themselves.
Usage: Common in words like 装饰 (decoration), 首饰 (jewelry), and 饰演 (to play a role/act as)

Definition: A flat, round cake or pastry; any food item that is flat and round in shape like pancakes, cookies, or flatbreads.
Usage: Common in words like 月饼 (mooncake), 煎饼 (pancake), 饼干 (cookie/biscuit)

Definition: Fragrant, aromatic, or sweet-smelling; also describes food that smells or tastes delicious.
Usage: Common in expressions like 香水 (perfume), 很香 (smells good), or 吃得很香 (eating with great appetite)

Definition: A character component meaning skeleton or skull, rarely used alone but appears in compound words related to bones and death.
Usage: Most commonly seen in 骷髅 (kūlóu) meaning skeleton or skull

Definition: Skull or skeleton, specifically referring to the bones of the head after death.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the compound word 骷髅 (kūlóu) meaning 'skeleton' or 'skull'

Definition: Fish; refers to aquatic animals with fins and gills that live in water.
Usage: Used both as a standalone noun and in compound words like 鱼肉 (fish meat) or 金鱼 (goldfish)

Definition: Scale, as in the small overlapping plates that cover the skin of fish and reptiles.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 鱼鳞 (fish scales) and 鳞片 (scale/flake)

Definition: Deer; a hoofed mammal known for its antlers and graceful appearance.
Usage: Often appears in compound words like 麋鹿 (elk) or 驯鹿 (reindeer), and in place names

Definition: A mole (the small burrowing mammal with tiny eyes that lives underground).
Usage: Almost always used in the compound word 鼹鼠 (yǎnshǔ, mole)

Definition: Abundant, plentiful, or rich; often describes a good harvest, wealth, or fullness.
Usage: Common in words like 丰富 (fēngfù - abundant/rich) and 丰收 (fēngshōu - bumper harvest)

Definition: To string together or connect in a series; a string or cluster of things linked together (like beads on a string or a bunch of grapes)
Usage: Common in words like 串烧 (skewered food), 一串钥匙 (a bunch of keys), or 串门 (to visit neighbors)

Definition: To suffer a loss or deficit, especially in business or financial contexts; to be deficient or lacking.
Usage: Common in expressions like 亏本 (lose money in business) or 多亏 (thanks to, luckily)

Definition: Mutual, reciprocal, or each other; indicates an action or relationship that goes both ways between two or more parties.
Usage: Commonly used in compound words like 互相 (hùxiāng, mutually) and 互联网 (hùliánwǎng, Internet)

Definition: A warehouse or storehouse; a place for storing goods, grain, or materials.
Usage: Commonly seen in compounds like 仓库 (warehouse) and 粮仓 (granary)

Definition: Ceremony, ritual, or appearance; also refers to instruments or apparatus used for measuring or observation.
Usage: Common in words like 仪式 (ceremony), 仪器 (instrument), and 礼仪 (etiquette)

Definition: To look upward or tilt one's head/face up; to admire or respect someone.
Usage: Common in words like 仰望 (to look up at), 信仰 (faith/belief), and 仰慕 (to admire)

Definition: An umbrella or parasol used for protection from rain or sun.
Usage: Common in phrases like 雨伞 (yǔsǎn, rain umbrella) and 打伞 (dǎsǎn, to hold/open an umbrella)

Definition: To estimate, assess, or appraise the value or amount of something. Often used when making rough calculations or judgments about quantity, price, or situation.
Usage: Common in words like 估计 (gūjì - to estimate) and 评估 (pínggū - to evaluate)

Definition: To bless, protect, or help from above; divine protection or assistance.
Usage: Often used in religious or formal contexts, commonly seen in names and phrases like 保佑 (bǎoyòu - to bless and protect)

Definition: Remaining, surplus, or extra; refers to what is left over after the main part has been used or taken away.
Usage: Common in words like 其余 (the rest), 业余 (spare time/amateur), and 多余 (superfluous)

Definition: To supply, provide, or furnish something to someone; to make offerings (especially in religious or ceremonial contexts).
Usage: Common in words like 供应 (supply), 提供 (provide), and 供奉 (make offerings to)

Definition: To depend on, rely on, or lean against something or someone. Also means 'according to' when used in formal contexts.
Usage: Common in words like 依靠 (to rely on), 依然 (still, as before), and 依照 (according to)

Definition: To insult, humiliate, or treat with contempt; to bully or abuse someone.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 侮辱 (wǔrǔ - to insult/humiliate) and 欺侮 (qīwǔ - to bully)

Definition: Means 'all' or 'together', indicating that multiple things or people share the same quality or action simultaneously. This is a formal or literary term.
Usage: Common in set phrases like 面面俱到 (comprehensive) and 俱乐部 (club, literally 'all happy place')

Definition: A measure word meaning 'times' or 'fold', used to express multiples or multiplication. Indicates how many times larger one quantity is compared to another.
Usage: Common in phrases like 两倍 (two times/double), 三倍 (three times/triple), or 成倍增长 (multiply/increase by multiples)

Definition: To lean, tilt, or incline; to pour out or empty. Also means to overturn or collapse, and figuratively to devote all one's resources or effort to something.
Usage: Common in words like 倾斜 (to tilt), 倾听 (to listen attentively), and 倾向 (tendency, inclination)

Definition: Healthy, strong, or robust; relates to physical health and well-being.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 健康 (jiànkāng, health) and 健身 (jiànshēn, fitness/exercise)

Definition: Means 'occasional' or 'by chance'; also refers to a puppet, idol, or statue. Commonly seen in the word 偶尔 (ǒu'ěr) meaning 'occasionally' or 'once in a while'.
Usage: Frequently used in 偶尔 (occasionally), 偶然 (accidentally/by chance), and 偶像 (idol)

Definition: A numerical unit meaning million (10^6) in modern usage, or trillion (10^12) in traditional contexts; also means omen or sign.
Usage: Commonly used in large numbers like 兆字节 (megabyte) or to indicate portents

Definition: Cautious, careful, or fearful; describes being meticulous and conscientious in one's actions.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the compound word 兢兢业业 (jīngjīng-yèyè), meaning 'conscientious and diligent'

Definition: A classical Chinese particle used for emphasis or to mark a pause in poetry and ancient texts, similar to 'ah' or 'oh' in English.
Usage: Mainly found in classical poetry and literary works, rarely used in modern Chinese

Definition: Describes water or air that is extremely cold, icy, or biting. Often used in literary or descriptive contexts to emphasize the piercing quality of coldness.
Usage: Commonly seen in compounds like 清冽 (qīngliè, clear and cold) or 凛冽 (lǐnliè, bitterly cold)

Definition: Describes a feeling or atmosphere that is desolate, miserable, or bleak. Often used to convey sadness, loneliness, or a chilly, dreary environment.
Usage: Commonly appears in literary contexts and compound words like 凄凉 (qīliáng, desolate) or 凄惨 (qīcǎn, miserable)

Definition: Cool or cold in temperature; describes something that is pleasantly cool or has become cold.
Usage: Commonly used for weather, drinks, or food, as in 凉水 (cold water) or 天气很凉 (the weather is cool)

Definition: To rise high above; to soar or tower over something. Also means to approach or reach (a time), or to insult/encroach upon.
Usage: Common in words like 凌晨 (língchén, early morning/dawn) and 欺凌 (qīlíng, to bully)

Definition: Describes bitterly cold weather or a stern, awe-inspiring manner that commands respect or fear.
Usage: Often seen in literary contexts like 凛冽 (bitterly cold) or 威风凛凛 (awe-inspiring)

Definition: Triumph or victory; a song of triumph. This character represents success and triumphant return, often used in literary or formal contexts.
Usage: Commonly appears in names and compounds like 凯旋 (triumphant return) or 凯歌 (song of victory)

Definition: A knife or blade; a cutting tool with a sharp edge used for cutting, chopping, or slicing.
Usage: Common in words like 菜刀 (kitchen knife), 刀子 (small knife), and 剪刀 (scissors)

Definition: To publish or print; a publication such as a magazine, journal, or periodical.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 杂志刊 (magazine), 期刊 (periodical), and 刊登 (to publish/print an article)

Definition: To judge, decide, or distinguish; to sentence or make a ruling in a legal context
Usage: Common in words like 判断 (to judge/determine) and 裁判 (referee/judge)

Definition: To brake or stop suddenly; also refers to a Buddhist temple or monastery (in this sense, often pronounced chà).
Usage: Most commonly seen in 刹车 (shāchē, to brake) or 古刹 (gǔchà, ancient temple)

Definition: To peel, pare, or cut off (a thin layer or surface) using a knife or similar tool.
Usage: Commonly used for peeling fruit or sharpening pencils, as in 削苹果 (peel an apple) or 削铅笔 (sharpen a pencil)

Definition: A sword, specifically a double-edged straight sword used in Chinese martial arts and ancient warfare.
Usage: Common in martial arts contexts like 剑术 (swordsmanship) and historical or fantasy literature

Definition: To cut out or gouge out something, typically by digging or carving with a knife or sharp tool.
Usage: Often used in contexts like removing rotten parts from fruit or vegetables, or carving out holes

Definition: To peel, strip, or remove the outer layer or skin from something, such as fruit, bark, or paint.
Usage: Commonly used with objects like 剥皮 (peel skin), 剥壳 (shell/peel), 剥橘子 (peel an orange)

Definition: Means vigorous, flourishing, or suddenly rising; describes something bursting forth with energy or vitality.
Usage: Most commonly seen in compounds like 勃勃 (bóbó, vigorous) as in 生机勃勃 (full of vitality) or 勃然大怒 (to fly into a rage)

Definition: Merit, meritorious deed, or outstanding achievement, especially in military or public service. Often refers to honors or distinctions awarded for exceptional contributions.
Usage: Commonly seen in formal contexts like 勋章 (medal), 功勋 (meritorious service), or in names

Definition: A spoon or ladle used for scooping and serving food or liquids.
Usage: Common in compound words like 汤勺 (soup spoon) and 勺子 (spoon)

Definition: To hook, tick, or check off; to draw or sketch an outline. Also means to evoke or arouse (memories, interest).
Usage: Common in 勾选 (to check/tick a box) and 勾起 (to evoke/bring back)

Definition: A character primarily used in the word 匈牙利 (Xiōngyálì), meaning Hungary, and historically in 匈奴 (Xiōngnú), referring to an ancient nomadic people.
Usage: Rarely used alone; almost exclusively appears in compound words related to Hungary or historical references

Definition: A measure word (classifier) used for counting horses and bolts of cloth. Also means 'to match' or 'to equal' in literary contexts.
Usage: Commonly seen in 一匹马 (one horse) or 一匹布 (one bolt of cloth)

Definition: To sell; to offer goods or services in exchange for money.
Usage: Common in phrases like 卖东西 (to sell things) or 出卖 (to sell out/betray)

Definition: Misfortune, disaster, or adversity; refers to bad luck or difficult circumstances.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 厄运 (bad luck) and 灾厄 (calamity)

Definition: Toilet or restroom. This character is most commonly seen in the compound word 厕所 (cèsuǒ), meaning bathroom or lavatory.
Usage: Usually appears in 厕所 (toilet/restroom) or 公厕 (public toilet)

Definition: To hang or suspend something from above; to lift or hoist up with a rope or cable.
Usage: Common in words like 吊灯 (chandelier, hanging lamp) and 吊桥 (suspension bridge)

Definition: To tell or instruct someone to do something; to give orders or directions.
Usage: Almost always used in the compound word 吩咐 (fēnfù), meaning 'to tell/instruct'

Definition: To choke on something (like water, smoke, or spicy food) that irritates the throat or nose, causing coughing or discomfort.
Usage: Commonly used when water goes down the wrong way (呛水) or when smoke irritates the throat (被烟呛到)

Definition: To tell or instruct someone to do something; to give orders or directions.
Usage: Almost always used in the compound word 吩咐 (fēnfù), meaning 'to tell/instruct'

Definition: An onomatopoeia representing a hissing or sizzling sound, like air escaping or something frying.
Usage: Often used to describe sounds made by snakes, steam, or hot oil

Definition: Salty; having a salty taste, the opposite of sweet or bland.
Usage: Commonly used to describe food, as in 咸菜 (salted vegetables) or 太咸了 (too salty)

Definition: An onomatopoeia describing a loud, rushing sound, such as water flowing or a crowd making noise. Often used to express sudden, noisy commotion.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 哗啦 (huālā, crashing sound) or 哗然 (huárán, in an uproar)

Definition: A whistle or sentry post; refers to both the device used to make a sharp sound and a guard station or patrol position.
Usage: Common in words like 口哨 (kǒushào - whistle), 哨兵 (shàobīng - sentry), and 放哨 (fàngshào - to stand guard)

Definition: To ridicule, mock, or make fun of someone in a scornful way.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 嘲笑 (cháoxiào - to laugh at/mock) and 嘲讽 (cháofěng - to satirize/ridicule)

Definition: An onomatopoeia representing the sound of laughter, giggling, or chuckling.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the expression 嘻嘻 (xīxī) meaning 'hehe' or giggling sounds

Definition: An onomatopoeia representing rumbling, muttering, or gurgling sounds. Often used in reduplication (噜噜) to describe continuous low sounds.
Usage: Commonly appears in compounds like 嘟噜 (dūlu, to mutter) or 咕噜 (gūlu, gurgling sound)

Definition: To close one's mouth tightly; to keep silent or be unable to speak, often due to cold, fear, or being forced into silence.
Usage: Commonly seen in the expression 噤声 (jìnshēng, to fall silent) or 噤若寒蝉 (jìn ruò hán chán, silent as a cicada in cold weather, meaning too frightened to speak)

Definition: To chew or masticate food with the teeth and mouth. This pronunciation is used in formal or literary contexts.
Usage: Often appears in written language or formal speech; the more common colloquial pronunciation is jiáo

Definition: A chimney or window; an opening in a roof or wall that allows smoke to escape or light to enter.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the compound word 烟囱 (yāncōng) meaning chimney

Definition: Earth, soil, or dirt; also refers to land or ground. Can mean 'local' or 'unsophisticated' when used as an adjective.
Usage: Common in words like 土地 (land), 土豆 (potato), and 本土 (native/local)

Definition: A raised platform or altar used for ceremonies or rituals; also refers to a jar or earthen vessel for storing wine or food.
Usage: Common in words like 天坛 (Temple of Heaven), 论坛 (forum), or 酒坛 (wine jar)

Definition: A grave or tomb; a burial mound where deceased people are buried.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 坟墓 (fénmù, grave) and 上坟 (shàngfén, to visit a grave)

Definition: Flat, smooth, or level; also means open, frank, or candid when describing character or behavior.
Usage: Common in words like 坦白 (frank/honest) and 坦克 (tank - the vehicle)

Definition: Model, type, or style; refers to a particular form, pattern, or category of something.
Usage: Commonly used in compound words like 类型 (type/category), 血型 (blood type), 发型 (hairstyle), or 大型 (large-scale)

Definition: Dust or dirt; also used as a transliteration character in foreign place names and scientific terms (like angstrom unit).
Usage: Most commonly seen in 埃及 (Egypt) and scientific contexts

Definition: Can bear, endure, or withstand something; to be worthy of or capable of doing something.
Usage: Often used in literary or formal contexts, commonly seen in phrases like 不堪 (unbearable) or 堪称 (can be called/worthy of being called)

Definition: To mold, shape, or model something; refers to creating forms from materials like clay or plastic.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 塑料 (plastic), 塑造 (to mold/shape), and 雕塑 (sculpture)

Definition: To fill in, fill out, or stuff something into a space or container. Commonly used when completing forms, filling blanks, or filling physical spaces.
Usage: Used in expressions like 填表 (fill out a form) and 填空 (fill in the blank)

Definition: Boundary, border, or territory; also refers to a state, condition, or realm (physical or abstract)
Usage: Common in words like 环境 (environment), 境界 (realm/level), 困境 (difficult situation), and 出境 (exit a country)

Definition: To increase, add, or grow in quantity or degree. This verb indicates something becoming greater or more numerous.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 增加 (to increase), 增长 (to grow), and 增强 (to strengthen)

Definition: Strong, robust, or sturdy; describes physical strength or an impressive, magnificent appearance.
Usage: Common in words like 强壮 (strong/robust), 壮观 (spectacular), and 壮大 (to grow in strength)

Definition: To praise, compliment, or boast about someone or something.
Usage: Common in phrases like 夸奖 (to praise) and 夸张 (to exaggerate)

Definition: Literary word meaning 'how' or 'what can be done about'; expresses helplessness or inability to deal with a situation.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the set phrase 无奈 (wú nài) meaning 'helpless' or 'have no choice but to'

Definition: Slave or servant; a person who is owned by or in servitude to another person. In modern usage, often appears in compound words or historical contexts.
Usage: Common in words like 奴隶 (slave), 奴才 (lackey), or as a humble self-reference in classical Chinese

Definition: An imperial concubine or consort; a wife of an emperor or king who ranks below the empress.
Usage: Commonly seen in historical contexts and period dramas, such as 贵妃 (imperial concubine) or 王妃 (princess consort)

Definition: To hinder, obstruct, or interfere with something or someone.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the word 妨碍 (fáng'ài - to hinder/obstruct) and the phrase 不妨 (bùfáng - might as well/there's no harm in)

Definition: Posture, gesture, or appearance; refers to the physical form or manner in which someone carries themselves or how something looks.
Usage: Common in words like 姿态 (posture/attitude), 姿势 (pose/position), and 舞姿 (dancing posture)

Definition: A character meaning graceful or elegant, primarily used in female names and transliterations of foreign names.
Usage: Commonly seen in names like 安娜 (Anna) or 娜娜 (Nana)

Definition: Peaceful, tranquil, or calm; also means 'would rather' or 'preferably' when used in certain expressions.
Usage: Common in phrases like 宁可 (would rather) and as part of place names like 南宁 (Nanning)

Definition: An official or government officer; refers to someone who holds a position of authority in government or public administration.
Usage: Common in words like 官员 (government official), 警官 (police officer), and 法官 (judge)

Definition: Treasure, precious thing, or jewel; something valuable or cherished.
Usage: Common in words like 宝贝 (baby/treasure), 珠宝 (jewelry), and as a term of endearment

Definition: To spoil, pamper, or dote on someone; to show excessive favor or affection.
Usage: Commonly used in 宠物 (pet, literally 'pampered thing') and 宠爱 (to dote on/spoil with love)

Definition: Wide or broad in physical dimension; can also mean lenient or tolerant when describing attitudes or treatment.
Usage: Commonly used to describe physical width (宽度 width, 宽敞 spacious) or generous/forgiving behavior (宽容 tolerant)

Definition: To sleep or fall asleep; a literary or formal term for sleeping.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the idiom 夜不能寐 (unable to sleep at night) or literary texts

Definition: Means 'brand new' or 'outstanding/prominent'. Most commonly seen in the compound word 崭新 (zhǎnxīn) meaning 'brand new'.
Usage: Primarily used in the set phrase 崭新 (brand new) or 崭露头角 (to reveal one's talent)

Definition: A young child or offspring; also used colloquially to refer to young animals or as a dialectal term for 'son' or 'kid'.
Usage: Common in southern Chinese dialects; can be affectionate or casual depending on context

Definition: To celebrate or congratulate; a celebration or festive occasion
Usage: Common in words like 庆祝 (celebrate), 国庆 (National Day), and 欢庆 (joyfully celebrate)

Definition: Health, healthy, or well-being; also means peaceful or prosperous.
Usage: Most commonly seen in compounds like 健康 (jiànkāng, health) and 康复 (kāngfù, to recover from illness)

Definition: Outline, contour, or broad expanse; refers to the general shape or boundary of something. Can also mean to expand or clear out.
Usage: Most commonly seen in compound words like 轮廓 (lúnkuò - outline/contour) and 廓清 (kuòqīng - to clarify)

Definition: To abandon, discard, or give up something or someone. It conveys the act of leaving behind or renouncing.
Usage: Common in words like 放弃 (fàngqì - to give up) and 抛弃 (pāoqì - to abandon)

Definition: An arc or curved line, especially in geometry or mathematics. Refers to any curved segment that is part of a circle or curve.
Usage: Common in mathematical terms like 弧线 (arc line) and 弧度 (radian)

Definition: To record, write down, or register information; also means a record or register itself.
Usage: Common in words like 记录 (jìlù - to record), 录音 (lùyīn - to record audio), 录取 (lùqǔ - to admit/enroll)

Definition: Law, rule, or regulation; also refers to rhythm or musical pitch in classical contexts.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 法律 (fǎlǜ - law), 纪律 (jìlǜ - discipline), and 律师 (lǜshī - lawyer)

Definition: To avoid, abstain from, or be jealous of something; to have a taboo against something
Usage: Common in words like 忌口 (dietary restriction), 禁忌 (taboo), and 妒忌 (jealousy)

Definition: Will, aspiration, or ambition; refers to one's determination, goals, or resolve to achieve something.
Usage: Common in words like 志愿 (volunteer/aspiration), 意志 (willpower), and 同志 (comrade)

Definition: Worried or anxious; describes a state of mental unease or concern.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the compound word 忡忡 (chōngchōng) meaning 'worried' or in the phrase 忧心忡忡 (yōuxīn-chōngchōng) meaning 'deeply worried'

Definition: To be stunned, dazed, or in a trance; describes a momentary state of being frozen or blank due to surprise, shock, or deep thought.
Usage: Often used in compounds like 发怔 (fāzhēng - to be in a daze) or 怔住 (zhēngzhù - to be stunned/frozen in place)

Definition: Means 'fear' or 'to be afraid'. This character is rarely used alone in modern Chinese.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the compound word 恐怖 (kǒngbù) meaning 'terror' or 'horrible'

Definition: Nature, character, or quality of something; also refers to sex or gender. Commonly used as a suffix to form abstract nouns indicating properties or characteristics.
Usage: Found in words like 性格 (personality), 女性 (female), 可能性 (possibility), 重要性 (importance)

Definition: Timid, cowardly, or lacking courage; describes someone who is afraid or hesitant to act.
Usage: Often used in words like 胆怯 (dǎnqiè - timid) or 怯场 (qièchǎng - stage fright)

Definition: Describes being sick, weak, or in low spirits; feeling listless or dispirited.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the compound word 恹恹 (yan1yan1), meaning sickly or dejected

Definition: To suffer from or contract (an illness or disease); can also mean worry, anxiety, or disaster as a noun.
Usage: Commonly used in medical contexts like 患病 (to fall ill) or 患者 (patient)

Definition: Haggard, worn out, or exhausted in appearance, especially referring to someone's face or physical condition due to worry, illness, or hardship.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the compound word 憔悴 (qiáo cuì), meaning haggard or worn

Definition: To cherish, value, or treasure something; to feel regret or pity about losing or wasting something.
Usage: Common in words like 可惜 (kěxī - what a pity) and 珍惜 (zhēnxī - to treasure)

Definition: Miserable, tragic, or terrible; describes situations or conditions that are extremely bad or unfortunate.
Usage: Common in expressions like 惨败 (crushing defeat), 悲惨 (tragic), or 好惨 (so miserable)

Definition: To punish or penalize someone for wrongdoing; to discipline or impose consequences for bad behavior.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 惩罚 (chéngfá - punishment) and 惩治 (chéngzhì - to punish)

Definition: To be stunned, dazed, or blank; to stare blankly in a distracted or confused state.
Usage: Often used to describe someone frozen in surprise or lost in thought, as in 发愣 (to be in a daze) or 愣住了 (to be stunned/frozen)

Definition: To feel ashamed, guilty, or embarrassed about something; to have a sense of remorse or inadequacy.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 惭愧 (ashamed), 愧疚 (guilty), and 问心无愧 (have a clear conscience)

Definition: To admire, yearn for, or long for someone or something with respect and affection.
Usage: Often seen in formal or literary contexts, such as 羡慕 (xiànmù - to envy/admire) or 爱慕 (àimù - to adore)

Definition: Describes a haggard, worn-out, or exhausted appearance, especially in one's face due to worry, illness, or fatigue.
Usage: Almost always used in the compound word 憔悴 (qiáocuì), meaning haggard or worn out

Definition: A conjunction meaning 'or' that presents alternatives or choices between two or more options.
Usage: Used in statements like 你或我 (you or me), 今天或明天 (today or tomorrow)

Definition: Relative or family member; also means sorrow or grief in literary contexts.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the compound word 亲戚 (qīnqi, relatives)

Definition: To carry or lift something heavy on one's shoulder or with both hands raised above the head.
Usage: Often used for carrying heavy objects like bags, poles, or equipment, as in 扛着大包 (carrying a big bag on the shoulder)

Definition: To raise, lift up, or hoist something; to spread or make known (such as fame or reputation).
Usage: Common in words like 表扬 (to praise), 飘扬 (to flutter), and 发扬 (to develop/carry forward)

Definition: To restrain, suppress, or hold back (emotions, actions, or forces); to inhibit or repress something.
Usage: Commonly seen in formal contexts and compounds like 抑制 (to suppress/restrain) and 压抑 (to depress/repress)

Definition: To throw, toss, or fling something through the air. Can also mean to abandon or discard something.
Usage: Common in phrases like 抛球 (throw a ball) and 抛弃 (abandon/forsake)

Definition: To wipe, smear, or apply something by spreading it across a surface; to erase or cross out.
Usage: Common in phrases like 抹桌子 (wipe the table) or 抹口红 (apply lipstick)

Definition: To carry or hold something by hand, especially with fingers or by a handle, often dangling at one's side.
Usage: Commonly used for carrying bags, baskets, or items with handles, as in 拎包 (carry a bag)

Definition: Clumsy, awkward, or lacking skill; also used in humble expressions to refer to one's own work or abilities.
Usage: Often seen in formal or literary contexts, such as 拙见 (my humble opinion) or 笨拙 (clumsy)

Definition: To move or shift something from one place to another, typically by pushing or sliding it slightly.
Usage: Commonly used for moving furniture, objects, or one's body position, as in 挪动 (to shift/move)

Definition: To shake, vibrate, or invigorate; to rouse or stimulate into action or energy.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 振动 (vibrate), 振作 (pull oneself together), and 振奋 (inspire/invigorate)

Definition: To catch, seize, or grab something or someone, especially with hands or by pursuing.
Usage: Common in phrases like 捉鱼 (catch fish) and 捉迷藏 (play hide-and-seek)

Definition: To bring or take something to someone along the way; to deliver a message or item for someone as a favor while going somewhere.
Usage: Commonly used in phrases like 捎个口信 (deliver a message) or 捎带 (bring along)

Definition: To catch, capture, or seize something or someone, especially animals or criminals.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 捕鱼 (to catch fish), 逮捕 (to arrest), and 捕捉 (to capture)

Definition: To hold or carry something with both hands, usually cupped together; can also mean to praise or flatter someone excessively.
Usage: Commonly used for holding objects like 捧着花 (holding flowers) or in expressions like 捧场 (to support/show up for someone)

Definition: Victory, triumph, or success; also means quick, nimble, or agile.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 捷报 (news of victory), 快捷 (fast and convenient), and 敏捷 (agile)

Definition: To plunder, loot, or seize by force; to sweep past or graze lightly over something.
Usage: Common in words like 掠夺 (lüèduó - to plunder) and 掠过 (lüèguò - to sweep past)

Definition: To cover, conceal, or hide something from view; to close or shut (like a door).
Usage: Common in words like 掩盖 (to cover up), 掩饰 (to disguise), and 掩护 (to shield/protect)

Definition: To grab, pull, or clutch tightly with the hand, often with a twisting motion. Can also mean to seize or hold onto something or someone firmly.
Usage: Commonly used in expressions like 揪住 (to grab hold of) or 揪心 (heart-wrenching, literally 'clutching the heart')

Definition: To place or put something down; to set aside or shelve something.
Usage: Commonly used in everyday speech for placing objects, like 把书搁在桌子上 (put the book on the table)

Definition: To stir, mix, or agitate something by moving it around in a circular motion. Can also mean to disturb or disrupt.
Usage: Commonly used in cooking contexts like 搅拌 (jiǎobàn - to stir/mix) or 搅动 (jiǎodòng - to stir up)

Definition: To pick, pluck, or take off something (like fruit, flowers, or accessories). Can also mean to extract or select portions from written text.
Usage: Common in phrases like 摘苹果 (pick apples), 摘眼镜 (take off glasses), 摘要 (summary/abstract)

Definition: To prop up, support, or hold up something with force; also means to push or pole a boat, or to be overly full (from eating).
Usage: Common in phrases like 撑伞 (hold up an umbrella), 撑船 (pole a boat), or 吃撑了 (ate too much/stuffed)

Definition: To broadcast, transmit, or spread (information, media, or seeds). Most commonly used in the context of radio, television, or online media transmission.
Usage: Found in words like 广播 (broadcast), 播放 (to play/broadcast), and 直播 (live broadcast)

Definition: To gather up or pinch together with fingers; a small pinch or handful of something (as a measure word)
Usage: Used for small amounts like 一撮盐 (a pinch of salt) or to describe the action of picking up with fingers

Definition: To be good at or skilled in something; to excel at a particular ability or field.
Usage: Commonly used in the phrase 擅长 (shàncháng) meaning 'to be good at'

Definition: To change, alter, or modify something; to correct or revise.
Usage: Common in phrases like 改变 (to change), 修改 (to revise), and 改正 (to correct)

Definition: Effect, result, or efficacy; to imitate or follow someone's example.
Usage: Common in words like 效果 (effect/result), 有效 (effective), and 效率 (efficiency)

Definition: Slanted, tilted, or diagonal; not straight or perpendicular. Can describe physical angles or positions that are at an incline.
Usage: Common in words like 斜坡 (slope), 倾斜 (to tilt), and 斜线 (diagonal line)

Definition: Crystal or bright and sparkling; refers to something clear, transparent, or shining like a crystal.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 水晶 (crystal), 晶莹 (sparkling/glistening), and 结晶 (crystallization)

Definition: Wisdom, intelligence, or knowledge; the ability to think clearly and make good judgments.
Usage: Commonly found in words like 智慧 (wisdom), 智能 (intelligence), and 理智 (reason)

Definition: Warm or mild in temperature; can also describe warmth in an emotional or heartfelt sense.
Usage: Common in weather descriptions like 天气很暖 (the weather is warm) and emotional contexts like 温暖 (warmth/warm-hearted)

Definition: Hazy, dim, or obscure; describes something that is unclear or blurred, especially related to vision or light.
Usage: Most commonly used in the compound word 朦胧 (ménglóng) meaning hazy or misty

Definition: End, final part, or tip of something; refers to the last stage or conclusion of a period of time or object.
Usage: Common in words like 周末 (weekend), 末尾 (end/tail), and 年末 (year-end)

Definition: A plum (the fruit); most commonly used as one of the most popular Chinese surnames.
Usage: Frequently seen in names like 李明 (Li Ming) or 李老师 (Teacher Li)

Definition: To construct, form, or compose something; to build or make up a structure or system.
Usage: Commonly used in compound words like 结构 (structure), 构成 (to constitute), and 构建 (to construct)

Definition: To dye or stain something; to be infected or contaminated by something.
Usage: Common in words like 染发 (to dye hair), 感染 (to infect), and 污染 (to pollute)

Definition: A character used primarily in the word for lemon (柠檬, níngméng). It refers to a type of citrus tree but is rarely used alone.
Usage: Almost always appears in the compound word 柠檬 (lemon)

Definition: Willow tree, a type of tree with long, drooping branches and narrow leaves. Often associated with grace and flexibility in Chinese culture.
Usage: Commonly seen in place names, poetry, and surnames like 柳树 (willow tree)

Definition: To perch, roost, or dwell; refers to birds resting on branches or people living/staying in a place.
Usage: Commonly seen in literary or formal contexts, such as 栖息 (to inhabit/dwell)

Definition: The tip, top, or end of something, especially the end of a tree branch or twig.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 树梢 (treetop) and 眉梢 (tip of the eyebrow)

Definition: An edge, corner, or ridge where two surfaces meet; also refers to the angular lines or corners of an object.
Usage: Commonly used in geometric terms like 棱角 (edges and corners) or 棱镜 (prism)

Definition: To plant or grow vegetation; refers to plants in general.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 植物 (zhíwù, plant) and 种植 (zhòngzhí, to cultivate)

Definition: Horizontal, crosswise, or sideways; describes something positioned from side to side rather than up and down.
Usage: Common in words like 横线 (horizontal line) and 纵横 (vertical and horizontal)

Definition: Oak tree or rubber tree; commonly refers to rubber-related materials.
Usage: Most frequently seen in compounds like 橡胶 (rubber) and 橡树 (oak tree)

Definition: A cupboard, cabinet, or closet used for storage or display. Most commonly seen in compound words related to furniture for storing items.
Usage: Found in words like 橱柜 (chúguì - cabinet) and 橱窗 (chúchuāng - display window)

Definition: A character component meaning 'lemon' that rarely appears alone but is commonly used in compound words.
Usage: Most frequently seen in 柠檬 (níngméng) meaning 'lemon'

Definition: Apology or regret; feeling sorry or apologetic about something. Most commonly used in the word 抱歉 (bàoqiàn) meaning 'sorry' or 'to apologize'.
Usage: Typically appears in apology expressions like 道歉 (dàoqiàn - to apologize) and 抱歉 (bàoqiàn - sorry)

Definition: Different, special, or exceptional; indicates something that stands out or is distinct from the ordinary.
Usage: Commonly seen in formal expressions like 特殊 (tèshū - special) and 殊不知 (shū bù zhī - little does one know)

Definition: To destroy, ruin, or damage something, often severely or completely. Can refer to physical destruction or damage to reputation.
Usage: Common in words like 毁坏 (to damage), 毁灭 (to annihilate), 销毁 (to destroy by burning)

Definition: Atmosphere or ambiance; refers to the mood, feeling, or general environment of a place or situation.
Usage: Most commonly used in the compound word 气氛 (qìfēn) meaning 'atmosphere' or 'ambiance'

Definition: Juice or liquid extracted from fruits, vegetables, or other substances.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 果汁 (fruit juice), 汤汁 (broth/gravy), and 墨汁 (ink)

Definition: Sweat or perspiration that comes from the body when hot or exercising.
Usage: Common in expressions like 出汗 (to sweat) and 流汗 (to perspire)

Definition: Soup or broth; any liquid food made by boiling ingredients in water.
Usage: Common in phrases like 鸡汤 (chicken soup) or 喝汤 (drink soup)

Definition: Onomatopoeia representing the sound of a dog barking, similar to 'woof' or 'bark' in English. Also used as a surname.
Usage: Commonly seen in children's books and when describing dog sounds; 汪汪 (wang1 wang1) means 'woof woof'

Definition: Describes the sound and force of turbulent, surging water; conveys a sense of violent or tumultuous movement.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the compound word 汹涌 (xiōngyǒng) meaning 'surging' or 'turbulent'

Definition: To touch or come into contact with a liquid and get it on something; to be stained or moistened by something.
Usage: Common in phrases like 沾水 (to get wet) or 沾光 (to benefit from association with someone)

Definition: To float or drift on water; to spread widely or overflow. Also means broad, general, or non-specific.
Usage: Common in compounds like 泛滥 (to flood/overflow) and 广泛 (widespread, extensive)

Definition: A bubble or foam; also means to soak or steep something in liquid.
Usage: Common in 泡茶 (make tea by steeping), 泡澡 (take a bath), and 气泡 (air bubble)

Definition: Continent; a large landmass on Earth. Also refers to large islands or land areas surrounded by water.
Usage: Used in words like 亚洲 (Asia), 欧洲 (Europe), 美洲 (Americas), 非洲 (Africa), 大洋洲 (Oceania)

Definition: A thick liquid or paste, often referring to starch paste, pulp, or various thick fluids like soybean milk.
Usage: Commonly seen in compounds like 豆浆 (soy milk), 浆糊 (paste), or 泥浆 (mud/slurry)

Definition: Thick, dense, or strong in concentration; describes liquids, colors, flavors, or atmospheres that are intense or concentrated.
Usage: Common in phrases like 浓茶 (strong tea), 浓雾 (thick fog), 浓厚 (dense/strong)

Definition: A wave in water; also means to wander or roam aimlessly, or to waste/squander (resources, time).
Usage: Common in words like 波浪 (waves), 浪费 (to waste), and 流浪 (to wander)

Definition: Tears or nasal mucus; refers to fluids that flow from the eyes or nose, especially when crying or having a runny nose.
Usage: Most commonly seen in literary or formal expressions like 涕泪 (tears) or 感激涕零 (moved to tears with gratitude)

Definition: Liquid or fluid; refers to any substance in liquid state as opposed to solid or gas.
Usage: Commonly seen in compounds like 液体 (liquid), 血液 (blood), 液晶 (liquid crystal)

Definition: To flood, submerge, or drown; to be covered or soaked by water.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 淹没 (to submerge) and 淹死 (to drown)

Definition: To add or increase something; to replenish or supplement what already exists.
Usage: Commonly used in phrases like 添加 (to add), 增添 (to increase), or 添麻烦 (to cause trouble)

Definition: To overflow or spill over; to exceed the normal limit or capacity
Usage: Commonly used in words like 洋溢 (brimming with), 溢出 (overflow), and 充溢 (filled to overflowing)

Definition: Describes water flowing abundantly or surging; often used to convey the image of vast, overflowing water.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the phrase 滔滔不绝 (tāotāo bùjué) meaning 'talking non-stop' or in 滔天 (tāotiān) meaning 'monstrous/overwhelming'

Definition: To stagnate, be blocked, or remain stuck without moving forward. Describes things that are delayed, sluggish, or not flowing smoothly.
Usage: Common in words like 停滞 (stagnation), 滞留 (be stranded), and 呆滞 (dull/lifeless)

Definition: To filter or strain liquids; to drip or trickle through a filter.
Usage: Often used in contexts involving filtering water, tea, or other liquids through cloth or mesh

Definition: Desert; also means indifferent or unconcerned when used in compound words.
Usage: Common in 沙漠 (desert) and 冷漠 (indifferent, cold)

Definition: To hide beneath the surface, dive, or submerge; can also mean hidden or latent.
Usage: Common in words like 潜水 (dive/scuba diving), 潜力 (potential), and 潜在 (latent/hidden)

Definition: Tide or tidal current; also means damp/moist, or trendy/fashionable in modern usage
Usage: Used in words like 潮流 (trend), 潮湿 (humid), and 高潮 (high tide/climax)

Definition: Disaster, calamity, or catastrophe. Refers to natural or man-made events that cause great damage or suffering.
Usage: Commonly used in compound words like 灾难 (disaster), 火灾 (fire disaster), 水灾 (flood)

Definition: To bake, roast, or dry something using heat or fire. Also means to set off or create a warm atmosphere.
Usage: Commonly used in cooking contexts like 烘烤 (to bake) or 烘干 (to dry with heat)

Definition: A classical Chinese particle used in literary texts, functioning as 'how', 'where', or 'therein'. In modern Chinese, it appears mainly in set phrases and classical expressions.
Usage: Found in classical idioms like 心不在焉 (absent-minded, literally 'heart not there')

Definition: To extinguish, put out, or go out (referring to fire, lights, or flames). It describes the action of stopping something from burning or shining.
Usage: Commonly used in phrases like 熄灯 (turn off lights) and 熄火 (turn off engine/fire goes out)

Definition: To smoke, fumigate, or cure food with smoke; to be affected or influenced by smoke, heat, or strong smells.
Usage: Common in cooking contexts like 熏肉 (smoked meat) or describing being affected by smoke/fumes

Definition: To boil or simmer for a long time; to endure or suffer through a difficult period
Usage: Used for cooking (熬粥 - to cook porridge) or enduring hardship (熬夜 - to stay up late)

Definition: To burn or ignite; to light something on fire. Can also mean combustion or flammable.
Usage: Common in words like 燃烧 (to burn), 燃料 (fuel), and 点燃 (to ignite)

Definition: To burn or scorch; refers to a fire burning fiercely or something being set ablaze.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the idiom 星火燎原 (a single spark can start a prairie fire)

Definition: Grandfather (paternal); also used as a respectful term for elderly men or as a suffix for certain male figures of authority or respect.
Usage: Common in family terms like 爷爷 (grandpa) and respectful titles like 大爷 (uncle/sir)

Definition: Refreshing, comfortable, or pleasant; describes a feeling of satisfaction or physical comfort. Can also mean straightforward or frank when describing personality.
Usage: Common in expressions like 凉爽 (cool and refreshing), 爽快 (straightforward), or colloquially 真爽 (feels great!)

Definition: Cow, ox, or cattle; a common domesticated farm animal. Also used colloquially to mean 'awesome' or 'impressive'.
Usage: Used literally for the animal (奶牛 dairy cow) or as slang to praise someone/something (你真牛 you're awesome)

Definition: Prison, jail, or cage; also means firm or secure when used as an adjective.
Usage: Common in words like 监牢 (prison) and 牢固 (firm, solid)

Definition: Cunning, crafty, or sly in a deceptive way. Describes someone who is clever but dishonest or tricky.
Usage: Most commonly seen in 狡猾 (jiǎohuá - cunning/crafty) and 狡辩 (jiǎobiàn - to argue sophistically)

Definition: Narrow or confined in width or scope; limited or restricted in extent.
Usage: Common in words like 狭窄 (narrow/cramped) and 狭隘 (narrow-minded)

Definition: Lion; a large wild cat known as the king of beasts
Usage: Commonly used in words like 狮子 (lion) and 狮子舞 (lion dance)

Definition: Prison or jail; a place where criminals are confined and detained.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 监狱 (jiānyù - prison) and 地狱 (dìyù - hell)

Definition: Sly, cunning, or crafty in a negative sense; describes someone who is deceitful or tricky.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the word 狡猾 (jiǎohuá) meaning cunning or sly

Definition: A character used primarily in the word for rose (玫瑰 méiguī). It rarely appears alone and has no independent meaning in modern Chinese.
Usage: Almost exclusively used in the compound word 玫瑰 (rose)

Definition: To carve, polish, or cut (jade or stone); to refine or perfect something through careful work.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the compound word 琢磨 (zuómó, to ponder/polish)

Definition: A traditional Chinese musical instrument with 25 strings, similar to a zither. Also used in literary contexts to describe rustling sounds or a cold, bleak atmosphere.
Usage: Most commonly seen in classical Chinese texts and the word 瑟瑟 (sèsè) meaning 'rustling' or 'shivering from cold'

Definition: Means 'magnificent', 'rare', or 'precious', often describing something extraordinary or valuable. Most commonly seen in the word 瑰宝 (guībǎo, treasure) and 玫瑰 (méiguī, rose).
Usage: Typically used in literary or formal contexts to describe precious objects or remarkable things

Definition: A flat, low-lying area of land suitable for farming; suburban or outlying areas. This character is rarely used alone in modern Chinese.
Usage: Most commonly seen in place names like 缅甸 (Myanmar/Burma) or in classical texts

Definition: Tired, exhausted, or fatigued. Describes a state of physical or mental weariness.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 疲劳 (pílào - tired/fatigued) and 疲倦 (píjuàn - weary)

Definition: Lame or crippled; describes someone who limps or has difficulty walking due to a leg injury or disability.
Usage: Commonly used as an adjective (瘸腿 - lame leg) or verb (他走路瘸了 - he walks with a limp)

Definition: Refers to skin diseases like scabies or mange; also means scabby or mangy. Often used to describe skin conditions with sores or scabs.
Usage: Commonly seen in compounds like 癞蛤蟆 (toad, literally 'scabby toad') or 癞皮狗 (mangy dog)

Definition: To be full, filled, or overflowing; to have surplus or profit. Often used in business contexts to indicate gains or abundance.
Usage: Common in words like 盈利 (profit), 充盈 (abundant), and 盈余 (surplus)

Definition: A helmet or protective headgear, typically made of metal or hard material. Used to refer to armor helmets worn by soldiers or protective helmets in modern contexts.
Usage: Common in compounds like 头盔 (tóukuī - helmet) and 钢盔 (gāngkuī - steel helmet)

Definition: Flourishing, prosperous, or vigorous; also means to fill or ladle (food/liquid) into a container.
Usage: Common in expressions like 盛开 (in full bloom), 茂盛 (lush), or 盛饭 (to serve rice)

Definition: To gaze into the distance or look far ahead, often from a high place or vantage point.
Usage: Commonly used in compounds like 眺望 (tiàowàng - to look out over) and 远眺 (yuǎntiào - to gaze into the distance)

Definition: To see or witness something, often used in formal or literary contexts.
Usage: Commonly appears in set phrases like 目睹 (mùdǔ - to witness with one's own eyes) and 有目共睹 (yǒu mù gòng dǔ - obvious to all)

Definition: To look at or glance at something; an informal, colloquial way to say 'to see' or 'to take a look'
Usage: Common in northern Chinese dialects and casual speech, as in 瞅瞅 (take a look)

Definition: To hide the truth from someone; to conceal or keep secret from another person.
Usage: Often used in phrases like 瞒着 (hide from) or 隐瞒 (conceal), typically when someone deliberately withholds information

Definition: To glance at or take a quick look at something or someone, often sideways or secretly.
Usage: Commonly used in expressions like 瞟一眼 (piǎo yī yǎn) meaning 'to take a quick glance'

Definition: A very brief moment or instant; to blink or wink. Refers to an extremely short period of time.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 瞬间 (shùnjiān - instant/moment) and 一瞬 (yīshùn - a split second)

Definition: Large, great, or substantial in size; commonly used in academic contexts to mean 'master's degree'
Usage: Most frequently seen in 硕士 (master's degree) and in formal or literary descriptions of size

Definition: Broken into small pieces or fragments; shattered or smashed. Can describe physical objects that have been crushed or broken apart.
Usage: Common in words like 破碎 (broken/shattered), 粉碎 (smashed to pieces), 碎片 (fragments)

Definition: A stone tablet or monument, typically inscribed with text to commemorate events, people, or achievements.
Usage: Commonly seen in compounds like 石碑 (stone tablet), 纪念碑 (memorial monument), 墓碑 (tombstone)

Definition: Evil spirit or demon; misfortune or harm caused by supernatural forces
Usage: Often seen in compound words like 作祟 (zuòsuì - to cause trouble/mischief) or in classical/literary contexts referring to supernatural harm

Definition: To call, to name, or to weigh; refers to addressing someone or something by a particular name or title, or measuring weight.
Usage: Common in expressions like 称呼 (to address/call), 称为 (to be called/known as), and 称重 (to weigh)

Definition: Stable, steady, or firm; describes something that is secure and not likely to change, move, or fail.
Usage: Commonly used to describe physical stability (稳定 steady), emotional composure (沉稳 calm), or reliable situations

Definition: To examine, investigate, or verify; to bow down or kowtow (in classical Chinese)
Usage: Most commonly seen in the compound word 稽查 (jīchá, to inspect) or the idiom 无稽之谈 (wújī zhī tán, absurd talk)

Definition: A hole, cave, or cavity in the ground or other surface. In traditional Chinese medicine, it also refers to acupuncture points on the body.
Usage: Common in words like 洞穴 (cave), 穴位 (acupuncture point), and 孔穴 (hole/opening)

Definition: To steal or take secretly without permission; to pilfer or commit theft
Usage: Often used in formal or written contexts, as in 窃取 (to steal/usurp) or 盗窃 (theft/burglary)

Definition: Narrow or tight, describing something that has little width or space. Opposite of 宽 (wide).
Usage: Commonly used to describe roads, clothing, or spaces, as in 窄路 (narrow road) or 太窄了 (too narrow)

Definition: To peep, spy, or look secretly at something through a small opening or gap. Often implies looking at something one shouldn't be viewing.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 窥视 (to peep at) and 窥探 (to pry into)

Definition: To compete or contend with others; to strive for superiority or victory.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 竞争 (competition), 竞赛 (contest), and 竞选 (run for election)

Definition: A symbol, mark, or sign used to represent something; also refers to a talisman or magical charm in traditional Chinese culture.
Usage: Common in words like 符号 (symbol), 音符 (musical note), and 护身符 (amulet)

Definition: A plan, strategy, or scheme; also means to whip or urge forward (a horse). In modern usage, most commonly refers to policies, strategies, or tactics.
Usage: Frequently appears in compound words like 政策 (policy), 对策 (countermeasure), 策略 (strategy)

Definition: Rice (uncooked grains); also the standard unit of length meaning 'meter'
Usage: Used in food contexts like 大米 (rice) and measurements like 三米 (three meters)

Definition: To stick or adhere to something; to glue or paste together.
Usage: Commonly used for things that are sticky or that attach to surfaces, like 粘贴 (to paste) or 粘住 (to stick to)

Definition: Rough, coarse, or unrefined in texture or quality; not smooth or polished.
Usage: Commonly used to describe rough surfaces, unpolished rice (糙米), or crude workmanship

Definition: Describes things falling, scattering, or appearing in great numbers or confusion; numerous and disorderly.
Usage: Most commonly seen in compounds like 纷纷 (one after another), 纷乱 (confused/chaotic), and 纷纷扬扬 (falling thickly, like snow)

Definition: Lines, stripes, or patterns on a surface; grain or texture. Can refer to natural markings like wood grain, fingerprints, or decorative patterns.
Usage: Common in words like 指纹 (fingerprint), 条纹 (stripes), 皱纹 (wrinkles)

Definition: To tie, bind, or fasten something with rope, string, or similar material. Can also mean to kidnap or take hostage.
Usage: Common in phrases like 绑架 (kidnap), 绑鞋带 (tie shoelaces), 绑定 (bind/link accounts)

Definition: Soft, fine hair or fur; also refers to velvet, down, or fluffy textile materials with a soft nap.
Usage: Common in words like 绒毛 (fine hair/down), 天鹅绒 (velvet), and 羽绒 (down feathers)

Definition: A strand, thread, or wisp of something; also used as a measure word for things that are thin and long like threads, smoke, or light.
Usage: Common in phrases like 一缕阳光 (a ray of sunlight) or 一缕头发 (a strand of hair)

Definition: To weave, knit, or braid together; to compile, edit, or organize information into a structured form
Usage: Common in words like 编辑 (to edit), 编织 (to weave), and 编号 (to number/code)

Definition: A jar, can, or pot used for storing or containing things. Commonly refers to containers made of metal, glass, or ceramic.
Usage: Used in words like 罐头 (canned food), 水罐 (water jar), 茶罐 (tea canister)

Definition: To punish or penalize someone for wrongdoing; to impose a fine or penalty.
Usage: Common in contexts like 罚款 (to fine), 惩罚 (to punish), or 罚球 (penalty kick/free throw)

Definition: To feel shy, bashful, or ashamed; describes the feeling of embarrassment or shyness in social situations.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 害羞 (hàixiū - shy) and 羞耻 (xiūchǐ - shame)

Definition: To envy or admire someone for what they have or can do; to feel a desire to have something that belongs to another person.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the word 羡慕 (xiànmù, to envy/admire)

Definition: Deaf; unable to hear or having severe hearing impairment.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 耳聋 (deaf) or 聋哑 (deaf-mute)

Definition: Duty, job, or position; refers to one's occupation, responsibility, or official post.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 职业 (zhíyè, occupation), 职位 (zhíwèi, position), and 职责 (zhízé, duty/responsibility)

Definition: To gather, assemble, or come together; to collect or accumulate people or things in one place.
Usage: Common in words like 聚会 (gathering/party), 团聚 (reunion), and 聚集 (to assemble)

Definition: Rib; the curved bones that form the chest cage in humans and animals.
Usage: Commonly seen in medical contexts and in the word 肋骨 (lèigǔ - rib bone)

Definition: Muscle or flesh tissue in the body. Also refers to skin in compounds.
Usage: Common in words like 肌肉 (muscle), 肌肤 (skin), and 心肌 (heart muscle)

Definition: The elbow, the joint connecting the upper arm and forearm.
Usage: Commonly used in body part vocabulary and phrases like 胳膊肘 (elbow) or 肘部 (elbow area)

Definition: Skin, referring to the outer covering of the human body or surface of something.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 皮肤 (pífū - skin), 肤色 (fūsè - skin color)

Definition: Fat, plump, or obese; can describe people, animals, or things that are thick or rich. Also means fertile when describing soil.
Usage: Common in phrases like 肥胖 (obese), 肥肉 (fatty meat), 肥料 (fertilizer)

Definition: Dirty or filthy; used primarily in the compound word 肮脏 (āngzāng) meaning dirty or unclean.
Usage: Rarely used alone; almost always appears in the word 肮脏 to describe physical dirtiness or moral corruption

Definition: The stomach, the digestive organ in the body. Used in medical contexts and when discussing digestion or stomach-related issues.
Usage: Common in phrases like 胃痛 (stomach ache) and 肠胃 (gastrointestinal)

Definition: Gallbladder (the organ); also means courage, bravery, or guts in a figurative sense.
Usage: Common in expressions like 胆量 (courage) and 大胆 (bold/daring)

Definition: To win, to defeat, or to be victorious in a competition or conflict. Can also mean to surpass or be superior to something.
Usage: Common in words like 胜利 (victory), 获胜 (to win), and 战胜 (to overcome)

Definition: Hazy, dim, or obscure; describes something that is not clear or distinct, especially in relation to light or vision.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the compound word 朦胧 (ménglóng) meaning 'hazy' or 'dim', as in 月色朦胧 (hazy moonlight)

Definition: Pus; the thick yellowish or greenish liquid produced in infected tissue or wounds.
Usage: Commonly used in medical contexts, such as 脓包 (pustule) or 化脓 (to fester/suppurate)

Definition: The spleen (organ in traditional Chinese medicine and anatomy); also refers to temperament or disposition.
Usage: Commonly seen in 脾气 (pí qi - temper) and medical contexts referring to the digestive system

Definition: Rotten, decayed, or spoiled; also refers to tofu (bean curd) in compound words. Can describe both physical decay and moral corruption.
Usage: Common in words like 豆腐 (tofu), 腐烂 (to rot), and 腐败 (corrupt)

Definition: A thin layer or membrane, such as biological tissue or a film-like covering.
Usage: Common in words like 薄膜 (thin film), 细胞膜 (cell membrane), and 角膜 (cornea)

Definition: To expand, swell, or inflate in size or volume.
Usage: Commonly used in compounds like 膨胀 (péngzhàng - to expand/swell)

Definition: The tongue, the muscular organ in the mouth used for tasting, swallowing, and speaking.
Usage: Found in words like 舌头 (tongue), 口舌 (verbal dispute), and 火舌 (flame)

Definition: Difficult, hard, or arduous. Describes situations, conditions, or tasks that require great effort or involve hardship.
Usage: Commonly used in compound words like 艰难 (difficult), 艰苦 (arduous), 艰辛 (hardship)

Definition: Bright, colorful, or gorgeous in appearance; often describes vivid colors or striking beauty.
Usage: Commonly used to describe flowers, clothing, or beautiful women, as in 艳丽 (gorgeous) or 鲜艳 (bright-colored)

Definition: A seedling or young plant; also refers to sprouts or shoots of plants. Can also mean descendants or a certain ethnic group (Miao people).
Usage: Common in agricultural contexts like 禾苗 (rice seedlings) or 树苗 (tree saplings)

Definition: Lush, luxuriant, or flourishing; describes abundant and thriving vegetation or growth.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 茂盛 (màoshèng - lush/flourishing) and place names like 茂名

Definition: Glory, honor, or prosperity; refers to prestige, distinction, or flourishing success.
Usage: Common in words like 光荣 (glorious), 荣誉 (honor), and 繁荣 (prosperous)

Definition: A type of sedge grass; most commonly seen as a transliteration component in foreign names
Usage: Frequently used in names like 莎士比亚 (Shakespeare) and 莎拉 (Sarah)

Definition: Describes something that is lustrous, sparkling, or crystal clear, like jade or gemstones. Often used to describe a bright, translucent quality.
Usage: Commonly appears in names and poetic descriptions; seen in compounds like 晶莹 (sparkling clear)

Definition: To operate, run, or manage (a business or organization); can also mean military camp or battalion
Usage: Common in business contexts like 经营 (to operate/manage) and 营业 (to do business)

Definition: Thin or flimsy in physical thickness; can also mean weak or lacking in intensity.
Usage: Commonly used to describe thin materials like paper (薄纸), pancakes (薄饼), or weak tea (茶很薄)

Definition: A conjunction meaning 'although' or 'even though', used to introduce a concessive clause that contrasts with the main clause.
Usage: Almost always appears in the pattern 虽然...但是... (although...but...), as in 虽然很累,但是很高兴 (although tired, but happy)

Definition: Frog; an amphibian animal that lives both in water and on land.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 青蛙 (qīngwā, frog) and 牛蛙 (niúwā, bullfrog)

Definition: A clam, frog, or toad; refers to various amphibians and shellfish.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 蛤蜊 (clam) and 蛤蟆 (toad)

Definition: A character meaning 'to wriggle' or 'to wind,' describing snake-like or meandering movement.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the compound word 蜿蜒 (wānyán), meaning 'winding' or 'meandering,' used to describe rivers, roads, or paths

Definition: To curl up or coil into a ball shape, typically describing how a body or limbs are positioned when contracted.
Usage: Commonly used in phrases like 蜷缩 (to curl up) or 蜷曲 (to curl/bend)

Definition: To wind or twist in a snake-like manner; describes something that curves and bends continuously.
Usage: Almost always used in the compound word 蜿蜒 (wānyán) to describe winding roads, rivers, or paths

Definition: A character meaning bat (the flying mammal). It is rarely used alone and almost always appears in the compound word 蝙蝠 (biānfú).
Usage: Most commonly seen in 蝙蝠 (bat)

Definition: Bat (the flying mammal). This character is rarely used alone and appears almost exclusively in the compound word 蝙蝠 (biānfú).
Usage: Most commonly seen in 蝙蝠 (bat) and in cultural contexts where bats symbolize good fortune due to the homophone with 福 (fú, blessing)

Definition: A character meaning toad or frog, rarely used alone in modern Chinese.
Usage: Almost exclusively appears in the compound word 蛤蟆 (háma, toad)

Definition: To cut (cloth or paper); to reduce or trim. Also means to judge or decide in formal contexts.
Usage: Common in words like 裁剪 (to cut and tailor), 裁员 (to lay off staff), and 裁判 (referee/judge)

Definition: Trousers or pants; a general term for lower-body garments that cover the legs.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 裤子 (kùzi - pants), 短裤 (duǎnkù - shorts), 长裤 (chángkù - long pants)

Definition: The front part of a Chinese garment, particularly the collar or lapel area where the fabric overlaps.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 对襟 (front opening) or 胸襟 (mind/breadth of mind, literally 'chest opening')

Definition: To touch, come into contact with, or reach something physically or metaphorically. Can also mean to trigger or provoke a reaction or feeling.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 触摸 (to touch), 接触 (to contact), and 触发 (to trigger)

Definition: Reputation, fame, or honor; praise or acclaim that someone receives for their achievements or character.
Usage: Common in words like 荣誉 (honor/glory) and 名誉 (reputation/fame)

Definition: An oath, vow, or pledge; to swear or make a solemn promise
Usage: Common in formal contexts like 发誓 (to swear/vow) and 宣誓 (to take an oath)

Definition: Mistake, error, or to miss/delay something; also means to do something incorrectly or by accident.
Usage: Common in words like 错误 (mistake), 误会 (misunderstanding), and 耽误 (to delay)

Definition: To lure, entice, or tempt someone into doing something, often with negative connotations.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 诱惑 (temptation), 引诱 (to seduce/lure), and 诱导 (to guide/induce)

Definition: To promise or consent; an expression of agreement or acknowledgment. Often used in formal or literary contexts to mean 'yes' or 'to pledge'.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 承诺 (chéngnuò - promise) and 诺言 (nuòyán - pledge/vow)

Definition: Friendship or friendly feelings between people. This character emphasizes the emotional bond and goodwill in relationships.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the word 友谊 (yǒuyì, friendship) and 情谊 (qíngyì, friendly feelings)

Definition: Valley or gorge; also means grain or cereal crops.
Usage: Common in geographical terms like 山谷 (mountain valley) and in words related to agriculture

Definition: Bean or legume; a general term for various types of beans and peas used in Chinese cuisine.
Usage: Common in words like 豆腐 (tofu), 大豆 (soybean), 豆浆 (soy milk)

Definition: Appearance, looks, or outward form of a person or thing. Often refers to physical appearance or facial features.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 外貌 (wàimào - appearance), 面貌 (miànmào - face/features), and 礼貌 (lǐmào - politeness/manners)

Definition: Shell or shellfish; an ancient form of currency in China. Also used as a radical component in many characters related to money and value.
Usage: Commonly seen in compound words like 宝贝 (treasure/darling) and as a component in characters like 财 (wealth) and 货 (goods)

Definition: Quality, nature, or essence of something; also refers to substance or material composition.
Usage: Common in words like 质量 (quality), 物质 (matter/substance), 本质 (essence)

Definition: Expensive or costly; also means noble, precious, or honorable.
Usage: Common in phrases like 太贵了 (too expensive) and 贵姓 (honorable surname, polite way to ask someone's name)

Definition: Resources, capital, or funds; also refers to qualifications or natural endowments.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 资金 (funds), 资源 (resources), 工资 (salary), and 资格 (qualification)

Definition: Foot or leg; also means sufficient or enough when used as an adjective.
Usage: Common in words like 足球 (football/soccer) and 满足 (satisfied, sufficient)

Definition: To lie on one's stomach or bend over with the body face down; to lean or rest on something with the upper body.
Usage: Common in phrases like 趴下 (lie down face down) or 趴在桌子上 (lean on the table)

Definition: Describes an unsteady, staggering way of walking, often due to being weak, drunk, or losing balance.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the compound word 踉跄 (liàngqiàng), meaning to stagger or stumble

Definition: Distance or gap between two points or things; to be apart from or away from something.
Usage: Most commonly seen in 距离 (jùlí, distance) and phrases like 距离北京10公里 (10 kilometers from Beijing)

Definition: To stagger or walk unsteadily, describing the motion of stumbling or losing one's balance while walking.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the compound word 踉跄 (liàngqiàng), meaning to stagger or totter

Definition: To kick or strike with the foot. Most commonly used in the context of sports, especially soccer/football.
Usage: Used in phrases like 踢足球 (kick a soccer ball/play soccer) or 踢球 (kick a ball)

Definition: To pace or walk slowly back and forth, often in a leisurely or contemplative manner.
Usage: Commonly used in the phrase 踱步 (duó bù) meaning 'to pace' or 'to stroll'

Definition: To walk on tiptoe or tread softly and quietly; to follow closely behind someone's footsteps.
Usage: Often used in literary contexts or set phrases like 蹑手蹑脚 (to walk stealthily)

Definition: Awkward, clumsy, or of poor quality; describes something that is inferior or not smooth.
Usage: Most commonly used in 蹩脚 (biéjiǎo) meaning 'clumsy' or 'inferior'

Definition: To squat or crouch down with knees bent and buttocks close to the heels.
Usage: Commonly used to describe the physical position of squatting, such as 蹲下 (squat down)

Definition: Webbed feet or flippers; the membrane between the toes of aquatic animals like ducks, frogs, and seals.
Usage: Commonly used in biology contexts, such as 鸭蹼 (duck's webbed feet) or 蛙蹼 (frog's webbed feet)

Definition: Body or torso, referring to the physical human body or trunk. Often used in formal or literary contexts.
Usage: Common in words like 身躯 (shēnqū - body/physique) and 躯体 (qūtǐ - body)

Definition: To lose (a game, competition, or bet); to be defeated. Can also mean to transport or transmit.
Usage: Common in contexts like 输了比赛 (lost the game) or 输钱 (lose money)

Definition: Spicy or pungent (taste); hardship or suffering. Also used as the eighth of the ten Heavenly Stems in traditional Chinese calendars.
Usage: Common in words like 辛苦 (hardship/hard work) and 辛辣 (spicy)

Definition: The fifth of the twelve Earthly Branches in the Chinese zodiac, corresponding to the Dragon; also refers to time or celestial bodies in classical Chinese.
Usage: Commonly seen in zodiac references (龙年 - Year of the Dragon), time expressions, and names

Definition: To humiliate, insult, or bring shame upon someone or oneself. It conveys the idea of disgrace or dishonor.
Usage: Common in words like 侮辱 (wǔrǔ - to insult) and 耻辱 (chǐrǔ - shame/disgrace)

Definition: To step or stride forward; to take a step or make progress.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 迈步 (to take a step) and 迈进 (to stride into/advance)

Definition: To alternate, repeat, or occur one after another in succession; to pile up or accumulate in layers.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 更迭 (to replace/alternate), 迭代 (iteration), and 层出不迭 (appearing one after another)

Definition: To tease, amuse, or make someone laugh; to play with or provoke in a playful way.
Usage: Commonly used in 逗笑 (to make laugh) or 逗人 (amusing/funny)

Definition: Distant or far away, describing something remote in space or time.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 遥远 (yaoyuan, distant/remote) and 遥控 (yaokong, remote control)

Definition: To invite or request someone to join an activity or event
Usage: Commonly used in words like 邀请 (yāoqǐng - to invite) and 邀约 (yāoyuē - to make an appointment)

Definition: A nation, state, or country; a formal or literary term for a sovereign territory or political entity.
Usage: Commonly seen in formal contexts like 友邦 (friendly nation/ally) or 邻邦 (neighboring country)

Definition: To match, pair, or coordinate things together; to be worthy of or deserve something.
Usage: Common in words like 配合 (cooperate), 搭配 (match/pair), 分配 (distribute), and 配偶 (spouse)

Definition: A tool with two parts that grip or hold things tightly together; pliers or pincers. Can also refer to claws or pincers of animals like crabs.
Usage: Common in words like 钳子 (pliers), 火钳 (fire tongs), or 蟹钳 (crab claws)

Definition: Iron, the metal; can also mean strong, hard, or unbreakable when used figuratively.
Usage: Common in words like 地铁 (subway), 铁路 (railway), and 钢铁 (steel)

Definition: Copper, a reddish-brown metal; also refers to bronze in some contexts.
Usage: Common in words like 青铜 (bronze), 铜钱 (copper coin), and 铜牌 (bronze medal)

Definition: A chain or link, referring to connected metal rings or a series of connected things. Often used in compound words related to chains, links, or connected systems.
Usage: Common in words like 项链 (necklace), 链条 (chain), 链接 (link/hyperlink), 区块链 (blockchain)

Definition: Describes something shiny, bright, or gleaming, especially metal surfaces that are polished or well-maintained.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the reduplicative form 锃亮 (zèngliàng) meaning 'shiny and bright'

Definition: A key on a keyboard or piano; also refers to something crucial or critical.
Usage: Commonly seen in 键盘 (keyboard), 按键 (button/key), and 关键 (crucial/key)

Definition: To inlay, embed, or set something decorative (like gems, gold, or borders) into a surface or edge.
Usage: Commonly used for jewelry (镶钻石 - to set diamonds) or decorative borders (镶边 - to edge/trim)

Definition: Free, idle, or not busy; having leisure time with nothing particular to do.
Usage: Common in expressions like 有空闲 (have free time) or 闲聊 (chat idly)

Definition: A common Chinese surname meaning 'to display' or 'to arrange'; also means 'old' or 'stale' as an adjective.
Usage: Most frequently encountered as a family name, as in 陈先生 (Mr. Chen)

Definition: To sink into, fall into, or get trapped in something (physically or metaphorically); to cave in or collapse.
Usage: Common in phrases like 陷入困境 (fall into difficulty) or 陷阱 (trap, pitfall)

Definition: A gap, crack, or crevice; also refers to a rift or discord between people.
Usage: Common in words like 缝隙 (crack/gap), 空隙 (opening/space), and 嫌隙 (grudge/rift)

Definition: Tunnel or underground passage. This character is most commonly seen in the compound word 隧道 (suìdào), meaning tunnel.
Usage: Primarily used in the word 隧道 to refer to tunnels for roads, railways, or pedestrians

Definition: To be subordinate to or attached to; historically refers to a slave or servant in ancient China.
Usage: Commonly seen in compounds like 隶属 (lìshǔ - to be subordinate to) and 奴隶 (núlì - slave)

Definition: A small bird, particularly a sparrow. This character is commonly used in compound words related to various types of small birds.
Usage: Found in words like 麻雀 (sparrow) and 孔雀 (peacock)

Definition: Male (of animals); also means grand, powerful, or heroic when describing things or people.
Usage: Common in words like 雄性 (male gender), 英雄 (hero), and 雄伟 (magnificent)

Definition: To carve or engrave (wood, stone, etc.); also refers to a large bird of prey such as an eagle or vulture
Usage: As a verb in 雕刻 (carve), 雕塑 (sculpture); as a noun in 老雕 (eagle)

Definition: The color blue-green or cyan; also refers to young or youthful things, particularly green plants and vegetation.
Usage: Common in words like 青年 (young person), 青春 (youth), and 青菜 (green vegetables)

Definition: To feed or raise animals; to provide food for livestock or pets.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 饲养 (to raise/breed animals) and 饲料 (animal feed/fodder)

Definition: Filling or stuffing inside food items such as dumplings, buns, pies, or pastries.
Usage: Common in words like 饺子馅 (dumpling filling), 包子馅 (bun filling), 馅饼 (meat pie)

Definition: Camel; also means hunchbacked or to have a hunched back.
Usage: Most commonly seen in 骆驼 (luòtuo, camel) or describing a hunched posture

Definition: To scold, curse, or verbally abuse someone; to use harsh or angry words to criticize.
Usage: Common in expressions like 骂人 (to curse at people) or 挨骂 (to be scolded)

Definition: Proud or arrogant; having an excessively high opinion of oneself. Often carries a negative connotation of being conceited or haughty.
Usage: Commonly seen in words like 骄傲 (jiāo'ào - proud/arrogant) and 骄横 (jiāohèng - arrogant and domineering)

Definition: Bones, especially of a skeleton or corpse; remains of a dead body.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the compound word 骸骨 (hái gǔ, skeletal remains) or literary contexts

Definition: Curly or wavy, especially referring to hair that is naturally curled or has curls.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the word 鬈发 (curly hair) or 鬈曲 (curled, wavy)

Definition: Crocodile or alligator; a large aquatic reptile with powerful jaws and a long tail.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the word 鳄鱼 (èyú, crocodile/alligator)

Definition: Chicken; refers to the domesticated bird raised for meat and eggs, or the meat itself.
Usage: Common in food contexts like 鸡肉 (chicken meat) and everyday expressions

Definition: To cry out, chirp, or make a sound (especially of birds and animals); to ring or sound (of objects like bells).
Usage: Common in words like 鸣叫 (to cry out), 蜂鸣 (buzzing), and 共鸣 (resonance)

Definition: A goose, a large waterfowl with a long neck, typically white or gray in color.
Usage: Commonly used in words like 天鹅 (swan) and 鹅毛 (goose feather)

Definition: Sticky, adhesive, or viscous; describes something that clings or sticks to surfaces.
Usage: Commonly used to describe sticky substances like glue, rice, or tape (e.g., 黏性 sticky quality, 黏糊糊 sticky and gooey)

Definition: Describes something that is pitch-black or extremely dark in color.
Usage: Most commonly seen in the reduplicative form 黢黑 (qū hēi) meaning 'pitch-black' or 'jet-black'

Definition: An ancient Chinese three-legged cooking vessel or cauldron, often made of bronze; also means 'grand' or 'at the height of power' in literary contexts.
Usage: Commonly seen in classical texts and idioms like 鼎盛 (at its peak/flourishing)

Definition: To snore; the sound made while breathing loudly during sleep.
Usage: Commonly used in the word 打鼾 (dǎ hān) meaning 'to snore'

Definition: Age, referring to the number of years someone or something has existed. Most commonly used in compound words related to age.
Usage: Found in words like 年龄 (niánlíng - age), 高龄 (gāolíng - advanced age), 学龄 (xuélíng - school age)

Definition: Turtle or tortoise; a shelled reptile that moves slowly and is associated with longevity in Chinese culture.
Usage: Common in words like 乌龟 (wūguī, turtle) and idioms about longevity
